tenant is refused.
The wording of the confirmation message is resolved from the Tenancy notification template catalogue
(`template_key=EmailChangeConfirmation`), and the locale is decided in the order: the recipient User's locale attribute,
the tenant's `default_locale`, the system default locale. A tenant override takes precedence over the built-in default.
Both a plain text and an HTML body are always produced, and the confirmation link is built from the issuer URL of the request.

the AuthenticatedSelf and session-based access classification does not apply. On settling, `email_verified` becomes true
and a `verify_email` required action, if there is one, is cleared automatically.

get.description:
An administrator reads the audit DomainEvents of their tenant, newest first, through bidirectional keyset pagination.
Built for SOC and compliance work, it offers a time window (`after` / `before`), a page size (`limit`), continuation
(`cursor`, reached through the `rel="prev"` and `rel="next"` links of the Link response header), and filtering by
`type`, `user_id`, and `username` (the actor). Authentication events -- login success and failure, MFA, sessions,
aggregates -- live in the same store, so `category` (authentication / success / fail / aggregated / user / group /
client / consent / token / tenant / key) narrows the search for a security or an operational investigation. Beyond
that, `q` matches raw text as a substring and `filter` takes a structured expression over the field/operator allow
list of the registry. Only fields the AuditEventSearchAttribute registry permits may appear in `filter`; arbitrary
SQL or JSONPath is refused. `user_id` and the `actor.id` of `filter` name the actor, and `username` resolves the
actor's login name to a user id at search time -- not hashed, and matching nothing when no such user exists.
`actor.username` in `filter` is a plaintext match reserved for authentication failures, so that an account name
that never existed can still be traced. `target.id` in `filter` is a different concept: the user an administrative
operation acted on (AuditActorVsTarget). A system_admin reaching the endpoint through the default tenant sees
every tenant; an admin stays inside their own. The query takes no tenant_id input, so an admin is confined to
their tenant structurally, and only a system_admin can cross that line, through the dedicated route.

A LogoutRequest arrives over the HTTP-Redirect or HTTP-POST binding, the SP is resolved from Issuer, the IdP profile of the route is matched against the profile the SP is bound to, and for an SP that requires signatures the signature is verified. Destination must be the SLO endpoint of the selected profile, and the reply goes only to a registered SingleLogoutService. The local session is destroyed and a LogoutResponse, signed with the key of the assigned profile, is returned to the registered SLO URL. A local logout naming entityID or sp is accepted too, but nothing is ever redirected to a destination that cannot be resolved or is not registered, so this cannot become an open redirect.

get.description: Sign-in for SAML 2.0 Web Browser SSO. An SP-initiated request arrives as an AuthnRequest over the HTTP-Redirect or HTTP-POST binding, and the service provider is resolved only after Version=2.0, the acceptance window around IssueInstant, Issuer, Destination, the HTTP-POST response ProtocolBinding, the mutual exclusion and the supportability of the ACS URL and index, and the NameIDPolicy format have all been checked. When the IdP profile of the route, the profile the SP is bound to, and Destination do not agree, the request is refused fail-closed. For an SP that requires signatures, either the Redirect binding signature or the XML signature is verified. A request that is unsupported or self-contradictory is refused fail-closed, and a SAML protocol error is HTTP-POSTed back only when there is a verified ACS to reply to. ForceAuthn=true sends the caller to sign in unless they reauthenticated recently. With IsPassive=true, an unusable existing session yields a NoPassive response rather than a move to the sign-in page. An IdP-initiated request names the target SP through the entityID query. An unauthenticated caller is sent to sign in, and the request survives the round trip. Once authenticated, the application assignment gate is applied fail-closed and nothing is issued to an unassigned subject. The NameID and attributes the SP's claim policy produces are carried in a bearer SAML assertion; the assertion and the response are signed with the XML signing credentials of the assigned profile and according to the SP's settings; and the SAMLResponse is auto-posted to the ACS over HTTP-POST. The tenant, the SP, and the AuthnRequest ID are recorded in the TTL replay store atomically and exactly once, immediately before the assertion is issued. InResponseTo, AudienceRestriction, Recipient, and Destination are kept consistent with one another.

POST to SCIM 2.0 /Groups. `displayName` is required, and its absence gives an `invalidValue` ScimProtocolError. `id`
is always generated by the server and ignored even when the body carries one (readOnly). Each element of `members`
must have a `type` that is absent or User (case-insensitive) and must be the SCIM id of a User that resolves inside
the same tenant; a member of type Group, and a member that does not resolve, both give `invalidValue` and no group is
created. Every member of the created resource carries type=User, and the resource carries `id`,
`meta.resourceType`, `meta.created`, `meta.lastModified`, and `meta.location`. A `displayName` that collides with an
existing Group in the same tenant gives 409 `uniqueness`.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

get.description:
Searches the SCIM 2.0 /Groups collection under `filter`, `startIndex`, and `count`.
Of the RFC 7644 section 3.4.2.2 grammar, `filter` accepts only comparison operators over the permitted Group
attributes -- eq, ne, co, sw, ew, pr on displayName and id; eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, pr on meta.created and
meta.lastModified, where dateTime comparison uses real RFC 3339 instants -- together with the logical operators and,
or, not, and grouping parentheses. An attribute name may also be written with its schema URN prefix
(urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group: and the like). An attribute or operator outside the allow list, an
unknown URN prefix, a syntax error, and input longer or more deeply nested than the ceiling all give an
`invalidFilter` ScimProtocolError; none of them degrade into an internal error.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

get.description:
GET on SCIM 2.0 /Groups/{id}. Every member is returned with type=User. The resource carries `id`,
`meta.resourceType`, `meta.created`, `meta.lastModified`, and `meta.location`.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

patch.description:
PATCH on SCIM 2.0 /Groups/{id} (RFC 7644 section 3.5.2). `path` must name one of the Group attributes RFC7644-PATCH
covers, `displayName` or `members`; anything else gives an `invalidPath` ScimProtocolError. An `op` other than add,
replace, or remove, and a value whose type does not fit the target attribute, give `invalidValue`. `members` accepts
only members whose `type` is absent or User (case-insensitive); a member of type Group, and a member that does not
resolve, both give `invalidValue` and the group is left unchanged. Writing to `id`, `meta`, or `schemas` gives a
mutability error.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

put.description:
PUT on SCIM 2.0 /Groups/{id}. It **replaces** the mutable attributes RFC7643-CORE-RESOURCES covers outright; this is
not a partial update. `displayName` is required, and its absence gives an `invalidValue` ScimProtocolError. Leaving
`members` out removes every existing member, replacing the set with the empty one. `members` accepts only members
whose `type` is absent or User (case-insensitive); a member of type Group, and a member that does not resolve, both
give `invalidValue` and the group is left unchanged. Writes to `id` and `meta` are ignored (readOnly).

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

delete.description: DELETE on SCIM 2.0 /Groups/{id}.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

get.description:
Reads the SCIM 2.0 /ResourceTypes. Only the two resource types that are implemented, User and Group, are returned,
with their schema URN and endpoint. User advertises the enterprise extension it supports
(urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User) under `schemaExtensions`.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

get.description:
Reads the SCIM 2.0 /Schemas. It advertises the User and Group attributes RFC7643-CORE-RESOURCES covers, and the
`employeeNumber`, `department`, and `manager` of the enterprise extension RFC7643-ENTERPRISE-EXTENSION covers
(urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User), each with its `type`, `multiValued`, `required`,
`mutability` (readOnly or readWrite), `returned`, and `uniqueness`. It states that User emails project onto a single
canonical email and that the `referenceTypes` of Group members is User alone, and it does not advertise what is not
supported: phoneNumbers, addresses, a Group as a member, costCenter, division, and organization. An empty attribute
array is never returned.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

get.description:
Reads the SCIM 2.0 /ServiceProviderConfig.
The response declares which authentication schemes are accepted, in `authenticationSchemes`. RFC 7643 section 5
makes that attribute a REQUIRED multi-valued one, so it may be neither empty nor absent. The SCIM API authenticates
with an access token presented under the Bearer scheme, so at least the `oauthbearertoken` scheme is listed.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

post.description:
POST to SCIM 2.0 /Users, creating an internal User. `userName` is required, and its absence gives an `invalidValue`
ScimProtocolError. Every element of `emails` is validated, then projected onto a single email in the order
primary=true, type=work (case-insensitive), wire order. A malformed `emails`, `phoneNumbers`, or `addresses` gives
`invalidValue`. `employeeNumber`, `department`, and `manager` (either the `value` of an object or a plain string)
under urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User are supported too; an `employeeNumber` or
`department` that is not a string, and a `manager` naming a SCIM User that does not exist in the same tenant, both
give `invalidValue`. `id` is always generated by the server and ignored even when the body carries one (readOnly),
and `active` defaults to true. The created resource carries a single type=work, primary=true entry only when there
is a canonical email, carries the enterprise extension URN in `schemas` together with the matching attribute object
only when at least one extension attribute is set, and always returns `id`, `meta.resourceType`, `meta.created`,
`meta.lastModified`, and `meta.location`. A `userName` that collides with an existing User in the same tenant gives
409 `uniqueness`.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

get.description:
Searches the SCIM 2.0 /Users collection under `filter`, `startIndex`, and `count`.

attributes -- eq, ne, co, sw, ew, pr on userName, active, name.formatted, name.givenName, name.familyName,
emails.value, and id; eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, pr on meta.created and meta.lastModified, where dateTime comparison
uses real RFC 3339 instants -- together with the logical operators and, or, not, and grouping parentheses. An
attribute name may also be written with its schema URN prefix (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User: and the
like). An attribute or operator outside the allow list, an unknown URN prefix, a syntax error, and input longer or
more deeply nested than the ceiling all give an `invalidFilter` ScimProtocolError; none of them degrade into an
internal error.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

get.description:
GET on SCIM 2.0 /Users/{id}. A canonical email is returned as a single type=work, primary=true entry, and only when
there is one. The resource carries `id`, `meta.resourceType`, `meta.created`, `meta.lastModified`, and
`meta.location`.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

patch.description:
PATCH on SCIM 2.0 /Users/{id} (RFC 7644 section 3.5.2). Each element of `Operations` carries an `op` -- add, replace,
or remove -- and a `path`. `path` must name one of the User attributes RFC7644-PATCH covers: userName, name,
name.formatted, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails, active, employeeNumber, department, and manager, where an
enterprise extension attribute may be written either bare or fully qualified with
urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User. Anything else, phoneNumbers and addresses included,
gives `invalidPath`. An add or replace on `emails` validates every element and then projects onto a single email in
the order primary=true, type=work (case-insensitive), wire order, and a malformed value gives `invalidValue`. An add
or replace on `manager` accepts a value object or a plain string, and naming a SCIM User that does not exist in the
same tenant gives `invalidValue`. An `op` other than add, replace, or remove, and a value whose type does not fit
the target attribute, also give `invalidValue`. Writing to `id`, `meta`, or `schemas` gives a mutability error.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax.

put.description:
PUT on SCIM 2.0 /Users/{id}. It **replaces** the mutable attributes RFC7643-CORE-RESOURCES covers outright; this is
not a partial update. `userName` is required, and its absence gives an `invalidValue` ScimProtocolError. Every other
mutable attribute left out -- name.*, emails, active, and the enterprise extension employeeNumber, department, and
manager -- is reset to its default: empty for name, emails, and the extension attributes, true for active. Every
element of `emails` is validated, then projected onto a single email in the order primary=true, type=work
(case-insensitive), wire order. A malformed `emails`, `phoneNumbers`, or `addresses` gives `invalidValue`, as does an
`employeeNumber` or `department` that is not a string and a `manager` naming a SCIM User that does not exist in the
same tenant, all under urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User. Writes to `id` and `meta` are
ignored (readOnly).

optional, because the specification is still a draft and has never reached Final).
It returns static HTML and JavaScript, and answers a `postMessage` from the RP with nothing more than whether the

It verifies the UsernameToken, confines `To` to the active STS endpoint of the current realm, `Action` and `RequestType` to Issue, and `KeyType` to Bearer, and resolves `AppliesTo` to a registered WsFedRelyingParty. get.description: The single HTTP endpoint of the WS-Federation passive requestor profile. `wa` dispatches between sign-in and sign-out. Sign-in resolves the relying party from `wtrealm` and confines `wreply` to the allowed set, so it cannot become an open redirect. An unauthenticated caller is sent to sign in; an authenticated one gets the claims built by the relying party's claim policy, carried in a signed SAML assertion (SAML 1.1 by default, which Entra expects; SAML 2.0 when the RP is configured for it), wrapped in an RSTR and auto-posted. When the authentication is older than the maximum age `wfresh` states, the caller is sent to reauthenticate, and the authentication method `wauth` asks for is honoured. The meaning of sign-out belongs to WsFederationSignOut.

status.description: Always `ok`.

return_to.description: Where to go after signing in, confined to the `/admin` subtree of the same realm.

granted_scopes.description: The scopes the caller's access token carries. The check refuses fail-closed when they do not cover what the operation requires.

network_allow_cidrs.description: The CIDRs the client IP is permitted to fall in. Empty means no restriction. When it is non-empty and the client IP falls in none of them, or the IP cannot be determined at all, the request is refused fail-closed.

Contract.AccessCondition.description: The static access conditions of a sign-in policy. Every one of them is a structured condition the initial implementation can actually evaluate. `network_allow_cidrs` matches the client IP against the permitted CIDRs, and `reauth_max_age_seconds` is evaluated as the recency of an authentication or a step-up. The old free-text network and device fields have been dropped.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.AccessDeniedError.description: The principal does not satisfy the policy for the operation. Published-language stub for the shared error the Authentication context defines. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:access_denied`. The OAuth 2.0 endpoints report the same condition as OAuthAccessDeniedError instead.

act.description: The `act` claim of RFC 8693 section 4.1, naming the current actor of the delegation. When the `subject_token` carried an `act`, they nest.

may_act.description: The `may_act` claim of RFC 8693 section 4.4, naming the actors permitted to act on the subject's behalf.

authorization_details.description: RFC 9396: the structured details bound to the token. It is the resource server's checkpoint. Optional, for backward compatibility.

Contract.AccessTokenClaims.description: The claims of a JWT access token (RFC 9068). TTL 600 seconds.

tenantId.description: The tenant the token was issued in.

Contract.AccessTokenIssued.description: An access token (a JWT) was issued. When there is a `senderConstraint`, it is bound to a proof of possession through DPoP or mTLS.

Contract.AccessTokenSenderConstraint.description: The sender constraint applied to an issued access token. `none` means a bearer token.

Contract.AccountApprovalDecisionRequest.description: The end user's decision on one approval request: approve or deny.

client_name.description:
The display name the client_id resolved to. It resolves in the order `OAuth2Client.client_name`, then the
Application catalogue name, and falls back to the client_id itself when there is neither.

agent_name.description: The display name of the Agent bound to the client, when there is one.

Contract.AccountApprovalRequest.description:
One pending approval request the end-user account portal returns (self-service). It is fixed to requests
addressed to the caller, so no `user_id` appears. It does not let `binding_message` stand in for the content: who
asked and what they asked for are returned side by side.

Contract.AccountApprovalRequestListRespo.description: The approval requests pending for the end user themselves (self-service).

Contract.AccountConsentListResponse.description: The end user's own connected applications, that is, their active Consents (self-service).

client_name.description:
The display name the client_id resolved to. It resolves in the order `OAuth2Client.client_name`, then the
Application catalogue name, and falls back to the client_id itself when there is neither.

Contract.AccountConsentResponse.description:
One connected application the end-user account portal returns (self-service).
It is fixed to the caller's own `sub`, so neither `sub` nor `tenant_id` appears. It returns the client_id, the display
name, the granted scopes, and when they were granted and expire, for display.

Contract.AccountContextResponse.description: The administration shell bootstrap information of an authenticated browser session. It returns the CSRF token, the subject, the current realm, and the effective roles.

Contract.AccountDataExport.description:
An end user's export of their own personal data (GDPR Article 15, the right of access). At this stage it is
generated synchronously and gathers the profile and the connected applications (consents) available from the current API.

Contract.AccountEmailChangeConfirm.description:
The request confirming the one-time link sent to the new address (self-service). The token is itself the
proof that the new address is owned, so no authenticated session is required, following the same principle as password reset.

Contract.AccountEmailChangeRequest.description:
The request raising a primary email change (self-service). It only sends a confirmation link to the
new address; `User.email` does not change until ConfirmEmailChange completes.

Contract.AccountLinkingPolicy.description: How an external identity is correlated with a local User. The default, `none`, correlates nothing automatically beyond an existing link. `verified_email` permits a unique match on a verified email, and only when the tenant says so explicitly.

Contract.AccountMfaFactor.description:
The projection of one MFA factor shown on the self-service security screen. No secret is
returned: only the kind, the label, and when it was created and last used. Today, TOTP alone.

mandatory.description: Whether it is a kind the user may not turn off.

enabled.description: Whether the user currently receives notifications of this kind.

Contract.AccountNotificationCategoryPref.description:
How one kind of security notification is presented to the user. A kind whose `mandatory` is true always has
`enabled` true, and an update cannot set it to false.

Contract.AccountNotificationPreferences.description:
What GetMyNotificationPreferences returns. Every kind comes back in the stable order the specification fixes,
so the UI need not hold the list of kinds in its own code.

Contract.AccountProfileResponse.description:
What `/api/account/profile` returns (self-service): a display projection of the calling user themselves.
`attributes` carries only what they may read of their own (`self_readable` or `claim_exposed`), and
`editable_attributes` lists the definitions with `editable_by_user=true`, which the UI uses to render its form.

Contract.AccountProfileUpdateRequest.description:
The self-service profile update request. It accepts only the display name and the attributes marked
`editable_by_user=true`. `attributes` merges per key -- the keys given are upserted and the rest are left alone -- and the
administrator-managed attributes (status, roles, organization) are out of its reach.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

userId.description: The `sub` of the user receiving the notification. Under impersonation it is the target user, not the administrator who acted.

triggerEventType.description: The type name of the event that occasioned the notification.

delivered.description: Whether the EmailSender accepted it. Delivery is best-effort, so the original operation stands even when this is false.

Contract.AccountSecurityNotificationSent.description:
One account security notification was sent, or an attempt to send it failed. It exists to keep what the user
was told in the audit trail, and carries neither the body nor the recipient address in its payload. The notification
dispatcher emits it itself, and because this event type is not in the catalogue no further notification cascades from it.

Contract.AccountSecurityResponse.description:
What `/api/account/security` returns, the security overview of the end-user account portal.
It gathers the password change time, whether MFA (TOTP and WebAuthn) is enrolled, and how many backup recovery codes
remain.

Contract.AccountSession.description:
The projection of one entry in the self-service session list. It holds no secret: only the identifiers and
the authentication details. `current` says whether it is the caller's present session. `started_at` is the
`auth_time` of the LoginSession and `expires_at` when it is due to expire.

Contract.AccountSessionListResponse.description: What ListMySessions returns: the user's own live sessions, by start time, newest first.

Contract.AccountSummary.description:
What `/api/account/summary` returns, the home of the end-user account portal. It is the calling user's own
account summary, a separate contract from the AccountContext of the administration shell (`/api/auth/account`).
It carries no roles, and returns the last sign-in, the password change time, the MFA state, and the outstanding
required actions for the summary card of the portal home.

Contract.AccountTrustedDevice.description:
The projection of one trusted device shown on the self-service security screen. Neither the selector nor
`verifier_hash` is returned: only what identification and display need. `current` says whether it is the device
matching the cookie the present request offered.

max_age_seconds.description: The tenant's `trusted_device_max_age_seconds`. Zero means the feature is off and the UI offers no way to remember a device.

Contract.AccountTrustedDeviceListRespons.description:
What ListMyTrustedDevices returns: the user's own live trusted devices, by last use, newest first.
It is always empty when the tenant has trusted devices turned off.

Contract.ActiveJobQuotaExceededError.description: The tenant already has as many export jobs running as it may have at once, so another one cannot start. The two conditions currently share the error code `quota_exceeded`, so the `type` is `urn:idmagic:error:quota_exceeded` here as well; the concurrency ceiling and the tenant resource quota are separate concepts and the shared code is a defect on the server side.

Contract.AdminApiEndpointSet.description: The canonical base URLs an external management client, a SCIM client, or a self-service client uses together with an API token.

Contract.AdminApplicationCategoryListRes.description: The ApplicationCategory list response, by position ascending with ties breaking by name ascending.

Contract.AdminApplicationCategoryRequest.description: The request to create or update an ApplicationCategory. Leaving `position` out places it last.

launch_url.description: The launch URL a portal tile opens. Required for `weblink`.

redirect_uris.description: Required when `type` is `oidc`: the redirect URIs of the OAuth2 client to create.

wtrealm.description: Required when `type` is `wsfed`: the `wtrealm` of the WS-Fed RP to create.

reply_urls.description: Required when `type` is `wsfed`: the permitted `wreply` targets.

entity_id.description: Required when `type` is `saml`: the entity ID of the SAML SP to create.

acs_urls.description: Required when `type` is `saml`: the Assertion Consumer Service URL.

Contract.AdminApplicationCreateRequest.description: The request that creates an Application in one call. It names the kind and carries the matching protocol settings with it. The backend prepares the protocol row outside the catalogue first, then inserts the Application and sets `row.application_id` in a single transaction. A protocol row whose second half failed is a valid configuration outside the catalogue, so no meaningless Application is left behind.

client_id.description: The generated client id, returned when `type` is `oidc`.

client_secret.description: The secret, returned once when `type` is `oidc`.

Contract.AdminApplicationCreateResponse.description: The result of a bulk creation. For `type=oidc` it returns the `client_id` and `client_secret` of the OAuth2 client it created, once; the secret cannot be read again.

Contract.AdminApplicationDetailResponse.description: The application detail response. Besides the Application itself it carries the real settings resolved through the protocol relation. At most one of `oidc`, `saml`, and `wsfed` is set, the one matching `Application.protocol.type`.

Contract.AdminApplicationResponse.description: How the administration API represents an Application.

Contract.AdminApplicationUpdateRequest.description: The request updating an Application. Only the fields given are changed.

Contract.AdminAuditEventListResponse.description: The result of an audit event search. Pagination navigation lives in the Link response header, not in the body.

id.description: The event id the store assigned (UUIDv4).

tenant_id.description: The tenant the event belongs to.

type.description: The wire name of `DomainEvent.type`.

payload.description: The event body, shaped as the payload in the events section of the specification.

Contract.AdminAuditEventResponse.description:
A DomainEvent as it is exposed to administrators. The payload is structured JSON.
PII fields such as email and IP are assumed to have been redacted by the EventSink before this point.
The store is append-only and keeps events for seven years (GDPR Article 30).

preferred_username.description: The display name the user_id resolved to. Left out when no such User is found.

client_name.description:
The display name the client_id resolved to. It resolves in the order `OAuth2Client.client_name`, then the
Application catalogue name, and falls back to the client_id itself when there is neither.

Contract.AdminConsentResponse.description: How the administration API represents a Consent of the tenant. Because the client_id and user_id are UUIDs, the resolved human-readable names (`client_name` and `preferred_username`) are returned alongside them for display.

fingerprint_sha256.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint, as uppercase hex separated by colons.

Contract.AdminFederationCertificate.description: The public part of the active X.509 certificate IdMagic uses to sign new XML federation messages. It carries no private key, and the metadata remains the authority for every certificate inside a rotation overlap.

Contract.AdminIntegrationEndpointCatalog.description: The read-only projection of `/api/admin/integration-endpoints`. Everything is derived from the canonical issuer of the request tenant alone, so the UI needs to know nothing about paths, subdomains, or custom domains. It carries no client secret, token, or private key.

Contract.AdminKeyListResponse.description: Every signing key. Two keys are never active at once, because rotation deactivates the old one in the same step.

kid.description: The JWK key id, the same one the JWKS publishes.

alg.description: The signing algorithm; today PS256 only.

active.description: True for the key that signs new ID tokens and access tokens. False for a key that stays on the JWKS only to verify already-issued tokens during the overlap after a rotation.

created_at.description: When the key was generated; SigningKeyMaxAge and SigningKeyMinJwksOverlap are measured from here.

public_jwk.description: The public JWK, in the same representation the JWKS uses.

Contract.AdminKeyResponse.description:
The signing key metadata exposed to a tenant administrator. It returns neither the private key nor how the key is stored,
only the same public JWK the JWKS carries. It is detailed enough to tell the current signing key from a key that merely
verifies already-issued tokens during the overlap after a rotation.

Contract.AdminOAuth2ClientCreateRequest.description: An administrator creates an OAuth client in their tenant. The generated `client_secret` is returned once, in the creation response.

Contract.AdminOAuth2ClientCreateResponse.description: The client creation response. The `client_secret` is returned once, and only when one was generated.

tenantId.description: The tenant the client belongs to. It matches the actor.

Contract.AdminOAuth2ClientCreated.description: An administrator created an OAuth client in their tenant. It carries no secret.

tenantId.description: The tenant the client belongs to. It matches the actor.

Contract.AdminOAuth2ClientDeleted.description: An administrator deleted an OAuth client from their tenant.

Contract.AdminOAuth2ClientResponse.description: How the administration API represents a client. `client_secret` and `client_secret_hash` are deliberately not part of the contract.

Contract.AdminOAuth2ClientUpdateRequest.description: An administrator updates the client metadata. The client_id, the authentication method, and the secrets are left alone; secret rotation has its own endpoint.

tenantId.description: The tenant the client belongs to. It matches the actor.

Contract.AdminOAuth2ClientUpdated.description: An administrator updated the OAuth client metadata.

Contract.AdminOAuthEndpointSet.description: The canonical endpoints an administrator needs to configure a relying party or an API client against the OAuth 2.0 authorization server and OpenID Connect provider. The discovery and authorization server metadata are the machine-readable authority; the individual URLs are returned for configuring by hand.

Contract.AdminRequiredActionRequest.description: The JSON request of SetUserRequiredAction. `action` is the wire value of the RequiredAction enum.

Contract.AdminRoleInterface.description: One HTTP interface a permission unlocks, identified the same way the compiled contract identifies it.

action.description: The action the permission allows, such as `read` or `write`.

description.description: What the permission allows. Always English and never localized.

Contract.AdminRolePermission.description: One permission a role carries, together with the HTTP interfaces the permission unlocks.

name.description: Role name, the value that appears in a User's `roles`.

description.description: What the role is for. Always English and never localized.

aliases.description: Other names that resolve to the same role.

Contract.AdminRolePolicy.description: One administrative role and the permissions it carries, as ListAdminRolePolicies reports them. The catalogue is derived from the compiled contract, so it always matches the operations the server actually exposes.

previous.description: The key that was active until now. Absent on the first rotation.

Contract.AdminRotateKeyResponse.description: The result of a key rotation: the kid of the new active key and of the one that just stepped down to verifying.

Contract.AdminSamlIdentityProviderEndpoi.description: The canonical details of the tenant's shared SAML IdP, to feed into an SP.

tenant_id.description: The immutable UUID key of the tenant.

realm.description: The slug that appears in the URL `/realms/{realm}/`. It is used to build the SCIM endpoint URLs and the like.

max_delegation_depth.description: Tenant override for the maximum Token Exchange `act` chain depth. When omitted, the system default applies.

max_delegation_depth_default.description:
Delegation depth applied when the tenant has no override, and the ceiling that an override cannot exceed.
The response exposes this value so the administrative UI can display the concrete limit and reject an excessive value before sending it.

trusted_device_max_age_seconds.description: How many seconds a trusted device stays valid. Zero, or leaving it out, disables the feature.

trusted_device_max_age_seconds_ceiling.description:
The ceiling on how many seconds a trusted device may stay valid. It is returned so the administration UI can state the
limit concretely and reject a larger value before sending it.

default_locale.description: The tenant's default locale. Unset, the system default locale is used.

supported_locales.description: The locales the catalogue ships translations for. It is returned so the administration UI can build the choices for the default locale and for notification templates.

Contract.AdminSettingsResponse.description:
What `/api/admin/settings` returns. It is a projection for the administration UI rather than the tenant itself, and
besides the tenant_id (a UUID), the realm (a URL slug), the display name, and the password policy override it returns the
standard PasswordPolicy values of the Authentication context, used both for display and for the weaker-policy gate.

Contract.AdminUserCreateRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator creates a user. The PasswordPolicy of the Authentication context applies to the initial password.

total_users.description: The exact number of Users in the tenant whose lifecycle status is not `deleted`. It is unaffected by `query` and `status`.

Contract.AdminUserListResponse.description: The user list of the administration API, together with the exact total number of users in the tenant, excluding the deleted ones and independent of `query` and `status`.

required_actions.description: The actions forced at the next sign-in.

password_changed_at.description: When the password was last changed.

disabled_at.description: The previous-generation field holding when the user was disabled. `User.lifecycle.status` plus `status_changed_at` is the single source of truth, and this field survives only for backward compatibility of the current response. It is an existing gap that needs its own cleanup, outside the scope of this migration.

updated_at.description: It equals `created_at` at creation and is updated on every administrative operation afterwards.

Contract.AdminUserResponse.description: How the administration API represents a user. `password_hash` is deliberately not part of the contract.

Contract.AdminUserUpdateRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator updates a user's mutable profile and roles. `id` and `password_hash` are left alone.

Contract.AdminWsFederationEndpointSet.description: The canonical details of the tenant, to feed into a WS-Federation RP or Microsoft Entra domain federation.

Contract.Agent.description: The minimal stub of the Agent principal the IdManagement context publishes.

Contract.AgentAccessRevoked.description: A summary event for audit and governance, recording that an Agent's access was revoked at once because of a kill switch or an owner offboarding.

Contract.AgentCredentialBindRequest.description: The JSON request binding an OAuth2Client to an Agent.

Contract.AgentCredentialBinding.description: The binding between an Agent and an OAuth2Client of the same tenant, unique on `agent_id` and `client_id`. An Agent obtains tokens using the credentials of the Client it is bound to. The `client_id` must name an OAuth2Client whose `tenant_id` matches the Agent's (AgentReferencesStayTenantLocal). One `client_id` cannot be bound to more than one Agent, which BindAgentCredential checks in its preconditions.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

Contract.AgentCredentialBound.description: An administrator bound an OAuth2Client to an Agent.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

Contract.AgentCredentialUnbound.description: An administrator unbound an OAuth2Client from an Agent.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

Contract.AgentDeleted.description: An administrator deleted an Agent. Its bindings were released by cascade.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

Contract.AgentDisabled.description: An administrator suspended an Agent reversibly.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

Contract.AgentEnabled.description: An administrator returned a suspended Agent to service.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

Contract.AgentKilled.description: An administrator killed an Agent. This is one-way and terminal; there is no way back.

Contract.AgentKind.description: How autonomous an Agent is. `autonomous` runs on its own; `supervised` runs under human supervision.

Contract.AgentListResponse.description: The Agent list of the administration API.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.AgentNameRequiredError.description: The `name` of an Agent is empty. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:agent_name_required`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

Contract.AgentOwnerChanged.description: An administrator transferred the owner (`owner_user_id`) of an Agent.

status.description: Active, Disabled, or Killed. Binding to anything but Active is refused fail-closed.

Contract.AgentRef.description: Published-language stub for the Agent principal the IdManagement context publishes, carrying only the attributes binding verification needs.

owner_user_id.description: Left out, the caller's id becomes the owner.

Contract.AgentRegisterRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator registers an Agent. Leaving `owner_user_id` out makes the caller the owner.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

source_event_id.description: A reference for tracing what advanced the epoch: the domain event, or the `jti` of the inbound SET.

Contract.AgentRevocationEpoch.description: The one-to-one companion record holding the revocation epoch of an Agent. An access token or session whose `issued_at` precedes the epoch is treated as invalid (fail-closed). The epoch advances on KillAgent, DisableAgent, UnbindAgentCredential, a Disable or Delete of the owner (`owner_user_id`), or an accepted inbound SecurityEvent. An Agent with no row has never been revoked.

Contract.AgentStatus.description: The operational state of an Agent. `active` runs normally, `disabled` is a reversible suspension, and `killed` is an emergency stop that is one-way and terminal. Anything but `active` issues no new token, fail-closed.

client_ids.description: The id of the OAuth2Client it is bound to.

Contract.AgentSummaryResponse.description: How an Agent is represented. The list and the detail views of the administration UI return the same representation.

Contract.AgentUpdateRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator updates an Agent's name, description, kind, `owner_user_id`, or roles. A field left out keeps its current value. Changing `owner_user_id` transfers ownership.

tenantId.description: The tenant the Agent belongs to.

Contract.AgentUpdated.description: An administrator updated an Agent's name, description, kind, or roles.

tenant_id.description: The tenant it belongs to. It matches `WorkloadTrustBundle.tenant_id`.

trust_bundle_id.description: The id of the WorkloadTrustBundle it belongs to.

subject_pattern.description: A glob pattern matched against the `sub` claim of the external attestation token, such as `spiffe://example.org/ns/*/sa/agent-*` or `system:serviceaccount:prod-agents:*`. Duplicates within one `trust_bundle_id` are forbidden.

agent_id.description: The Agent to project onto. It must be an existing Agent whose `tenant_id` matches the WorkloadTrustBundle's.

Contract.AgentWorkloadBinding.description: A mapping under a WorkloadTrustBundle that projects a glob pattern over external subjects onto an Agent of the same tenant. `agent_id` must name an existing Agent whose `tenant_id` matches the WorkloadTrustBundle's (WorkloadIdentityReferencesStayTenantLocal).

Contract.AgentWorkloadBindingAgentNotFou.description: The `agent_id` given does not resolve to an Agent in the tenant. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:agent_workload_binding_agent_not_found`.

Contract.AgentWorkloadBindingCreateReque.description: The JSON request an administrator sends to create an AgentWorkloadBinding.

Contract.AgentWorkloadBindingEnabled.description: An administrator re-enabled a disabled AgentWorkloadBinding.

Contract.AgentWorkloadBindingListRespons.description: The AgentWorkloadBinding list of the administration API.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

Contract.AgentWorkloadBindingPatternRequ.description: `subject_pattern` is empty. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:agent_workload_binding_pattern_required`.

Contract.AgentWorkloadBindingResponse.description: How an AgentWorkloadBinding is represented. The list and the detail endpoints of the administration API return the same representation.

user_id.description: The active User that issued the token. An `account:*` operation always acts on this User and no other.

client_id.description: The built-in public client id the realm owns. Issuing a token through the administration API does not require an OAuth client to be registered first.

Contract.ApiToken.description: The management record of a tenant-scoped JWT access token, which authenticates the administration API, the SCIM API, and the issuer's own account API. A token is not authorized once its scopes are empty, once `expires_at` has passed, or once `revoked_at` is set. The JWT itself is returned once, at issuance, and never stored.

Contract.ApiTokenMetadata.description: The token metadata returned by the list and issue responses. It never carries the JWT itself.

Contract.ApiTokenPrincipal.description: The authentication context resolved from a valid API access token: the tenant, the issuer's subject, and the scopes.

Contract.ApiTokenScope.description: The canonical list of scopes an API access token may carry, written as `<resource>:<action>` (read for queries, write for changes). The `scim:*` scopes belong to the SCIM 2.0 inbound provisioning API alone and split users and groups against read and write. The SCIM discovery endpoints (ServiceProviderConfig, ResourceTypes, Schemas) are readable with any `scim:*` scope. The Application aggregate and its protocol bindings sit under `applications:*`, while the standalone protocol and resource management APIs split into `oauth-clients:*`, `authorization-detail-types:*`, `mcp-resource-servers:*`, `saml:*`, `wsfed:*`, `provisioning:*`, `workload-identity:*`, and `shared-signals:*`. The `account:*` scopes belong to the self-service API of the token's own issuer, separating read from write and carving out the sensitive facets of MFA, sessions, consent, and passwords. Public, protocol, step-up, and email verification endpoints take no scope at all.

Contract.AppAccessDeniedByPolicy.description: Federation was refused by an Application sign-in policy.

application_id.description: The global UUID foreign key to the parent Application. The tenant boundary follows from that parent.

Contract.AppSignInPolicy.description: The sign-in policy of one Application, owned by the ApplicationCatalog. When it holds any rule it replaces the tenant default outright for that application; when it holds none, the default applies. This is an override model. A setting weaker than the default can still be saved, and the UI warns about it.

Contract.AppSignInPolicyRequest.description: The request in which an administrator replaces the sign-in policy of an Application. Sending any rule overrides the tenant default; sending none returns it to applying the default.

effective_rules.description: The rule sequence actually evaluated under the override model: `policy.rules` when the application holds any rule, and `tenant_default.rules` when it does not.

weaker_than_default.description: True when the application's own policy is weaker than the default, that is, when it loosens the authentication strength, the reauthentication window, or the permitted networks. It is for a UI warning and does not stop evaluation.

Contract.AppSignInPolicyResponse.description:
How the sign-in policy of an Application is represented. It lets the application detail screen tell apart the application's
own override (`policy`), the tenant default (`tenant_default`), and the effective rule sequence that actually applies.

Contract.AppSignInPolicyUpdated.description: The sign-in policy of an Application was updated.

Contract.AppStepUpRequired.description: A step-up became necessary to satisfy the authentication strength of an Application sign-in policy.

Contract.Application.description: A published stub the Application context owns. A ProvisioningConnection exists at most once per Application.

Contract.ApplicationAssigned.description: A user or a group was assigned to an Application.

Contract.ApplicationAssignment.description: A published stub the Application context owns, used to resolve the target set when `scope` is `assigned_only`.

Contract.ApplicationAssignmentRequest.description: The request assigning an Application. Leaving `visibility` out means `visible`.

Contract.ApplicationCategoriesRequest.description: The request replacing the set of categories assigned to an Application. `category_ids` may hold only categories that already exist in the tenant.

position.description: The display order of the section; smaller comes first, and ties break by name ascending.

Contract.ApplicationCategory.description:
A portal section an administrator defines per tenant. An Application carries zero or more of them, and
the user portal groups its tiles into sections by category. It never crosses the assignment boundary: a section holds
only the apps assigned to that user.

Contract.ApplicationCategoryDeleted.description: An ApplicationCategory was deleted. It was removed from the Applications it was assigned to as well.

Contract.ApplicationClaimMappingUpdated.description: The claim release override of an Application was updated: the rules, and the source attribute of `sub` or of the NameID.

Contract.ApplicationClientSecretCredenti.description: Non-sensitive metadata projecting an OAuth2 credential for the Application editor. It exposes neither the OAuth2 hash nor the plaintext, and derives the state from `revoked_at`, `expires_at`, and the time of evaluation.

Contract.ApplicationIconUpdated.description: The stored icon of an Application was uploaded or deleted.

Contract.ApplicationIconUploadResponse.description: How an Application is represented after its icon has been uploaded or deleted.

Contract.ApplicationKind.description: The kind of an Application. `federated` is a business application tied together by SSO federation, `weblink` is an external link with no SSO, and `service` is a machine-to-machine client_credentials API client -- Okta's API Services, with neither a portal tile nor user assignments.

client_secret_rotatable.description: True only for a confidential client using client_secret_basic or client_secret_post. False for private_key_jwt, mTLS, and a public client.

secret_credentials.description: Credential metadata carrying neither a hash nor a plaintext. The editor shows the creation time, the expiry, and whether the credential is Active, Expired, or Revoked.

sub_source_attribute.description:
The source attribute used for the `sub` claim of the ID token and UserInfo. Left unset, the
user's internal id is used, which is the default behaviour. It overrides the subject identifier the same way
`name_id_source` does for WS-Fed and SAML.

rules.description:
The claim release override for this application. Independently of what the scope-driven
standard claims (profile, email, and so on) would disclose, it narrows or remaps what is released.
An attribute whose visibility is `private`, and a reserved claim type, are refused by the floor.

Contract.ApplicationOidcConfig.description: The real settings of the OAuth2 client the OIDC protocol of an Application points at, for the application detail screen. Advanced fields are included. `token_endpoint_auth_method`, `client_type`, and `fapi_profile` are immutable under the update contract and are shown for reference only.

sub_source_attribute.description: Left out, the existing setting is kept. Sending an empty string returns it to the default, the user's internal id.

rules.description: Left out, the existing claim release override is kept. Sending an empty array returns it to no override, meaning the standard claims alone.

Contract.ApplicationOidcConfigUpdateRequ.description:
The request updating the OIDC protocol settings. Only the fields given are changed. Advanced fields are included, while
fields immutable under the update contract, `token_endpoint_auth_method` among them, are not.

Contract.ApplicationOrdering.description:
The manual order on the user portal. Keyed by `user_id`, it holds the display order of Applications as a
sequence of `application_id` values. `user_id` names an existing, globally unique User.
An application in the sequence that is no longer assigned drops out of the list, and an assigned app absent from the
sequence is appended by name ascending. `application_ids` is kept as an array rather than a database foreign key, so
the use case validation of ReorderMyApplications is what confines it to Applications assigned to that user and visible.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.ApplicationOwnedProtocolError.description: The SAML service provider is owned by an Application and cannot be deleted on its own; delete the Application instead. Returned with HTTP 409. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:application_owned_protocol`.

type.description: The protocol kind.

wtrealm.description: The `wtrealm` of the WS-Fed RP that `wsfed` points at.

Contract.ApplicationProtocol.description: A reference to the single protocol configuration an Application is tied to. It carries only the key that matches `type`, and the protocol row is related back to the Application through its `application_id` as an ordinary foreign key.

Contract.ApplicationProtocolType.description: The single protocol an Application uses. It cannot be changed after creation.

Contract.ApplicationProvisionType.description: The application kind chosen at bulk creation. `oidc`, `saml`, and `wsfed` create a federated Application together with the matching protocol settings and publish both to the catalogue atomically; `weblink` creates an external link with no SSO; and `service` creates a machine-to-machine client_credentials OAuth2 client of the `service` kind.

idp_profile_id.description: The id of the IdP profile in the same tenant that every SAML SP is assigned to.

Contract.ApplicationSamlConfig.description: The real settings of the service provider the SAML protocol of an Application points at, for the application detail screen.

idp_profile_id.description: The IdP profile in the same tenant to assign to the SP. When a dedicated profile is already in use by another SP, the update is refused.

Contract.ApplicationSamlConfigUpdateRequ.description: The request partially updating the SAML protocol settings. It updates the ACS and SLO URLs, the audience, the NameID, the signature policy, and the claim rules.

Contract.ApplicationUnassigned.description: An assignment was removed from an Application.

Contract.ApplicationUpdated.description: The metadata of an Application was updated.

Contract.ApplicationWsFedConfig.description: The real settings of the relying party the WS-Fed protocol of an Application points at, for the application detail screen. The per-RP advanced fields -- audience, token type, claim rules -- are included. Entra domain federation is handled separately, as a per-tenant setting.

Contract.ApplicationWsFedConfigUpdateReq.description: The request updating the WS-Federation protocol settings. Only the fields given are changed. The per-RP advanced fields -- audience, token type, claim rules -- are included. Entra domain federation is out of scope here.

client_id.description: The client that raised the approval request.

agent_id.description: The Agent bound to the client, when there is one. It is used on the approval screen and in the `agent_id` claim of the tokens issued.

user_id.description: The `sub` of the User who decides. It is resolved from `login_hint` or `id_token_hint`, and from then on only that User may decide.

scopes.description: The scopes of the token to issue if it is approved.

authorization_details.description: RFC 9396: the structured permission request being approved. The approval screen renders it for a human to read.

binding_message.description: The short identifying text shown on the approval screen so the wrong request cannot be approved by mistake (CIBA Core section 7.1, `binding_message`).

auth_req_id_hash.description: The SHA-256 hash of the CIBA `auth_req_id`. It is an index of the transport layer and takes no part in the meaning of the decision.

interval_seconds.description: Transport bookkeeping: the minimum polling interval in seconds the client is told to keep. It rises on every `slow_down`.

last_polled_at.description: Transport bookkeeping: when it was last polled. It decides `slow_down`.

Contract.ApprovalRequest.description:
The approval request that holds a client's request until a human settles it. The state and the content of the
decision are kept apart from the transport bookkeeping of CIBA, but they sit in the same record so that a competing
decision and a poll serialize inside one store boundary. The `id` is a UUID, and only the SHA-256 hash of the
`auth_req_id` is stored, as the index.

Contract.ApprovalRequestState.description: The states the ApprovalRequestLifecycle state machine may take. It is held as the general form of "a precondition is not yet satisfied" rather than as CIBA transport vocabulary. `consumed` is a terminal state reachable only from `approved`, standing for the single exchange into tokens. See the state machine section as well.

Contract.Approve.description: The event where a device authorization was approved.

Contract.AssignmentSubjectType.description: Published-language stub for a definition the Application context owns.

Contract.AssignmentVisibility.description: The visibility of an assignment. Published-language stub for a definition the Application context owns, used only for the `visibility` of an `assign_application` action.

Contract.AttrVisibility.description: Published-language stub for the attribute visibility the Tenancy context owns. Only `private` is excluded unconditionally by the fail-closed floor of claim issuance.

Contract.AttributeApplyOn.description: When an AttributeMappingRule applies. Use `create_only` for a field whose manual change downstream should be respected.

source_key.description: Required when `source_kind` is `attribute`: the attribute key on the IdMagic side.

constant_value.description: Required when `source_kind` is `constant`. Any JSON value, because the constant is written straight into the target attribute and the remote SCIM schema decides what that attribute may hold.

required.description: When true, a value that cannot be resolved fails the delivery, fail-closed.

default_value.description: Used when the source resolves to nothing. Any JSON value, for the same reason as `constant_value`: the remote SCIM schema decides what the target attribute may hold.

Contract.AttributeMappingRule.description: The declarative mapping of one output attribute. `target_path` is a SCIM attribute path, and may be simple, complex, a multi-valued filter, or an enterprise extension.

Contract.AttributeSourceKind.description: Where the value of an AttributeMappingRule comes from. An `expression` (a function evaluation) is out of scope for the first version; only a direct reference and a fixed value are permitted.

Contract.AttributeType.description: The sum type discriminator of an attribute value. Published-language stub for a definition the Tenancy context owns.

Contract.AttributeValue.description: The value of one attribute, as a sum type: only the field `type` names is set. It is shared by the built-in OIDC attributes and the tenant-defined custom ones.

one_or_many.description: A JSON string, or an array of one or more JSON strings.

Contract.Audience.description: A string, or an array of one or more strings (JWT, RFC 7519 section 4.1.3).

field.description: The `field` of an AuditEventSearchAttribute in the registry.

operator.description: An operator listed in the attribute's `allowed_operators`.

values.description: The values, as many as the operator takes: one for `eq`, N for `in`, two for `time_range`. For a PII attribute the server transforms the plaintext input before matching.

Contract.AuditEventFilterExpression.description:
One term of `AuditEventQuery.filter`: a field and an operator from the registry allow list together with the values, as one
element of the conjunction (AND). Arbitrary SQL is not permitted.

Contract.AuditEventFilterOperator.description: The comparison operators an audit search filter expression may use. The registry declares which operators each attribute permits. `eq` is an exact match, `in` matches any member of a value set, `contains` is a substring match (used by `q`), and `time_range` bounds `occurred_at`.

type.description: Exact match on `type`, the low-level machine-facing filter. For example, `AccessTokenIssued`.

category.description: Narrows by event category: authentication, success, fail, aggregated, user, group, client, consent, token, tenant, or key.

user_id.description:
Exact match on the actor's user sub. It names the same thing as `actor.id` in `filter` (see AuditActorVsTarget).
To narrow by the user an administrative operation acted on, use `target.id` in `filter` instead -- a different concept
from this field. The UI labels it "user id (actor)".

username.description:
Searches by the actor's login name. Events where the real account is always settled -- UserAuthenticated, the OAuth2
flow events, and the like -- carry no username in their payload, so the search resolves the name to a user id through
UserRepo and then narrows exactly as `user_id` does. When no such user exists the result is empty; it never falls back
to ignoring the filter and returning everything. It cannot be used to search authentication failures, where an account
name that never existed still has to be traceable -- use `actor.username` in `filter` for that.

cursor.description:
Pass through the value embedded in the URL of the response's Link header. It is a stateless, versioned, opaque token
holding the direction, the anchor, the page number it moves to, and the keyset in a compact binary payload, signed with
the tenant, the sort, and the filter as associated data. A new v3 token does not expire with time, and legacy v0 and v2
tokens are still accepted under their existing rules.

q.description: Free text matched as a substring against the text columns stored raw (`type`, `outcome`, and the like). PII columns are excluded.

filter.description:
A conjunction (AND) of structured search terms over the field/operator allow list of the registry. `actor.username` is a
plaintext match reserved for authentication failures, where an account name that never existed still has to be traceable;
it is not hashed. To search events where the real account is settled, use the `username` query parameter instead -- a
different path from this field. `client.ip` is matched in plaintext too, neither truncated nor hashed. `event.type` draws
from the allow list of type names in the events section of the specification (`owns_events`), and `outcome` from the enum
the Go `eventOutcome` classification defines (success or failure); both are picked from a list rather than typed freely
(see AuditActorVsTarget and AuditSearchRegistry). `actor.id` and `actor.username` name the actor while `target.id` names
the user an administrative operation acted on -- different meanings. `workflow.id`, `workflow_run.id`, and
`workflow_step.id` are registry attributes matched with `eq` against the workflowId, runId, and stepIndex of the
IdGovernance LifecycleWorkflow*, WorkflowRun*, and WorkflowStepFailed events. Attribute values and email bodies are not in
the payload, so they are not searchable either.

Contract.AuditEventQuery.description:
The query parameters of ListAdminAuditEvents. `tenant_id` comes from the context, so it is not a field here.
`type` is a type name from the events section of the specification.

field.description: The canonical dotted name of the search axis, such as `actor.username`, `client.ip`, or `event.type`.

raw_storable.description: Whether the plaintext may be stored in the sidecar as it is. True for every attribute today.

transform.description: The transform applied to the plaintext before storing or searching. Only `none` exists today.

allowed_operators.description: The allow list of operators this attribute permits.

ui_visible.description: Whether to offer it as a UI preset in the administrative search builder.

Contract.AuditEventSearchAttribute.description:
A search axis permitted in audit event search, that is, one registry entry. It declares the field/operator allow list and
so fixes a closed search grammar in place of arbitrary SQL or JSONPath. The Go AuditSearchRegistry is the twin of this
value object. Every attribute, `actor.username` and `client.ip` included, is stored and searched in the sidecar as
plaintext. `actor.id` and `actor.username` name the actor -- who did it -- while `target.id` names the user an
administrative operation acted on -- who it was done to; the same word "user" means different things (AuditActorVsTarget).
`event.type` and `outcome` are picked from a list rather than typed freely: `event.type` from the type names in the events
section (`owns_events`), and `outcome` from the two values Go's `eventOutcome()` returns, success and failure, with no
value at all for events it does not classify.

event_types.description:
The `event.type` values that can be picked, that is, the type names of the events section. It is the union of the
categorized types, the same population the event category picker in the administration UI draws from.

outcomes.description: The `outcome` values that can be picked. Today there are two, success and failure, and only authentication events are classified.

Contract.AuditEventSearchOptionsResponse.description:
The choices that turn `event.type` and `outcome` into pick lists. The UI does not hard-code them; it reads them from the
same single source of truth in Go (the category-to-type map and the eventOutcome classification).

Contract.AuditEventSearchTransform.description:
The transform applied to a plaintext value before a search attribute is stored in the sidecar or searched. Today only
`none` exists, meaning the value is stored raw.

Contract.AuthenticateUser.description: The event where resource owner authentication succeeded.

Contract.AuthenticationContext.description: The authentication result the Authentication bounded context hands to the OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect bounded context. The latter never looks at passwords, the UserRepository, or the details of the session cookie.

tenantId.description: The tenant the aggregation happened in.

keyHash.description: The SHA-256 of the username in lowercase, or of the IP, as hex.

count.description: How many fell in the window at emission; the real number keeps rising in the bucket store.

topKeys.description: The `keyHash` values seen most often in the window, at most five.

Contract.AuthenticationEventAggregated.description:
Records that, during a flood of credential attempts, individual AuthenticationFailed events were aggregated
into a bucket keyed by `(tenantId, kind, keyHash, 5-minute window)` rather than written one row at a time. Only the
first event of a window is emitted, and later ones add to the count in the bucket store. The `count` in this payload
is therefore the value at emission, and the real number is observed through ListAuthenticationEventBuckets.
`keyHash` is SHA-256 as hex, so no plaintext reaches the audit log, following LoginThrottled.

Contract.AuthenticationEventBucket.description:
The projection of one authentication event aggregate (bucket) for administrative display. It is the result of
aggregating individual sign-in failures into 5-minute windows during an attack: `window_start` is when the window
began, `count` is the running total inside it, and `first_seen` and `last_seen` are the first and last times inside it.
`key_hash` is SHA-256 as hex and holds no plaintext. It stays inside the tenant boundary.

Contract.AuthenticationEventBucketListRe.description: What ListAuthenticationEventBuckets returns, by `window_start` descending, newest window first.

tenantId.description: The tenant the authentication was attempted in, taken from the request path.

ip.description: The client IP. It is stored in plaintext for as long as the audit event is retained.

userAgent.description: The client User-Agent. It is stored in plaintext for as long as the audit event is retained.

deviceFingerprint.description: The device fingerprint. It is stored in plaintext for as long as the audit event is retained.

Contract.AuthenticationFailed.description:
A ResourceOwner failed to authenticate. It is an input event for rate limiting and fraud detection.
Attempts against a username that does not exist are recorded too, so there is no `sub`; the username is kept in
plaintext as the `actor.username` correlation key for audit search. The username and the other client attributes are
not hashed, and are kept for the same retention as the other failure events, 30 days by default.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.AuthenticationRequiredError.description: The request needs an authenticated session and does not have one. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:authentication_required`. Distinct from AccessDeniedError, which means the session exists but the policy denies the operation.

Contract.AuthenticationStepCompleted.description: One step of a multi-step authentication flow -- password, totp, webauthn, and so on -- succeeded. It is an input to settling the acr.

Contract.AuthenticationStepFailed.description: One step of a multi-step authentication flow failed.

Contract.AuthenticatorResetCompleted.description: An administrator's authenticator reset completed. It records the factors deleted and the recomputed `mfa_enrolled`. When both TOTP and WebAuthn are gone, `reenrollment_required` is true and a separate MfaEnrollmentBypassIssued is emitted.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.AuthenticatorResetNotAllowedErr.description: The requested combination of reset targets is not valid for the current MFA state of the target user. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:authenticator_reset_not_allowed`.

Contract.AuthenticatorResetRequest.description: The set an administrator names for deletion when resetting a target user's authenticators.

Contract.AuthenticatorResetRequested.description: An administrator asked for an authenticator reset on a target user. It is emitted before anything is deleted, so what was targeted at the time of the request stays in the audit trail.

Contract.AuthenticatorResetResponse.description: The result of an authenticator reset. `reenrollment_required` says that both TOTP and WebAuthn are now gone and a single-use bypass was issued automatically, so the next sign-in enters the enrollment-only pending flow. The bypass is present only when `reenrollment_required` is true.

Contract.AuthenticatorResetTarget.description: What an administrator's authenticator reset may target. `totp` and `webauthn` mean deleting every MfaFactor or WebAuthnCredential; `recovery_code` means deleting the whole set of backup recovery codes.

tenantId.description: The tenant the authorization code was issued in.

Contract.AuthorizationCodeIssued.description: An AuthorizationCode was issued as `/authorize` completed. It has to be exchanged at `/token` within 60 seconds.

amr.description: The authentication methods carried over from the authorization request. They are emitted into the ID token and the access token.

acr.description: The ACR URN carried over from the authorization request. It is emitted into the ID token and the access token.

sid.description: The OIDC session id carried over from the authorization request. It propagates into the `sid` claim of the ID token and into the `sid` of the RefreshTokenRecord issued.

authorization_details.description: RFC 9396: the structured details consented to. The exchange reflects them into the tokens issued.

redeemed_at.description: When the state became `redeemed`, for audit.

issued_family_id.description: The refresh family issued by a successful exchange, used to revoke the family when a replay is detected.

Contract.AuthorizationCodeRecord.description: The persistent record of an issued authorization code. The code itself is short-lived. Its state follows AuthorizationCodeRecordLifecycle, which describes the lifecycle of the code itself along a different axis from AuthorizationCodeFlow.

Contract.AuthorizationCodeRecordState.description: The states the AuthorizationCodeRecordLifecycle state machine may take. It describes the lifecycle of the code itself, along a different axis from AuthorizationCodeFlow.

tenantId.description: The tenant the exchange happened in.

Contract.AuthorizationCodeRedeemed.description: An AuthorizationCode was exchanged correctly at `/token`. Reusing the same code revokes the family.

Contract.AuthorizationCodeState.description: The states the AuthorizationCodeFlow state machine may take. See the state machine section as well.

type.description: The identifier of the registered AuthorizationDetailType, `payment_initiation` for instance.

locations.description: RFC 9396: the URIs of the resource servers the detail is aimed at.

actions.description: RFC 9396: the actions permitted against the target.

datatypes.description: RFC 9396: the kinds of data to be accessed.

identifier.description: RFC 9396: the identifier of the target resource.

privileges.description: RFC 9396: the privilege levels against the target.

fields.description: The structured fields specific to the type, `instructedAmount` and `creditorAccount` for instance. The registered schema binds their meaning.

Contract.AuthorizationDetail.description: One element of RFC 9396 `authorization_details`: a structured, fine-grained permission identified by its `type`. It is handled consistently through the request, the consent, and its reflection into the token, and is validated fail-closed against the registered AuthorizationDetailType.

name.description: The field it governs: a standard field such as `actions`, or a key inside the `fields` map.

semantics.description: The partial order used for the subset check.

required.description: When true, the detail must carry this field.

allowed.description: The closed set of permitted values when `semantics` is `set` or `enum`; empty means unrestricted.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailFieldRule.description: One field rule of an AuthorizationDetailsSchema, defining its downscoping partial order and its permitted values.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailFieldSemanti.description: The downscoping partial order each field carries in a registered authorization_details schema. `set` is set inclusion (the request is a subset of the consent or the source), `at_most` is monotone decrease (the request is at most the consent or the source), `enum` is an exact match against a permitted list, and `exact` is an exact match on an opaque value. Anything undecidable falls to the refusing side, fail-closed.

type.description: The `authorization_details` type identifier.

display_template.description: The template presenting a detail to a human in the consent UI, `up to {fields.instructedAmount} to {identifier}` for instance.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailType.description: An `authorization_details` type definition a tenant registers. It bundles the type identifier, the validation schema, and the display template for the consent UI. Only an `enabled` type is accepted. Management is guarded by AdminAuthorizationDetailTypesManage.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailTypeListResp.description: The `authorization_details` type list of the administration API.

type.description: Required at creation. On update the `type` from the path is used.
