Contract.AuthorizationDetailTypeRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator registers or updates an `authorization_details` type (RFC 9396). `type` is settable at creation only.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailTypeResponse.description: How an `authorization_details` type is represented. The list and the detail views of the administration UI return the same representation.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailTypeState.description: The operational states of an AuthorizationDetailType. Only `enabled` is accepted; `disabled` refuses new requests, and tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailsConsented.description: RFC 9396: a ResourceOwner consented to the `authorization_details` presented. It becomes the yardstick for the subset check at issuance and exchange.

reason.description: Why it was refused, `invalid_authorization_details` for instance.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailsRejected.description: RFC 9396: the request was refused fail-closed because the `authorization_details` were malformed, named an unregistered type, did not fit the schema, went beyond the consent, or exceeded the downscope.

userId.description: The `sub` of the principal, when it was already settled at the time of the request.

detailTypes.description: The types of the details requested.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailsRequested.description: RFC 9396: a client asked for `authorization_details` at `/authorize`, `/par`, or `/token`, and the request passed validation against the registered type.

Contract.AuthorizationDetailsSchema.description: The structural schema of one type. It lists the fields accepted and the downscoping partial order of each. An unregistered field, a mismatch against the schema, and a value outside the permitted set are all refused, fail-closed.

tenant_id.description: The tenant it belongs to. Cross-tenant references are forbidden.

version.description: The revision, rising monotonically within the tenant and starting at 1.

Contract.AuthorizationModel.description: The authorization model of a tenant. Revisions are only appended, and the latest published one decides every check. A revision referring to an unknown relation or type is refused fail-closed at registration.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.AuthorizationModelInvalidError.description: Registering the authorization model was rejected by validation: a reference to an unknown type or relation, a name that breaks the naming rules, a cycle in the rewrite rules, or a missing required field. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:authorization_model_invalid`.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.AuthorizationModelNotFoundError.description: The tenant has no published authorization model. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:authorization_model_not_found`.

Contract.AuthorizationModelPublished.description: An administrator published a new revision of the tenant's authorization model.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.AuthorizationPendingError.description: In the Device Authorization Grant, the user has not approved yet (RFC 8628 section 3.5, authorization_pending). The client waits `interval` seconds and retries.

amr.description: The methods by which authentication succeeded, propagated from the AuthenticationContext by `advance(authenticate_user)`.

acr.description: The URN derived from the amr according to the AuthenticationContextPolicy.

acr_values.description: The `acr_values` parameter the client gave to `/authorize` (RFC 8176). It decides step-up.

sid.description:
The OIDC session id propagated from `AuthenticationContext.session_id` by `advance(authenticate_user)`,
equal to `LoginSession.id` of the Authentication context. It is carried into the AuthorizationCodeRecord,
the RefreshTokenRecord, and the IdTokenClaims, and correlates both the family revocation a session revocation starts
and the front-channel and back-channel logout.

authorization_details.description: RFC 9396: the structured details the client requested. Only those already validated and conforming to a registered type are kept.

Contract.AuthorizationRequest.description: The server-internal intermediate state that tracks the flow.

resource.description: The RFC 8707 resource indicator. When it matches no registered, active McpResourceServer it is refused with `invalid_target`, and so is naming the parameter more than once.

Contract.AuthorizeParameters.description: The authorization parameters of `GET /authorize` or of a PAR. Every field is single-valued, and naming a parameter more than once is refused as `invalid_request`. `prompt` is a space-separated set of the unique tokens `login`, `consent`, and `none`, and `none` is never combined with another.

tenantId.description: The tenant the approval happened in.

Contract.BackchannelAuthApproved.description: CIBA Core section 7.3: the User being asked approved the request.

tenantId.description: The tenant the refusal happened in.

Contract.BackchannelAuthDenied.description: CIBA Core section 7.3: the User being asked refused the request.

tenantId.description: The tenant the expiry happened in.

Contract.BackchannelAuthExpired.description: CIBA Core section 11: an approval request reached its expiry without being decided.

tenantId.description: The tenant the approval request was accepted in.

Contract.BackchannelAuthRequested.description: CIBA Core section 7.3: an approval request was raised for a human to settle. The `auth_req_id` is a bearer secret and does not reach the audit log.

login_hint.description: The hint naming the User to ask. It resolves as a username or an email address.

id_token_hint.description: A valid ID token this OP issued. Its signature, `iss`, `aud`, `sub`, and `exp` are verified to resolve the User to ask.

scope.description: The scopes of the token to issue if it is approved. It is required, has to hold `openid`, and has to be a subset of the scopes the client declared.

authorization_details.description: RFC 9396: the structured permission request being approved, as a JSON string. Only registered types are accepted.

binding_message.description: The short identifying text shown on the approval screen (CIBA Core section 7.1).

requested_expiry.description: The lifetime the client asks for, in seconds. A positive integer, at most 600. 300 when left out.

Contract.BackchannelAuthenticationReques.description:
The `/bc-authorize` request (CIBA Core section 7.1), by which a client raises a request for human approval.
Exactly one of `login_hint` and `id_token_hint` is given, and when neither resolves the request is refused
fail-closed with `unknown_user_id`. `user_code` is not supported and is not advertised in discovery.

interval.description: The minimum polling interval, in seconds, the client has to keep.

Contract.BackchannelAuthenticationRespon.description:
The `/bc-authorize` response (CIBA Core section 7.3). The `auth_req_id` is a bearer secret, and the
client presents it to the token endpoint under the CIBA grant while polling.

Contract.BackupCodeConsumed.description: A backup recovery code was consumed, recovering access after TOTP or WebAuthn was lost.

Contract.BrowserChangePasswordRequest.description: The JSON an SPA posts to `/api/auth/change_password`. The authenticated session cookie resolves the `sub`, and CSRF is verified through the `X-CSRF-Token` header.

Contract.BrowserConsentRequest.description: The consent decision an SPA posts to `/api/auth/consent`.

Contract.BrowserCsrfContext.description: The CSRF token bootstrap information an unauthenticated browser form uses together with a SameSite cookie.

Contract.BrowserDeviceContextResponse.description: The no-store JSON an SPA uses to render the device `user_code` screen.

Contract.BrowserDeviceRequest.description: The device `user_code` decision an SPA posts to `/api/auth/device`.

Contract.BrowserFlowResponse.description: The next screen, or the client redirect URI, to show after an SPA authentication step.

Contract.BrowserForgotPasswordRequest.description: The JSON an SPA posts to `/api/auth/forgot_password`, an unauthenticated route. To prevent enumeration it always returns 204, whether or not the email exists.

Contract.BrowserMfaEnrollmentConfirmRequ.description: Settles a TOTP enrollment inside the administrator-approved login enrollment flow. Neither the secret nor the code reaches the audit trail or a log.

Contract.BrowserRecoveryCodeRequest.description:
The input of SubmitBrowserRecoveryCode: it consumes one recovery code as the second factor.
The code never reaches the audit trail or a log.

Contract.BrowserResetPasswordRequest.description: The JSON an SPA posts to `/api/auth/reset_password`. It takes the single-use token from the email link together with the new password.

code.description: The numeric code the authenticator app generated: six digits (RFC 6238 section 4 and RFC 4226 section 4).

return_to.description: Where to go inside the same realm when a direct sign-in to the administration console continues.

remember_device.description:
The user's explicit consent to remember this device and skip the second factor from now on. It is ignored
when the tenant has trusted devices turned off.

Contract.BrowserTotpRequest.description: The TOTP code a browser client posts to `/api/auth/totp`. The authorization request id is resolved from the HttpOnly transaction cookie and the CSRF from the `X-CSRF-Token` header. Other factors, WebAuthn among them, have a very different HTTP shape and so are defined independently, with their own endpoint and their own value object.

kind.description: Which screen to render: login, totp, consent, device, and more as factors are added.

client_name.description:
The readable name of the client shown on the consent screen. It resolves in the order `OAuth2Client.client_name`,
the Application catalogue name, then the client_id, which is a UUID and is avoided in raw form.

Contract.BrowserTransactionResponse.description: The no-store JSON an SPA uses to render the current browser authorization transaction.

assertion.description: The PublicKeyCredential holding an assertion response (WebAuthn Level 3).

remember_device.description:
The user's explicit consent to remember this device and skip the second factor from now on. It is ignored
when the tenant has trusted devices turned off.

Contract.BrowserWebAuthnRequest.description:
The input of SubmitBrowserWebAuthn: the assertion `navigator.credentials.get` returned, sent back as
JSON. The pending login session cookie resolves the `sub`, and `X-CSRF-Token` resolves CSRF.

Contract.CaepEvent.description: What a CAEP event means, before it is signed and wrapped into a SET.

Contract.CaepEventType.description: The CAEP event types that are implemented.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.CategoryNameRequiredError.description: The `name` of an ApplicationCategory is empty. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:category_name_required`.

Contract.ClaimMapping.description: The tenant-managed settings projecting verified upstream claims and attributes onto local identity fields. JIT provisioning requires a mapping for the subject and the username.

Contract.ClaimMappingPolicy.description: The minimal stub of the per-trust claim issuance rules the ClaimMapping context publishes.

claim_type.description: The claim type URI to emit, such as `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims/UPN`.

source.description: Where the claim value comes from.

source_key.description: The attribute name to read when `source` is `user_attribute`.

fixed_value.description: The fixed value to emit when `source` is `fixed`.

required.description: When true, issuance is refused if the source cannot be resolved (fail-closed).

Contract.ClaimMappingRule.description: The declarative mapping of one output claim: it builds the output claim type (a URI) from a source.

Contract.ClaimMappingSource.description: Where a claim value comes from. `user_attribute` reads an attribute of the identity principal, `fixed` emits a static value, and `nameid` carries the NameID that NameIdConfiguration resolved into a claim as well.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.ClaimReleaseDeniedError.description: Claim resolution was rejected fail-closed: a required source could not be resolved, an attribute whose visibility is `private` was named as the source of a rule or of the NameID, or a reserved claim type (iss, sub, aud, exp, iat, nbf, jti, azp, nonce, at_hash, c_hash, acr, amr, sid) was named as a `claim_type`. Reaches clients only through the OAuth 2.0 token and UserInfo endpoints, so it carries the OAuthError body rather than Problem Details.

client_id.description: It has to match the URL it was fetched from exactly.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: Absent is read as `none`. A document declaring any other value is refused.

Contract.ClientIDMetadataDocument.description: The Client ID Metadata Document fetched from an HTTPS URL the client hosts itself. The client_id is that fetch URL, and it has to match the client_id inside the document exactly. A document whose `token_endpoint_auth_method` is absent, or is anything other than `none`, is refused.

tenantId.description: The tenant the authorization request belongs to.

clientId.description: The URL it was fetched from.

reason.description: How the refusal is classified: a failed fetch, malformed JSON, a client_id mismatch, missing `redirect_uris`, an unsupported `token_endpoint_auth_method`, and so on.

Contract.ClientIdMetadataDocumentRejecte.description: For a client_id in URL form, fetching or verifying the Client ID Metadata Document failed and the request was refused fail-closed.

tenantId.description: The tenant the authorization request belongs to.

clientId.description: The URL it was fetched from.

Contract.ClientIdMetadataDocumentResolve.description: For a client_id in URL form, the Client ID Metadata Document was fetched and verified, and the authorization request went on. Nothing is registered persistently.

tenantId.description: The tenant the client belongs to.

Contract.ClientRegistered.description: A new client was registered dynamically at `/register` (RFC 7591). It is the starting point of the client registration audit trail.

Contract.ClientRegistrationRequest.description: The body of a dynamic client registration request to `/register` (RFC 7591). The OAuth2Client that results is derived from it.

client_secret.description: Returned only for a confidential client, and only in this response. It cannot be read back afterwards.

require_pushed_authorization_requests.description: Whether the client must use pushed authorization requests (RFC 9126).

dpop_bound_access_tokens.description: Whether the access tokens issued to this client are DPoP-bound (RFC 9449).

jwks.description: Echoed back only when the registration supplied an inline JWK Set.

jwks_uri.description: Echoed back only when the registration supplied a JWKS URL.

Contract.ClientRegistrationResponse.description: The client information response of Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591 section 3.2.1). It repeats the registered metadata as the server stored it, and carries `client_secret` exactly once, at registration, for a confidential client.

expires_at.description: When the credential expires. It is required for a newly added credential; null stands for a legacy credential from before the migration, which has no expiry, or for the current credential of a compatibility rotation.

revoked_at.description: When it was revoked outright. A credential with a `revoked_at` is not used for authentication whatever its `expires_at`.

Contract.ClientSecretCredential.description: The authentication credential of a secret-based OAuth2 client. The plaintext is returned only in the issuance response and appears in no storage, event, or listing. Issuing a new one leaves existing credentials alone, and they keep matching until they are revoked individually or expire. An existing credential with no expiry is tolerated so the migration needs no downtime.

Contract.ClientSecretCredentialMetadata.description: The non-sensitive metadata of a secret credential the Application editor shows. The state is derived from `revoked_at`, then `expires_at`, then the time of evaluation.

Contract.ClientSecretCredentialStatus.description: Published-language stub for the client secret credential state the OAuth2 context publishes.

Contract.ClientSecretIssued.description: Published-language stub for the event the OAuth2 context publishes when a client secret is additionally issued. It carries neither the secret nor its hash.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.ClientSecretLimitExceededError.description: An OAuth2Client already holds the maximum of two Active client secret credentials, so another one cannot be issued. Published-language stub for the limit error the OAuth2 context defines. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:client_secret_limit_exceeded`.

Contract.ClientSecretRevoked.description: Published-language stub for the event the OAuth2 context publishes when one client secret is revoked. It carries neither the secret nor its hash.

Contract.ClientSecretRotated.description: Through the compatibility interface, an administrator rotated or immediately revoked the credential of a secret-based client. Neither the secret nor a hash is in the payload.

sid.description: The OIDC session id, equal to `LoginSession.id`.

last_issued_at.description: It is updated on every re-issuance (re-authorization) to the same RP. It has no effect on resolving where to notify.

Contract.ClientSession.description:
The record that a given browser session (`sid`) issued an authentication result to a particular OAuth2Client
(an RP participation). The `sid` equals Authentication's `LoginSession.id` and is shared across RPs. The session state
itself is not copied here; this exists only as the index that resolves which RPs to notify by front-channel and
back-channel logout when a session is revoked.

Contract.ClientType.description: Published-language stub for the client kind owned by the OAuth2 context. Wire values follow RFC 6749 section 2.1.

Contract.CodeChallengeMethod.description: The hashing method of the PKCE `code_challenge` (RFC 7636). This application permits S256 alone; `plain` is refused as weak.

Contract.ConnectionQuarantined.description: `ProvisioningConnection.health` became quarantined, either from consecutive failures or from crossing the accidental-deletion guard. No further delivery is created.

revoked_at.description: When the state became `revoked`, for audit.

authorization_details.description: RFC 9396: the structured details the user consented to. It is the yardstick for the subset check at issuance and exchange.

Contract.Consent.description: The GDPR consent record. Its state follows the ConsentLifecycle state machine. `user_id` and `client_id` name an existing User and OAuth2Client.

tenantId.description: The tenant the consent was given in.

Contract.ConsentGranted.description: A ResourceOwner consented to a scope for a client. It is the record of obtaining a legal basis under GDPR Article 6.

tenantId.description: The tenant the consent belongs to.

actorUserId.description: The `sub` of the Administrator, when the withdrawal came through the administration API. It may be left out when the ResourceOwner withdrew it themselves.

Contract.ConsentRevoked.description: A ResourceOwner, or an Administrator of the tenant, withdrew an existing consent, exercising the right to withdraw under GDPR Article 7(3). Further issuance is blocked from then on.

Contract.ConsentState.description: The states the ConsentLifecycle state machine may take. The right to withdraw under GDPR Article 7(3) makes `granted` to `revoked` possible.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.ConsistencyNotSatisfiedError.description: The consistency token presented is newer than the write revision the store holds, or it belongs to another tenant. The check is fail-closed and rejects. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:consistency_not_satisfied`.

Contract.Consume.description: The lifecycle event consuming an approval request, once, into approved tokens.

Contract.DataEncryptionKeyBootstrapped.description: The tenant's first DataEncryptionKey (version 1, active) was generated.

Contract.DataEncryptionKeyDestroyed.description: The `wrapped_dek` was destroyed, so nothing encrypted under that version can ever be decrypted again.

Contract.DataEncryptionKeyDisabled.description: A retiring DataEncryptionKey was locked out by hand, immediately.

Contract.DataEncryptionKeyRotated.description: A new DataEncryptionKey became active and the previous version moved to retiring.

Contract.DataExportCanceled.description: An administrator cancelled a resource export before it terminated.

Contract.DataExportColumn.description: One column of the allow list for an export kind. `key` is the stable machine name, which is also the CSV header; `label` is for display alone; and `pii` says whether it holds personal information. The User allow list holds 13 built-in core columns plus `attr:<key>` -- 27 built-in extension attributes shared by every tenant, drawn from the OIDC profile, phone, and address claims and the SCIM enterprise organizational attributes -- and `custom:<key>`, the tenant-defined attributes resolved per tenant from the effective TenantUserAttributeSchema. Sensitive values such as `password_hash`, secrets, tokens, recovery codes, and MFA secrets are on no allow list at all.

Contract.DataExportDownloaded.description: An administrator downloaded a finished export file. It is kept in the audit trail as a high-risk operation that extracts PII in bulk.

Contract.DataExportError.description: Why an export failed. It returns no value, only a stable code.

Contract.DataExportExpired.description: The retention period elapsed and the export file itself was purged. The metadata and the audit trail remain.

Contract.DataExportFailed.description: Generating a resource export failed, and the incomplete file terminated without becoming downloadable.

Contract.DataExportFile.description: The finished export file returned on download. `content` is the CSV itself and may hold PII, so it is returned as a `Content-Disposition: attachment` only to an authorized administrator, and only for a job that has succeeded and not yet expired.

Contract.DataExportFormat.description: The output format of an export. At first, CSV (RFC 4180) alone.

Contract.DataExportJob.description: The public view of a resource export job, which doubles as its auditable record. It carries neither the CSV itself nor any PII value: only the target kind, the selected column keys, the counts, the byte size, the state, the expiry, and who asked for it.

Contract.DataExportRequest.description: The input starting an export. The target kind comes from the endpoint path and so is not in the body. It carries the output format, the column selection (a subset of the allow list), and the filter carried over from the list screen. A column key outside the allow list is refused.

Contract.DataExportRequested.description: An administrator asked for a resource export and the job was accepted. It carries no CSV value: only the target kind, the selected column keys, and who asked.

Contract.DataExportStarted.description: A worker started generating a resource export.

Contract.DataExportStatus.description: The state of a resource export job, matching DataExportLifecycle. `succeeded` means the file can be downloaded; `expired` means the file itself has been purged by its TTL and only the metadata and the audit trail remain.

Contract.DataExportSucceeded.description: A resource export finished generating and the file became downloadable. Only the row count and the byte size are recorded; no value is.

Contract.DataExportTargetKind.description: The resource kind a CSV export targets. The column definitions are closed within a per-kind allow list, so an unreviewed attribute cannot leave on its own.

Contract.DataKeyStillReferencedError.description: For the version DestroyTenantDataKey targets, the re-encryption job of the owning context (`data_key_reencryption` through Jobs) has not yet moved every reference onto the active version. Complete the re-encryption before destroying. A domain failure condition, not an HTTP response body.

Contract.DataKeyUnavailableError.description: The key operation cannot complete because the MasterKey provider is unreachable, a wrap or unwrap failed, or the AAD did not match (tampering). Callers must deny access fail-closed. A domain failure condition, not an HTTP response body: no operation returns it directly, and where it aborts a request the response is the generic 500 Problem Details.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.DefaultIdPProfileError.description: The tenant's default SAML IdP profile cannot be changed or deleted. Returned with HTTP 409 and `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:profile_in_use`, the same code the in-use rejection uses.

Contract.DelegationMode.description:
How the token's subject is currently acting. This derived value comes from the `act` chain and principal type and has no independent persistent state.
`OnBehalfOf` means another principal acts for the subject (`act` contains an actor different from the subject).
`Autonomous` means no delegation is present and the subject is a non-human principal (Agent or client).
`Direct` means no delegation is present and the subject is a human user.

Contract.Deliver.description: The lifecycle event where a LogoutNotification was delivered successfully.

Contract.Deny.description: The event where a device authorization was refused.

status.description: `healthy` when the dependency answered, `unavailable` when it did not.

message.description: Why the dependency is unavailable. Absent when it is healthy.

Contract.DependencyStatus.description: Reachability of one configured dependency, as the readiness probe reports it when `verbose` is set.

on_unassign.description: The unassign trigger coming from the Application.

on_delete.description: The user soft-delete or delete trigger. Choosing `delete` purges after `grace_period_days`.

on_group_deleted_or_unassigned.description: The group deletion or unassign trigger. A group has no equivalent of deactivate, so only `delete` and `none` are permitted.

accidental_deletion_count_threshold.description: When one sync would produce more deactivates and deletes than this, it is not run and the connection is quarantined instead.

Contract.DeprovisionPolicy.description:
How a deprovision trigger is translated into a downstream action. Disabling a user always maps to deactivate, and that is
not configurable; so is removing a group membership mapping to a PATCH that removes members. The defaults lean towards
the less destructive option.

user_code.description: A short code that avoids confusable characters.

Contract.DeviceAuthorization.description: The device authorization record of RFC 8628. The `device_code` is stored as a hash alone.

tenantId.description: The tenant the approval happened in.
The tenant the refusal happened in.

Contract.DeviceAuthorizationDenied.description: RFC 8628 section 3.3: the user refused, or kept entering the wrong `user_code`.

Contract.DeviceAuthorizationRequest.description: The `/device_authorization` request (RFC 8628 section 3.1), starting the flow from a device with constrained input.

tenantId.description: The tenant the device authorization was accepted in.

Contract.DeviceAuthorizationRequested.description: RFC 8628 section 3.1: a `device_code` and a `user_code` were issued. The `user_code` does not reach the audit log.

Contract.DeviceAuthorizationResponse.description: The `/device_authorization` response (RFC 8628 section 3.2). It returns the `device_code`, the `user_code`, and the `verification_uri`, and the device moves on to polling.

Contract.DeviceCodeState.description: The states the DeviceCodeFlow state machine (RFC 8628) may take. See the state machine section as well.

backchannel_authentication_endpoint.description: CIBA Core section 4: the backchannel authentication endpoint. It is advertised only when CIBA is offered.

backchannel_token_delivery_modes_support.description: CIBA Core section 4: the token delivery modes implemented. This implementation offers poll alone and advertises neither ping nor push.

backchannel_user_code_parameter_supporte.description: CIBA Core section 4: the `user_code` parameter is not supported. The approval screen is protected by the user's own authenticated session and a step-up, so it carries no second shared secret.

client_id_metadata_document_supported.description: Advertises that a client_id may also be resolved on each request as an HTTPS URL, a Client ID Metadata Document.

authorization_details_types_supported.description: RFC 9396: the `authorization_details` types this tenant accepts, derived from its enabled AuthorizationDetailTypes.

Contract.DiscoveryDocument.description: The metadata of RFC 8414 and OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0.

jti.description: An identifier unique to each proof. It cannot be reused within the replay window.

htm.description: The HTTP method of the request it covers.

htu.description: The HTTP URI of the request it covers, without the query and the fragment.

iat.description: When the proof was issued. Anything outside the permitted clock skew is refused.

ath.description: The base64url of the SHA-256 of the access token being presented (RFC 9449 section 4.3). It is required when accessing a protected resource, and absent at the token endpoint, where there is no such token yet.

Contract.DpopProofClaims.description: The claims of a DPoP proof JWT (RFC 9449 section 4.2). `typ` is `dpop+jwt`, and the public key is presented in the `jwk` header.

Contract.DynamicGroupPreviewRequest.description: The input for a read-only preview of an unsaved CEL against at most 100 users.

Contract.DynamicGroupPreviewResult.description: Per User, whether the rule matched and how that differs from the current membership. It carries no attribute value.

Contract.DynamicGroupRule.description: The restricted CEL rule paired one-to-one with a dynamic Group. The expression returns a boolean, and an unknown attribute, a function outside the permitted set, and an oversized expression can none of them be saved.

Contract.DynamicGroupRuleDisabled.description: An administrator deactivated a rule and invalidated the old dynamic membership at once.

Contract.DynamicGroupRuleEnabled.description: An administrator activated a validated rule and scheduled a full re-evaluation.

Contract.DynamicGroupRuleRequest.description: The input creating or updating a CEL rule.

Contract.DynamicGroupRuleUpdated.description: An administrator updated the CEL rule of a dynamic group to a new version.

Contract.DynamicMembershipEvaluated.description: The full re-evaluation of a rule version finished. It carries no attribute value, only how many memberships changed.

Contract.DynamicMembershipEvaluation.description: The auditable result of a full re-evaluation of a rule version and the membership it changed.

Contract.DynamicMembershipEvaluationFail.description: A full re-evaluation of dynamic membership failed, and the rule version stayed fail-closed.

Contract.DynamicMembershipEvaluationStar.description: A worker started a full re-evaluation of dynamic membership.

Contract.DynamicMembershipEvaluationStat.description: The state of a full re-evaluation for one rule version.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

newEmailHash.description: The SHA-256 of the new email, as hex.

Contract.EmailChangeRequested.description:
An end user raised a change of their primary email and a confirmation link was sent to the new address
(self-service). The email itself does not change until ConfirmEmailChange.
`newEmailHash` is a SHA-256, so the plaintext never reaches the audit log.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

Contract.EmailChanged.description:
The one-time link sent to the new address was confirmed and the primary email was settled
(self-service). `email_verified` becomes true, and a `verify_email` required action, if there is one, is
cleared automatically.

toHash.description: The SHA-256 of the recipient email, as hex.

Contract.EmailSent.description:
A message was sent through the EmailSender port. The port is fail-open, so a send failure does not
propagate into the use case layer; whether this event exists is how a SIEM observes it.
`to` is recorded as a SHA-256 hash.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.EmailUnchangedError.description: The new email address given is the same as the current one. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:email_unchanged`.

key_version.description: The `TenantDataEncryptionKey.version` the secret was encrypted under. It is unique inside the tenant boundary of the owning record, so decryption selects the TenantDataEncryptionKey from the caller's tenant_id together with this version; there is no global key id lookup.

ciphertext.description: The opaque ciphertext the Tink AEAD primitive emits, nonce and tag included. The caller rebuilds the AAD from `(tenant, context, table, record id, field)` and passes it in.

Contract.EncryptedSecret.description: An envelope holding a reversible secret encrypted under an Active or Retiring TenantDataEncryptionKey. The owning context (the MFA seed of Authentication, for one) persists this and never the plaintext. The ciphertext is the opaque bytes the Tink AEAD primitive emits as they are; nonce and tag are Tink's own business and get no separate field here, because we never assemble a nonce ourselves.

Contract.EndSessionParameters.description:
The query or form parameters of RP-Initiated Logout v1. The `post_logout_redirect_uri` is validated
against the client_id. An `id_token_hint` is accepted only when this OP issued the ID token, and its signature,
`iss`, `aud` (refused when it contradicts the client_id), `sub`, and `sid` are all verified.
`exp` is not verified, because sending an ID token that has already expired by the time of the logout is what a
normal RP implementation does.

policy_id.description: The identifier of the route it covers: `token`, `authorize`, `par`, `device_authorization`, `password_reset`, `login`, and so on.

fail_mode.description: What happens when the shared counter store is unreachable. Fixed at `fail_closed`.

Contract.EndpointRateLimitPolicy.description: The fixed-window rate limit settings of one route. The operator tunes the threshold and the window through environment variables; this model fixes only the shape and embeds no concrete value in the specification.

Contract.EnterUserCode.description: The event where a device user code was entered.

tenantId.description: The tenant that was configured.

Contract.EntraFederationConfigured.description: A Microsoft Entra domain federation preset was configured and the matching WS-Fed RP trust was upserted.

domain.description: A DNS domain already verified in Entra.

issuer_uri.description: The IssuerUri registered in Entra. It matches the issuer of the tokens issued and the wtrealm of the RP.

source_anchor_attribute.description: The immutable user attribute the ImmutableID is built from: either the GUID string of objectGUID or a value already base64-encoded.

immutable_id_attribute.description: The synthetic attribute name the converted ImmutableID is stored under; `entra_immutable_id` by default.

Contract.EntraFederationProfile.description: The profile for Microsoft Entra domain federation. It bundles the IssuerUri, the sourceAnchor attribute, and the passive, active, and MEX endpoints, and applies the claim preset for UPN, ImmutableID, and a persistent NameID to the WS-Fed RP.

Contract.Exchange.description: The event where a device code was exchanged for tokens.

Contract.ExecutionLane.description:
The partition that isolates execution slots for Jobs. The registration of a JobKind fixes its lane, and the caller
that enqueues cannot choose. `latency_sensitive` guarantees low-latency delivery its own slots, isolated from a bulk
backlog. `bulk` is for long-running, high-volume jobs, and `default` for everything that is neither.

Contract.Exhaust.description: The lifecycle event where a LogoutNotification reached `max_attempts` and settled as a dead letter.

Contract.Expire.description: The lifecycle event standing for reaching the expiry.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.ExpiredTokenError.description: In the Device Authorization Grant, the `device_code` has passed its expiry (RFC 8628 section 3.5, expired_token).

Contract.ExternalIdentityClaimsPreview.description: The normalized result an administrator reads to check a mapping. No token, assertion, or secret is returned.

Contract.ExternalIdentityProviderSummary.description: An active upstream provider, in the form fit to expose to the sign-in UI. It carries no secret, no internal endpoint, and no certificate.

Contract.FapiProfile.description: Published-language stub for the FAPI security profile owned by the OAuth2 context. Wire values are IdMagic-defined (backend/oauth2/client/domain/client.go).

provider.description: The external IdP identifier, `google`, `github`, or `saml:acme` for instance.

Contract.FederatedAuthenticated.description: A federated sign-in through an external IdP succeeded.

Contract.FederatedIdentity.description: The link correlating an immutable external subject with a local User. One tenant, provider, and subject map to at most one local user, and one local user and provider to at most one subject.

Contract.FederatedIdentityLinked.description: A link between a verified external subject and a local User was created. It carries no external token or assertion and no PII claim.

Contract.FederatedIdentityUnlinked.description: A ResourceOwner who had stepped up unlinked an external identity.

Contract.FederatedLoginAttempt.description: The single-use ephemeral record correlating an upstream browser round trip. It binds the state, nonce, and PKCE verifier, or the RelayState and AuthnRequest ID, to a tenant and a provider, and is consumed once within ten minutes.

Contract.FederatedLoginCompletion.description: The result of correlating a verified external identity with a local User and a LoginSession.

Contract.FederatedLoginRejected.description: The trust, correlation, or policy check of an upstream callback refused it fail-closed. It carries no token, assertion, state, or nonce.

Contract.FederatedLoginStartResponse.description: The validated redirect that starts upstream authentication.

Contract.FederationLinked.description: An external IdP identity was linked to a local user (account linking).

Contract.FederationUnlinked.description: An external IdP identity was unlinked from a local user.

type.description: A subject type the authorization model declares (`agent`, `user`, and so on). Checks and validity resolution use the same vocabulary.

Contract.FgaActor.description: One step of the principals acting on behalf of the subject at check time. The RFC 8693 `act` chain, ordered outermost first.

relationPath.description: A summary of the path followed, relation names only.

reasons.description: The rules that denied it. Empty when `permitted` is true.

actorChainDepth.description: How many steps the delegation chain had. Zero means direct access.

Contract.FgaCheckEvaluated.description: CheckAccess reached a decision. The resource identifier is reduced to the first 16 hex digits of its SHA-256, and neither the subject identifier nor the tuple contents are kept.

minimum_consistency.description: The smallest consistency token this check needs. Pass the value WriteRelationTuples returned.

granted_scopes.description: The scopes the caller's access token carries. The check refuses fail-closed when they do not cover what the operation requires.

Contract.FgaCheckRequest.description: The input to CheckAccess. `subject` is the principal being acted for -- usually the `sub` of the access token -- and `actor_chain` is the sequence of agents acting on its behalf. Giving `minimum_consistency` makes the check confirm the store's write revision has reached at least that point before deciding.

model_version.description: The revision of the authorization model the check used.

consistency.description: The store's consistency token at the moment of the check.

Contract.FgaCheckResult.description: The result of CheckAccess. When `permitted` is false, `reasons` names the rules that denied it. `relation_path` summarizes only the relation names that were followed; it carries no object or subject identifier.

Contract.FgaListAccessibleResourcesResul.description: The result of ListAccessibleResources. Reaching the scan ceiling sets `truncated`, and the caller must not treat the list as complete.

truncated.description: Whether the scan hit its ceiling and was cut short.

Contract.FgaResourcesEnumerated.description: ListAccessibleResources finished its scan. The per-candidate decisions are not expanded into the audit trail; this single event keeps only the counts and whether the scan was cut short. No resource identifier is kept.

iframe_uri.description: The registered `frontchannel_logout_uri`, with `iss` and `sid` added when `frontchannel_logout_session_required` is set.

Contract.FrontChannelLogoutTarget.description: One entry of a FrontChannelLogout result, corresponding to a single iframe the EndSession response embeds.

Contract.FullResyncCompleted.description: Every subject inside the scope StartFullResync targeted has converged.

Contract.GrantConsent.description: The event where the resource owner consented.

Contract.GrantType.description: Published-language stub for the grant types owned by the OAuth2 context. Wire values are the `grant_type` values registered by RFC 6749 section 4, RFC 8628 section 3.4 (device code), RFC 8693 section 2.1 (token exchange), and OpenID Connect CIBA Core section 4.

email.description: The contact email address of the group. Unlike `User.email` it has no authentication or verification flow.

attributes.description: The custom attributes, validated against the tenant's TenantGroupAttributeSchema.

Contract.Group.description: The tenant-scoped role bundle aggregate. It grants its `roles` to every member User at once. `id` is an immutable generated identifier and `name` an editable label unique within the tenant. `email` is a contact address and is never used to authenticate, and `attributes` is a sparse bag of custom attributes validated against the tenant's TenantGroupAttributeSchema.

Contract.GroupAddMemberRequest.description: The optional request body naming `group_id` when a membership is created from a screen such as the user detail view.

Contract.GroupAttributeDef.description: The definition of one custom attribute of a Group. Unlike the UserAttributeDef of User, Group has no built-in OIDC or SCIM catalogue, no self-service editor, and no claim exposure, so this is the reduced form carrying only the type and whether it is required.

Contract.GroupCreateRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator creates a group.

tenantId.description: The tenant the group belongs to.
The tenant the group belongs to.

Contract.GroupDeleted.description: An administrator deleted a group. The memberships were released by cascade, each with its own GroupMemberRemoved.

Contract.GroupListResponse.description: The group list of the administration API.

Contract.GroupMember.description: The membership relation between a User and a Group. It is unique on `group_id` and `user_id`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the group belongs to.

Contract.GroupMemberAdded.description: An administrator made a User a member of a group. It is not emitted when they were already a member, so the operation is idempotent.

tenantId.description: The tenant the group belongs to.

Contract.GroupMemberRemoved.description: An administrator removed a User from a group, or the membership was released by the group's deletion. It is not emitted when they were not a member, so the operation is idempotent.

Contract.GroupMemberResponse.description: How a group member is represented.

Contract.GroupMembershipPushed.description: A group membership change reached the downstream as a PATCH on members and the delivery settled as succeeded.

Contract.GroupMembershipSource.description: The one path that created a GroupMember.

Contract.GroupMembershipType.description: How a Group's membership is managed. It cannot be changed after creation.

Contract.GroupNameRequiredError.description: The `name` of a Group is empty. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:group_name_required`.

explicit_group_ids.description: The explicit list of `Group.id` values used when `selection` is `explicit`.

display_name_source.description: The IdMagic Group attribute key projected onto the downstream `displayName`.

Contract.GroupPushConfig.description: How the target groups are chosen while `push_groups` is on, and where their display names come from.

Contract.GroupPushed.description: A group create, update, deactivate, or delete reached the downstream and the delivery settled as succeeded.

Contract.GroupSummaryResponse.description: How a group is represented. The list and the detail views of the administration UI return the same representation.

Contract.GroupUpdateRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator updates a group's name, description, email, attributes, or roles. A field left out keeps its current value.

tenantId.description: The tenant the group belongs to.

Contract.GroupUpdated.description: An administrator updated a group's name, description, or roles.

sid.description:
The OIDC session id (OpenID Connect Front-Channel and Back-Channel Logout 1.0). It is present only for an
issuance bound to a browser session. The RP sends it back to `/end_session` as the `id_token_hint`, and it correlates
front-channel and back-channel logout.

additional_claims.description:
The additional claims formed by merging the scope-driven attribute claims (ClaimsForScopes) with the per-client
ClaimMapping claim policy. When a key collides with a standard claim, the standard claim
wins.

Contract.IdTokenClaims.description: The claims of an OpenID Connect ID token. TTL 3600 seconds.

secret_reference.description: The write-only field carrying the client secret itself. Only the ciphertext, envelope-encrypted under the per-tenant DEK of DataKeys, is stored in the database, and neither the value nor the ciphertext appears in an API response. The field name is carried over from the `env:` reference scheme it replaced.

client_secret_configured.description: A read-only derived field saying whether `secret_reference` is set. It is never used for a write carrying a value or a ciphertext; the detail view of the administration console uses it to show nothing more than set or unset.

Contract.IdentityProviderConnection.description: The tenant-scoped upstream trust settings. No URL supplied during a request is ever fetched; only the last-known-good endpoints, keys, and certificates from metadata validated at configuration time are used. The client secret arrives write-only as a `secret_reference` and is held envelope-encrypted under the per-tenant DEK of DataKeys.

Contract.IdentityProviderConnectionActiv.description: A connection that passed metadata and trust validation became usable for login routing.

Contract.IdentityProviderConnectionCreat.description: A tenant administrator created an upstream connection as a draft. It carries no secret, token, or certificate body.

Contract.IdentityProviderConnectionDisab.description: A connection was taken out of login routing.

display_name.description: The name shown to the user on the sign-in screen.

issuer.description: For OIDC, the issuer; validated at configuration time.

client_id.description: For OIDC, the client id registered upstream.

secret_reference.description: The client secret itself, write-only. Only its ciphertext is stored, and no response ever carries it back.

jit_provisioning.description: Whether a local User is provisioned just in time when no link exists.

allowed_email_domains.description: The email domains permitted to route to this connection. Empty means no restriction.

Contract.IdentityProviderConnectionReque.description: The JSON request creating or updating an upstream connection. It carries only what the caller may set; the id, the tenant, the status, the timestamps, and `client_secret_configured` all stay with the server, and a new connection starts Disabled.

Contract.IdentityProviderConnectionStatu.description: The lifecycle state of a connection. Only an Active connection may be used for discovery and login routing. A newly created one starts Disabled.

Contract.IdentityProviderConnectionTestR.description: The structured result of a connection test. It checks that OIDC discovery and JWKS are reachable, that the SAML certificate parses, and that `secret_reference` resolves, meaning it decrypts. It carries none of the values themselves: no secret, no token, no certificate body.

Contract.IdentityProviderProtocol.description: The wire protocol of an upstream connection. A social provider preset appears as the initial settings of `oidc`.

Contract.InsufficientScopeError.description: The scope of the presented token does not cover the requested operation (RFC 6750 section 3.1, insufficient_scope).

Contract.IntrospectionRequest.description: The `/introspect` request (RFC 7662 section 2.1), by which a resource server asks the authorization server whether a token is valid.

act.description: The `act` claim of RFC 8693 section 4.1. For a delegated token it returns the current actor and the actor chain.

delegation_mode.description:
Whether an active token represents autonomous, on-behalf-of, or direct execution.
The authorization server returns the derived value so resource servers do not reimplement the `act` and principal-type rules.
The value is produced by the same derivation function used for audit events.

Contract.IntrospectionResponse.description: The `/introspect` response (RFC 7662 section 2.2). It returns whether the token is active and, when it is, its metadata.
