Contract.IssueApplicationClientSecretReq.description: The request that issues an additional secret with an expiry on an Application's OIDC protocol, leaving existing credentials alone. `expires_in_days` is 90 when left out, and only 1 to 730 days is accepted.

Contract.IssueApplicationClientSecretRes.description: Returns the additionally issued secret once. It carries no hash, no existing secret, and no way to read the plaintext again.

Contract.IssueClientSecretRequest.description: The request that issues an additional client secret with an expiry, leaving existing credentials alone. `expires_in_days` is 90 when left out, and only 1 to 730 days is accepted.

Contract.IssueClientSecretResponse.description: The response returning the additionally issued secret, once. It carries no existing secret, no hash, and no way to read the plaintext again.

Contract.IssueCode.description: The lifecycle event issuing an authorization code.

values.description: The claim values; a multi-valued attribute yields several.

Contract.IssuedClaim.description: The output of the claim issuance engine: one claim type and its values.

Contract.JWK.description: A JSON Web Key (RFC 7517): one public key, identified by its kid.

Contract.JWKS.description: A JWK Set (RFC 7517 section 5), the public keys the /jwks endpoint returns. A client fetches it to verify token signatures.

tenant_id.description: The tenant boundary the Job belongs to. A worker causes side effects only inside it.

kind.description: The job kind, which decides the handler that runs.

lane.description:
The execution lane, fixed at enqueue time by the registration of the kind.
The caller cannot choose it, and it is immutable once the Job exists. A claim only looks at Jobs on its own lane.

params.description: The input handed to the handler at enqueue time. Callers keep raw PII out of it as far as they can.

result.description: The output the handler leaves behind when it succeeds.

error.description: The most recent failure. On reaching Failed (dead-letter) it holds the final error.

attempts.description: How many times execution has been attempted so far.

max_attempts.description: Failing more times than this settles the Job as a dead letter (Failed).

dedup_key.description: Unique on `(tenant_id, dedup_key)`. The idempotency key that keeps the same side effect from being enqueued twice; it is the main reason a handler's side effect is observed only once even under at-least-once delivery.

progress.description: Progress the handler may report while Running.

lease_owner.description: Identifies the worker currently holding Running. Unset in a terminal state and while Queued.

lease_expires_at.description: When the lease expires. A heartbeat extends it; once it lapses another worker may claim the Job again.

run_at.description: The Job becomes claimable at this instant: now, right after enqueue, and pushed out by the backoff on a retry.

Contract.Job.description:
One unit of enqueued asynchronous work. A worker takes a lease and moves it to Running, and the handler causes side
effects only inside the boundary where `handler_context.tenant_id == job.tenant_id`.
Records are kept for 30 days (`delete_after`).

Contract.JobCanceled.description: The Job was cancelled before reaching a terminal state.

Contract.JobEnqueued.description: A Job was put on the queue.

Contract.JobFailed.description: The handler failed. `terminal` being true means `max_attempts` was passed and the Job is settled as a dead letter.

Contract.JobKind.description:
The allow list of job kinds registered in the worker's handler registry. A consumer feature that adds a new job kind
adds its kind to this enum, and declares its ExecutionLane at the same time, before writing the implementation
(specification first). The core runtime contributes only `noop_echo`, for connectivity checks.
`backchannel_logout_delivery` is declared ahead of the feature that will use it, and `data_key_reencryption` is added
by DataKeys for the re-encryption job of envelope encryption.

Contract.JobLeaseLostError.description: By the time the worker sent a heartbeat, a completion report, or a failure report, its lease had already expired or been taken by another worker. The calling worker should abort the handler. A worker-facing domain condition, not an HTTP response body.

Contract.JobProgress.description: A progress snapshot the handler may report while Running.

Contract.JobRef.description:
The published language another bounded context holds when it has enqueued a Job or wants to refer to one. It carries
the smallest reference fit to publish, not the whole Job aggregate.

Contract.JobRetried.description: After a failure and its backoff, the Job returned to Queued for another attempt.

Contract.JobStarted.description: A worker claimed a Job and moved it to Running.

Contract.KeyProvider.description:
Where the key material is kept and who performs the signature. Local and Database keep the private key inside the process
and are for development and test; VaultTransit delegates the private key to Vault and is for production. Database names no
particular product.

Contract.KeyUsage.description:
What the key is for. Signing covers JWT signatures for OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect; XmlFederationSigning covers XML
signatures for SAML 2.0, WS-Federation, and WS-Trust, and the X.509 metadata published with them. Even inside one tenant,
each use has its own active key.

device_hash.description: `SaltedHash(tenant salt, User-Agent)`, as hex. It does not correlate across tenants.

label.description: A display label derived from the User-Agent, naming nothing beyond the browser and OS family, `Chrome / macOS` for instance.

Contract.KnownSignInDevice.description:
One browser the user has signed in from before. It serves both to decide `new_device_sign_in` and to
deduplicate it. Every sign-in upserts on `(user_id, device_hash)`, and only when a row is newly created is the sign-in
notified as coming from a new device. `device_hash` is the SHA-256 of the User-Agent, as hex, salted with the tenant's
correlation salt; neither the raw User-Agent nor the IP is stored.

Contract.LifecycleNotificationDelivery.description: The delivery idempotency key of a `send_email` action. It records that exactly one message was sent for a given `(run_id, step_index)`.

tenant_id.description: The tenant it belongs to. Cross-tenant references are forbidden.

name.description: The display name, unique within the tenant.

current_revision.description: The number of the most recently created revision.

enabled_revision.description: The revision the trigger currently evaluates. It may be unset while the workflow is draft, disabled, or archived.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflow.description:
The workflow definition aggregate, whose `name` is unique within the tenant. Creating one makes revision 1 as a draft.
Only an enabled revision is evaluated by the trigger, and an update that changes the meaning raises `current_revision`
while leaving `status` and `enabled_revision` alone. An administrator may delete it whatever its state, and a deleted
definition is excluded from listing, reading, and the name uniqueness check. Existing runs and audit events are kept
independently of the definition.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowCreateRequest.description: The request to create a workflow. Creating one makes revision 1 as a draft.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowCreated.description: An administrator created a LifecycleWorkflow, as revision 1 in draft.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowDeleted.description: An administrator deleted a LifecycleWorkflow. It is emitted whatever the state was beforehand, and kept as an audit trail.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowDisabled.description: An administrator disabled a LifecycleWorkflow. No new run is triggered, and a queued run that has not started is canceled.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowDryRunRequest.description: The input naming the user a dry run targets. The revision used is `enabled_revision`, or `current_revision` when none is named.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowDryRunResponse.description:
The result of a dry run. Nothing is created or changed: no WorkflowRun, Job, membership, assignment, required action,
status, or email. It carries `evaluated_at` and the revision, and is not presented as a guarantee about the real run.

would_change.description: One of would_change, no_op, or blocked.

reason.description:
Why it is blocked: resource_not_found, dependency_unavailable, notification_unavailable, trigger_not_matched, and the
like. Left out for would_change and no_op.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowDryRunStepResu.description:
The verdict for one action of a dry run. It reads the target User's current state -- group memberships, application
assignments, required actions, status, and email verification state -- and returns the same verdict the real action
executor would reach (would_change, no_op, or blocked), without any side effect. It carries no attribute value and no
email address.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowEnabled.description: An administrator got `current_revision` through validation and enabled it as `enabled_revision`.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowResponse.description: How a workflow definition is represented, including the contents of `current_revision`.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowRevision.description:
The immutable snapshot of a LifecycleWorkflow definition. Every update that changes its meaning raises the revision by one,
and past revisions stay immutable. Only the enabled revision creates new WorkflowRuns.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowRunCanceled.description: A disable stopped a queued run that had not started, or stopped a running one after the checkpoint of its current step.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowRunFailed.description: A WorkflowRun reached its attempt ceiling and ended without a single successful step.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowRunPartiallyFa.description: A WorkflowRun reached its attempt ceiling and ended with successes and failures mixed.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowRunStarted.description: The dispatcher handed a WorkflowRun to a worker and the first step began.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowRunSucceeded.description: Every step of a WorkflowRun ended as changed or no_op.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowStatus.description: The lifecycle of a LifecycleWorkflow. `archived` is an implementation state that keeps a deleted definition internally so the run history stays referentially intact; it is exposed neither in the administration console nor in the ordinary API.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowStepFailed.description: One WorkflowStep settled with a failed outcome. The workflow_id, run_id, step_id, and error_code are kept so an audit search can find it.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowUpdateRequest.description:
The request to update a workflow. When `expected_revision` does not match the current `current_revision` it is refused
with WorkflowRevisionConflictError, so a lost update cannot happen.

Contract.LifecycleWorkflowUpdated.description: An administrator updated a LifecycleWorkflow. When the trigger or the actions changed and the revision rose, `newRevision` is included.

Contract.LoginPendingPurpose.description: Why a LoginSession is not yet complete. `none` is an ordinary authenticated session, `challenge` is waiting on verification of an enrolled factor, and `enrollment` is waiting on the administrator-approved enrollment of a new one.

auth_time.description: The Unix second at which authentication succeeded. It is immutable as the session's start time, and the list is sorted by it, newest first.

amr.description: The RFC 8176 methods by which authentication succeeded (RFC8176-AMR-VOCABULARY).

acr.description: The authentication context class reference URN: either `urn:idmagic:acr:pwd`, when amr holds nothing beyond `pwd`, or `urn:idmagic:acr:mfa`, when amr holds one of otp, webauthn, hwk, swk, or rc (OpenID Connect Core section 2 and RFC 8176).

authentication_pending.description: Whether it is the intermediate state waiting on verification of another factor. False once complete.

pending_purpose.description: What `authentication_pending` is for. While it is `enrollment`, the session reaches no account, administration, or application resource, and only the enrollment API is permitted.

enrollment_deadline.description: The deadline for completing a `pending_purpose=enrollment`. Settling an enrollment after it is refused, and the session is not promoted to authenticated.

enrollment_bypass_id.description: The administrator-issued bypass consumed to move into Enrollment. Kept for audit correlation.

step_up_at.description: The Unix second at which a step-up reauthentication by password or MFA last succeeded; 0 when none has. It decides recency for high-sensitivity self-service operations.

last_seen_at.description: When the session was last used, in the sense of standing as an authentication result. It is touched on every authentication resolution, but a re-touch within LoginSessionTouchInterval of the last one is not persisted, so the value is coarse-grained and the idle timeout is approximated at that granularity.

revoked_at.description: When it was revoked; null while it is not. Revocation is a tombstone and never deletes the row.

revoke_reason.description: The revocation reason, set together with `revoked_at`. Null while `revoked_at` is null.

Contract.LoginSession.description:
The browser login session. PostgreSQL is its single source of truth, so a session stays valid across a
process restart. The cookie carries nothing but an opaque session id, while the `sub` and `auth_time` live in the
server-side store. The amr and acr stay here too and decide step-up at a later `/authorize`.
`authentication_pending=true` is an intermediate state the same LoginSession moves into only when the sign-in policy
or a step-up demands another factor; the mere fact that an MFA factor is enrolled does not make it pending. Moving
into a wait for another factor must never leave a separate, completed `pwd` session behind. The `/authorize`
completion path treats a pending session as unauthenticated and directs it to the matching factor challenge.
The cookie is issued `http_only` with `same_site=Lax`. The `tenant_id` is always part of the authentication
resolution query, so even if a session id were guessed or replayed across tenants the database layer would not return
a row of another tenant -- the isolation is fail-closed. Revocation sets `revoked_at` and `revoke_reason` as a
tombstone and never deletes the row, so revoking again succeeds idempotently. Authentication resolution treats only
rows with `revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now` as valid.

tenantId.description: The tenant the throttling happened in, taken from the request path.

keyHash.description: The SHA-256 of the username in lowercase, or of the IP, as hex.

Contract.LoginThrottled.description:
A sign-in attempt reached a throttling threshold -- per account (10 attempts in a 900-second window, 900-second
lockout) or per IP (30 attempts in a 900-second window, 900-second lockout) -- and was locked out.
It is an input event for credential stuffing and brute-force detection in a SIEM. `keyHash` is the SHA-256 of the
username in lowercase, or of the IP, so no plaintext reaches the audit log.

sid.description: The OIDC session id to notify about.

logout_token_jti.description: The `jti` of the logout token issued. The RP uses it for replay detection and IdMagic for audit correlation.

target_uri.description: Where it is delivered, a snapshot of the client's `backchannel_logout_uri` taken when delivery began.

job_id.description: The `JobRef.id` of the Jobs context, correlating the delivery run.

Contract.LogoutNotification.description:
The record of one back-channel logout delivery attempt. The local session and refresh token revocation is
already settled before this record is created, and a failed delivery does not undo it.
The delivery itself is delegated to a durable job of the Jobs bounded context
(`kind=backchannel_logout_delivery`).

Contract.LogoutNotificationState.description: The delivery state of a LogoutNotification. It does not map one-to-one onto the JobStatus of Jobs; it states only whether the delivery itself succeeded, while the job's own retries and lease stay with Jobs.

Contract.MatchingRule.description: The attributes compared to adopt an existing downstream resource on a 409 conflict. Correlation by `externalId` -- the IdMagic id -- is the primary route; this rule is the secondary one, for resolving a conflict with an existing resource that has no `externalId` set.

id.description: The unique identifier of the registration (a UUID), globally unique across tenants.

resource.description: The canonical resource URI strictly bound to the `aud` of the tokens issued. Unique within the tenant.

name.description: The display name in the administration UI.

scopes.description: The allow list of scopes permitted when accessing this resource. The scopes requested alongside a `resource` have to be a subset of it.

Contract.McpResourceServer.description: The tenant-scoped registration of an MCP resource server, a tool or a data source. It owns the canonical resource URI and the permitted scopes, and is the yardstick for Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) and for the resource indicator check (RFC 8707). Management is guarded by AdminMcpResourcesManage.

Contract.McpResourceServerListResponse.description: The McpResourceServer list of the administration API.

resource.description: Required at creation, and immutable on update, because changing it would change what the `aud` of already-issued tokens means.

Contract.McpResourceServerRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator registers or updates an McpResourceServer. `resource` is settable at creation only.

Contract.McpResourceServerResponse.description: How an McpResourceServer is represented. The list and the detail views of the administration UI return the same representation.

Contract.McpResourceServerState.description: The operational states of an McpResourceServer. Only `active` passes the resource indicator check; `disabled` refuses new issuance, and tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.

Contract.MfaChallengeFailed.description: An MFA challenge failed. It is also an input to the bucket aggregation with `kind=mfa_failed`.

Contract.MfaChallengeIssued.description: An MFA challenge was presented: TOTP, WebAuthn, or another.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentBypass.description: The short-lived, single-use enrollment approval an administrator issues to a user with no MFA enrolled. It is a trust anchor consumed after a successful password step so the session can move into enrollment pending; it does not exempt anyone from the MFA requirement of signing in. One that has expired, been revoked, or been consumed cannot be used, fail-closed.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentBypassConsumed.description: A target user who had authenticated with a password consumed their enrollment bypass, once, and entered the enrollment-only pending flow.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentBypassExpired.description: An unconsumed enrollment bypass was found to be past its deadline and unusable. It is emitted the first time the expiry is observed.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentBypassIssueRequest.description: The input with which an administrator issues a single-use enrollment bypass to a target user.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentBypassIssued.description: An administrator issued a short-lived, single-use enrollment bypass to a user with no MFA enrolled.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentBypassResponse.description: How an enrollment bypass is shown to an administrator. There is no secret: the server consumes it automatically when the target user's password step succeeds.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentBypassRevoked.description: An administrator revoked an unconsumed enrollment bypass.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentCompleted.description: Inside the login enrollment flow, a factor was enrolled and proof of possession completed, and the same LoginSession was promoted to MFA-satisfied.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentNotAllowedError.description: The target user does not meet the conditions for an MFA enrollment bypass. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:mfa_enrollment_not_allowed`.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentPolicy.description: Governs the pre-enrollment period before MFA becomes mandatory, and the administrator-approved onboarding after enforcement starts. Before `enforcement_start_at` an ordinary sign-in is allowed, which nudges the user to enroll through self-service; after it, an unenrolled user does not complete sign-in, and only when `allow_admin_bypass` is true and a valid single-use enrollment bypass exists do they proceed into the enrollment-only flow. `grace_period_seconds` is how long a bypass may be used after enforcement starts, not a period of free enrollment.

Contract.MfaEnrollmentRequired.description: Under a policy that requires MFA, an unenrolled user consumed a valid administrator approval and entered the enrollment-only pending flow. Password authentication alone does not establish an ordinary session.

secret.description: For `totp`, the base32 secret. It is left open so another factor can put its credential JSON in a field of its own. When persisted it is envelope-encrypted under the per-tenant DEK of DataKeys; the plaintext is never stored.

label.description: The display name the user gives it, `iPhone Authenticator` for instance.

Contract.MfaFactor.description: One second factor (MFA) a user has enrolled. For `totp` the secret is stored as base32 and evaluated at authentication under RFC 6238 (T0=0, STEP=30s, `digits` digits, a window of plus or minus one step). The algorithm is SHA1 and the secret is generated at 20 bytes. `User.mfa_enrolled` being true means exactly that this set is non-empty.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

Contract.MfaFactorEnrolled.description:
A user enrolled an MFA factor through self-service; today, TOTP. The secret never reaches
the audit trail -- only the kind does. It sets `User.mfa_enrolled` to true.

Contract.MfaFactorRemoveRequest.description:
The MFA factor removal request (self-service). The code is the current TOTP code, as proof of
possession. Removal requires the user themselves plus that proof.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

Contract.MfaFactorRemoved.description:
A user removed an MFA factor through self-service. Removal is accompanied by proof of
possession through a valid TOTP code. It returns `User.mfa_enrolled` to false.

Contract.MfaFactorType.description: The kinds of second factor (MFA), a subset of the RFC 8176 amr values chosen for this application. `totp` is RFC 6238, `webauthn` is WebAuthn Level 3, and `hwk` and `swk` are reserved for later.

category_ids.description: The ids of the categories it carries. The portal sorts its tiles into sections by these.

Contract.MyApplication.description: One assigned application shown on the user portal.

Contract.MyApplicationListResponse.description:
The list of assigned applications for the user portal. A manual order takes precedence when one is saved, and name ascending is used otherwise.
`categories` carries the tenant's category definitions by position ascending, and the portal uses them as section headings.

Contract.MyApplicationOrderResponse.description: The manual portal order a user has saved. With nothing saved, `application_ids` is empty.

format.description: The NameID format URI, such as `urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent`.

source_attribute.description: The identity attribute that supplies the NameID value.

Contract.NameIdConfiguration.description: The format of the NameID (the subject identifier) of an issued assertion, and where its value comes from.

user_id.description: The `sub` of the owning user. There is no `tenant_id`, because `users.id` is globally unique.

disabled_categories.description: The kinds the user has stopped receiving. A mandatory kind cannot be listed.

Contract.NotificationPreference.description:
The user's own security notification preferences. Having no row means exactly the same as everything
being on, so no row is created until the first change. Only optional kinds may be listed in `disabled_categories`, and
an update naming a mandatory kind is refused. The first thing an attacker silences after a takeover is the
notifications, and being able to silence them is no different from their not existing.

locale.description: The locale this override applies to. Only a locale the catalogue ships translations for is accepted.

subject.description: The mail subject. It is treated as a single line and may hold no newline.

body_text.description: The plain text body. It is never interpreted as HTML.

body_html.description: The HTML body. It is a fragment that goes inside `<body>`; the doctype, the `<head>`, the character encoding, and the styling of the body container all come from the system-supplied outer frame. Substituted values are always escaped before expansion. It is always saved together with the text body, and an override of only one of the two cannot be made.

from_display_name.description: The sender display name. An empty string means unset, and the system default sender display is used. The email address itself is a server setting and cannot be overridden.

Contract.NotificationTemplate.description: One notification template override by a tenant, unique on `(tenant_id, template_key, locale)`. A combination with no row uses the built-in default (BuiltinNotificationTemplate). Only the subject, the plain text body, the HTML body, and the sender display name can be overridden; replacing the whole HTML document or the CSS is not accepted. The substitution variables a body may use are confined to the permitted set of its template_key.

placeholders.description: The permitted set of substitution variable names for this template_key.

Contract.NotificationTemplateDetail.description: How one template is represented for editing. It returns the wording currently in force, the built-in default wording, and the permitted set of substitution variables together, so the administration UI can show the difference from the default and offer "restore the default" without another request.

Contract.NotificationTemplateKey.description: The fixed identifier naming what a notification is for. The catalogue holds a built-in default template in Japanese and English for every one of these keys, and a tenant cannot add a key. AccountSecurityAlert covers every kind of security notification under one key, and what happened is expressed through the `event_description` and `device_summary` substitutions.

Contract.NotificationTemplateListRespons.description: The template list. It returns every key of the catalogue against every supported locale, overridden or not.

Contract.NotificationTemplatePreviewRequ.description: The request rendering unsaved wording against sample values. A field left out uses the wording currently in force.

Contract.NotificationTemplatePreviewResp.description: The rendering with the sample values expanded. No mail is actually sent.

Contract.NotificationTemplateReset.description: A tenant administrator deleted a notification template override and returned to the built-in default.

customized.description: True when a tenant override exists; false when the built-in default is in force.

subject.description: The subject currently in force: the override if there is one, the built-in default otherwise.

updated_at.description: When the override was last updated, if there is one. Left out when only the built-in default is in force.

Contract.NotificationTemplateSummary.description: One row of the template list. For each key and locale pair it returns whether it has been overridden and the subject currently in force.

to.description: The address the message actually went to, the caller's own. It is returned so the UI can state plainly where it was sent.

Contract.NotificationTemplateTestSendRes.description: The result of a test send. The recipient is fixed to the acting administrator's own verified email address and cannot be named in the request.

Contract.NotificationTemplateUpdateReque.description: The request saving a template override. The four fields are replaced as a set -- this is not a partial update -- and the subject, the text body, and the HTML body are all required. A substitution variable outside the permitted set means nothing is saved and the request is refused.

Contract.NotificationTemplateUpdated.description: A tenant administrator saved a notification template override. The wording itself is not recorded; only the key and locale it applies to.

application_id.description: The Application it corresponds to. Ordinary CRUD leaves it alone; only the bulk creation and deletion of an Application manage the relationship.

redirect_uris.description: Required for a redirect-based grant (authorization_code). A machine-to-machine client using client_credentials alone has none (RFC 6749 section 3.1.2).

backchannel_logout_uri.description:
Where OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0 notifications go. When it is set, every session revocation POSTs a
signed logout token to this URI.

backchannel_logout_session_required.description: Whether the RP requires a `sid` claim in the logout token. When true, nothing is delivered for a target session without a `sid`, because an issuance with no browser session has no target to notify.

frontchannel_logout_uri.description:
Where OpenID Connect Front-Channel Logout 1.0 notifications go. The `/end_session` response carries an iframe
pointing at this URI.

frontchannel_logout_session_required.description: Whether to add the `iss` and `sid` query parameters to the iframe URI.

claim_policy.description:
The claim issuance policy for this client, the per-application release override.
The source attribute that plays the part of a NameID is used as the source of `sub`. Whether a ClaimExposed attribute
may be disclosed at all, decided by the scope and the consent through the standard scopes openid, profile, email, and
so on, is applied first and independently of this policy; this policy narrows and remaps within that range, and merges
into the ID token and UserInfo.

updated_at.description: It equals `created_at` at creation and is updated on every administrative operation on the client metadata afterwards.

Contract.OAuth2Client.description: A client under RFC 7591 with the FAPI 2.0 extensions. A client outside the catalogue, whose `application_id` is null, is allowed; when it is not null it names an `oidc` Application of the same tenant, and at most one client is bound to one Application.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.OAuthAccessDeniedError.description: The resource owner or the authorization server denied the request (RFC 6749 section 5.2, access_denied). The OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect endpoints report this condition with the OAuthError body; the generic APIs report the same condition as AccessDeniedError, an RFC 9457 Problem Details body.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.OAuthError.description: The shared OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect error response body (RFC 6749 section 5.2), written by `support_http.OAuthErrorBody` with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every endpoint whose error shape a standard fixes returns this body rather than RFC 9457 Problem Details, so that off-the-shelf clients can read it. The named `*Error` models declared as `is OAuthError` share this body and are told apart by the value of `error`.

Contract.OAuthErrorCode.description: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect protocol error codes, carried in the `error` member of an OAuthError body. Wire values are registered by RFC 6749 sections 4.1.2.1 and 5.2, RFC 6750 section 3.1 (invalid_token, insufficient_scope), RFC 8628 section 3.5 (authorization_pending, slow_down, expired_token), RFC 8707 section 2 (invalid_target), RFC 9449 section 7.1 (invalid_dpop_proof), RFC 7591 section 3.2.2 (invalid_client_metadata, invalid_redirect_uri), RFC 9126 section 2.2 (invalid_request_uri), RFC 9396 section 5 (invalid_authorization_details), OpenID Connect Core section 3.1.2.6 (login_required), and OpenID Connect CIBA Core section 13 (unknown_user_id, invalid_binding_message).

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.OAuthInvalidRequestError.description: The request is missing a required parameter, repeats one, or carries an invalid value (RFC 6749 section 5.2, invalid_request). The OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect endpoints report this condition with the OAuthError body; the generic APIs report the same condition as InvalidRequestError, an RFC 9457 Problem Details body.

Contract.PARRecord.description: The stored record of a Pushed Authorization Request. Its state follows PARRecordLifecycle.

Contract.PARRecordState.description: The states the PARRecordLifecycle state machine may take. From `stored` it becomes `used` when `/authorize` reads it, and `expired` when it runs out.

tenantId.description: The tenant the PAR was accepted in.

Contract.PARStored.description: The authorize parameters that arrived at `/par` were stored server-side and a short-lived `request_uri` was issued (RFC 9126).

Contract.ParRequest.description: It takes the authorize parameters as a form.

Contract.ParResponse.description: The `/par` response (RFC 9126 section 2.2). It issues a short-lived `request_uri` that a later `/authorize` refers to.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

Contract.PasswordChanged.description: A ResourceOwner changed their own password at `/api/auth/change_password`. It is the starting point of the change-password audit trail and of the notification.

min_length.description: The `min_length` of the PasswordPolicy of the Authentication context.

max_length.description: The `max_length` of the PasswordPolicy of the Authentication context.

history_depth.description: The `history_depth` of the PasswordPolicy of the Authentication context.

max_age_days.description:
The `max_age_days` of the PasswordPolicy of the Authentication context. Leaving it out means 0, no expiry, which
matches how an older client that does not know the field reads it.

Contract.PasswordPolicyDefaults.description:
The current values of the PasswordPolicy of the Authentication context. They are embedded in the API response so the
tenant settings UI can show the user, as concrete numbers, what actually applies when the tenant overrides nothing.
They are at the same time the threshold at which an override is rejected as weaker.

min_length.description: The minimum length; at or above the global default is recommended.

history_depth.description: How many past passwords are checked against (PasswordHistoryNoReuse).

max_age_days.description:
How many days a password stays valid. Zero, or leaving it out, disables expiry, which is the default in line with
NIST SP 800-63B-4. In a tenant that sets a positive value, a user whose password is past its expiry is directed into the
`update_password` required action after their next sign-in succeeds; the authentication itself does not fail.
The system ceiling is 30 to 3650 days, and a value outside that is refused with PolicyOverrideWeakerError.

Contract.PasswordPolicyOverride.description:
The per-tenant password policy overrides. It is the schema for replacing the standard PasswordPolicy values of the
Authentication context at the tenant resolution port. A field left out inherits the global default, and on the
evaluation paths of change_password, reset_password, and administrative user creation a tenant value may only move in
the stricter direction from the global one.

tenantId.description: The tenant the reset was requested in, taken from the request path.

emailHash.description: The SHA-256 of the submitted email, as hex.

Contract.PasswordResetRequested.description:
A password reset link was requested. To prevent enumeration it records only that
the request arrived; whether a link was actually issued -- that is, whether a user with a verified
email existed -- is observed separately through the EmailSent event.
`emailHash` is a SHA-256, so no plaintext reaches the audit log.

consumed_at.description: Non-null means it has been used and cannot be reused.

Contract.PasswordResetTokenRecord.description:
The single-use token for a password reset.
The token is 32 random bytes as base64url, and only its SHA-256 hash is stored.
It lives 1800 seconds (30 minutes) from issuance and is consumed once; once `consumed_at` is set it cannot be reused.
Expired and consumed rows are garbage-collected, and an INSERT also does a light sweep that invalidates any unconsumed
token of the same `sub`.

Contact points whose shape a standard fixes — OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), SCIM (RFC 7644), and the SharedSignals receive endpoint (RFC 8935) — return that standard's error body instead; see the HTTP error responses section of the root specification. authorization_servers.description: The authorization servers protecting this resource, that is, the IdMagic issuer.

Contract.ProtectedResourceMetadata.description: RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata. For the realm's IdMagic API it is derived from the ApiTokenScopes, and for an external resource from the McpResourceServer registration.

resource.description: The resource URI it was served for.

Contract.ProtectedResourceMetadataServed.description: RFC 9728: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` served the metadata of a registered McpResourceServer.

Contract.ProvisioningAuthMethod.description: How to authenticate to the downstream SCIM service provider.

Contract.ProvisioningCapabilities.description: The read-only capabilities the discovery of TestProvisioningConnection caches from the downstream /ServiceProviderConfig. They decide whether to fall back to PUT for a target that does not support PATCH.

base_url.description: The downstream SCIM v2 base URL. It must be https, and an internal or link-local IP and an arbitrary redirect are refused.

capabilities.description: Cached by the discovery of TestProvisioningConnection. Unset until that has run.

attribute_mappings.description: Seeded with the SCIM core User default mappings at registration.

notification_email.description: Where failures and quarantines are notified.

consecutive_failure_count.description: The internal counter that decides quarantine. A successful delivery resets it to zero.

Contract.ProvisioningConnection.description:
The outbound provisioning settings, of which at most one exists per Application. The source of truth is the User and Group
aggregates on the IdMagic side, and the downstream is a mirror. `scope` reuses the existing ApplicationAssignment rather
than carrying an assignment model of its own. Making `application_id` the identity expresses the one-connection-per-
Application constraint structurally.

Contract.ProvisioningConnectionDeleted.description: An administrator deleted a ProvisioningConnection. As with ApplicationStatus, the row itself is removed.

Contract.ProvisioningConnectionDisabled.description: An administrator set `ProvisioningConnection.status` to disabled. No new delivery is created.

Contract.ProvisioningConnectionQuarantin.description: An administrator lifted the quarantine through ResumeProvisioningConnection. The event was added because without a way out of quarantine there is no recovery.

Contract.ProvisioningConnectionRegistere.description: An administrator registered a new ProvisioningConnection on an Application.

Contract.ProvisioningConnectionStatus.description: The enabled state an administrator toggles. As with ApplicationStatus, deletion is not a state -- the row is removed, and the history stays in the ProvisioningConnectionDeleted event.

Contract.ProvisioningConnectionUpdated.description: An administrator updated the settings of a ProvisioningConnection, the credential aside.

Contract.ProvisioningCredentialInput.description: The write-only credential input RegisterProvisioningConnection and UpdateProvisioningConnection take. The value never appears in a response, an audit log, or an error.

Contract.ProvisioningCredentialRotated.description: An administrator updated the credential of a connection.

source_version.description: A monotonically rising counter the same-transaction capture emits. It is what resolves an out-of-order delivery.

job_id.description: The `Jobs.JobRef.id` the dispatcher attaches after enqueueing.

last_error.description: The sanitized error of the most recent failure. It carries no secret and no attribute value.

Contract.ProvisioningDelivery.description:
One delivery unit for one internal lifecycle event. The idempotency key
`(tenant_id, connection_id, source_type, source_id, source_version)` is a uniqueness constraint, and enqueueing the same
key again is a no-op on the existing row. The dispatcher attaches `job_id` after enqueueing to Jobs, and it is unset
until then.

Contract.ProvisioningDeliveryNotFoundErr.description: No ProvisioningDelivery exists with the `delivery_id` given, or it does not belong to the connection given. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:provisioning_not_found`.

Contract.ProvisioningDeliveryNotRetryabl.description: RetryProvisioningDelivery was called on a ProvisioningDelivery whose state is not `dead_letter`. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:provisioning_conflict`.

Contract.ProvisioningDeliveryStarted.description: The dispatcher attached a Jobs.Job to a ProvisioningDelivery and delivery began, the same shape as LifecycleWorkflowRunStarted.

Contract.ProvisioningDeliveryStatus.description:
The value set of `ProvisioningDelivery.status`. `in_flight` covers everything from the moment the dispatcher attaches a
Jobs.Job until a terminal state is reached, and it stays `in_flight` through attempt retries at the Jobs level -- as with
WorkflowRunLifecycle, a retry loop one layer down is not reflected in the state at this layer.
There is no non-terminal intermediate state called `failed`: `dead_letter` is a terminal state reached exactly once, when
the Job has used up `max_attempts`.

Contract.ProvisioningDeprovisionAction.description: How a deprovision trigger is translated for the downstream.

Contract.ProvisioningFeatureFlags.description: Toggles for the operations the connection may perform downstream, following Okta. `sync_password` is out of scope.

Contract.ProvisioningGroupSelection.description: How the target groups are chosen while `push_groups` is on.

Contract.ProvisioningHealth.description: How healthy the connection looks to the delivery engine. `quarantined` stops delivery until ResumeProvisioningConnection.

Contract.ProvisioningOperation.description: The operation a ProvisioningDelivery applies downstream.

Contract.ProvisioningScope.description: How the subjects to deliver are chosen. `assigned_only` reads the ApplicationAssignments; `all_users` is an advanced option covering every User of the tenant.

Contract.ProvisioningSourceType.description: Which internal aggregate a ProvisioningDelivery or RemoteResourceLink refers to.

Contract.ProvisioningSubjectNotInScopeEr.description: The subject ProvisionOnDemand names is outside the scope of the connection; under `assigned_only` that means the subject is not assigned. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:provisioning_conflict`.
