Contract.QuotaExceededError.description: The tenant has reached its resource creation ceiling (Quota). Published-language stub for the shared error the Tenancy context defines. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:quota_exceeded`, written by the shared error handler on every path, the Dynamic Client Registration endpoint included.

error.description: Always `rate_limited`.

retry_after_seconds.description: How many seconds to wait before retrying. Repeated in the `Retry-After` response header.

message.description: English fallback text for callers that do not localize by code. A UI that localizes maps `rate_limited` to its own message instead.

Contract.RateLimitedError.description: The threshold of an EndpointRateLimitPolicy was exceeded. This is the general endpoint rate limit, counted on every arriving request, and it is separate from the login throttle, which counts failures per account and per IP. Fail-closed: the request is rejected even when the shared counter store is unreachable. Written by `support_http.WriteRateLimited` with `Content-Type: application/json`, not as Problem Details, because the body carries `retry_after_seconds`. The response also carries a `Retry-After` header with the same number of seconds.

reflected_at.description: When the SET passed verification and was applied to the local revocation epoch.

Contract.ReceivedSecurityEvent.description: The record of an accepted inbound SET. `set_jti` is unique within the stream, so a replay is detected and refused.

code_hash.description: The SHA-256 of the recovery code plaintext, as hex. The plaintext is not stored.

Contract.RecoveryCode.description:
One backup recovery code, for when TOTP or WebAuthn is lost. The plaintext is shown once at
generation and only `code_hash` (SHA-256, as hex) is stored. A non-null `consumed_at` means it has been used and
cannot be reused. A user's valid codes are treated as one set and replaced outright on regeneration
(`regenerate_replaces_all`). Generation makes `count=10` codes, each `code_length=10` characters, drawn from the
alphabet 23456789abcdefghijkmnpqrstuvwxyz -- a base32-like alphabet with the confusable characters removed -- and they
are a backup alone, never a second factor on their own (NIST SP 800-63B section 5.1.2, Look-up Secrets).

Contract.RecoveryCodeStatus.description:
The state of the recovery codes shown on the self-service security screen. The codes themselves are not
returned: only when they were generated and how many there are in total and remaining.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

count.description: How many recovery codes were issued.

Contract.RecoveryCodesGenerated.description:
A user generated or regenerated backup recovery codes, having stepped up. Neither the plaintext nor a hash
reaches the audit trail -- only how many were issued. A regeneration replaces the existing set outright.

Contract.RecoveryCodesResponse.description:
What GenerateRecoveryCodes returns: the recovery codes in plaintext, once. Afterwards only the remaining
count (RecoveryCodeStatus) can be read; the codes are neither stored nor shown again.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

Contract.RecoveryCodesRevoked.description:
A user explicitly invalidated their backup recovery codes, having stepped up. No recovery code works as a
second factor afterwards.

Contract.RedeemCode.description: The lifecycle event redeeming an authorization code, once.

tenantId.description: The tenant the token was issued in.

Contract.RefreshTokenIssued.description: A refresh token was issued. The `familyId` identifies the family descended from the original authorization code and is inherited across rotations.

family_id.description: The identifier every token descended from one authorization code exchange shares.

absolute_expires_at.description: The absolute deadline, which a rotation does not extend.

sid.description:
The `sid` (OIDC session id) of the AuthorizationCodeRecord it came from. A rotation carries the parent's
value over unchanged. Null means an issuance with no browser session, client_credentials for instance.
Every family whose value matches the `sessionId` of Authentication's SessionEnded -- possibly spanning several
clients -- is resolved through this field, so a session revocation moves them all to RevokeToken at once.

resource.description:
The resource indicator it came from (`AuthorizationCodeRecord.resource`).
A rotation carries the parent's value over unchanged, so the audience stays strictly confined to the same
McpResourceServer afterwards. Null means an issuance with no `resource`.

Contract.RefreshTokenRecord.description: The store record of a refresh token. The plain value is never stored. Its state follows the RefreshTokenLifecycle state machine. The tenant is derived from the globally identified User and OAuth2Client rather than kept redundantly on the token row, and the use case checks the tenant-local invariant of both.

tenantId.description: The tenant the reuse was detected in.

Contract.RefreshTokenReuseDetected.description: A refresh token already in the `rotated` state was presented again. It triggers revocation of the whole family (RFC 9700 section 4.14).

tenantId.description: The tenant the rotation happened in.

Contract.RefreshTokenRotated.description: A refresh token was exchanged at `/token`: a new child token was issued and the parent moved to `rotated`.

Contract.RefreshTokenSenderConstraint.description: The sender constraint attached to a refresh token. It holds what it was bound to at issuance: the DPoP key thumbprint or the mTLS certificate thumbprint.

Contract.RefreshTokenState.description: The states the RefreshTokenLifecycle state machine may take. `rotated` has been consumed into a child token, `revoked` has been revoked, and `expired` has run out.

Contract.Reject.description: The event moving the lifecycle to its refusing terminal state.

name.description: The relation name, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` and unique within its ResourceTypeDefinition.

Contract.RelationDefinition.description: The definition of one relation a ResourceTypeDefinition exposes. A relation with no rewrites can never hold.

computed_relation.description: The relation name evaluated by `computed_userset` and `tuple_to_userset`. Not set for `direct`.

tupleset_relation.description: The relation `tuple_to_userset` follows to the parent object. Not set for the other kinds.

direct_subject_types.description: The subject shapes `direct` accepts: `user` for an individual subject, `group#member` for a subject set, and `user:*` for a wildcard. A RelationTuple whose shape is not listed here is refused both when written and when evaluated. Not set for the other kinds.

Contract.RelationRewrite.description: One rewrite rule making up a relation. A relation holds when the union of the rules on its RelationDefinition holds. Intersection and exclusion are not defined.

Contract.RelationRewriteKind.description: The kinds of rewrite rule an authorization model may use for a relation. `direct` reads a RelationTuple as it stands, `computed_userset` reads another relation on the same object, and `tuple_to_userset` reads a relation on the object reached through `tupleset_relation`.

resource_type.description: The resource type the relation is held on. A type name the authorization model declared.

resource_id.description: The resource identifier. IdMagic does not mint it; it holds the id from the caller's own resource space as it is.

subject_type.description: The subject type. A type name the authorization model declared.

subject_id.description: The subject identifier. `*` denotes a wildcard.

subject_relation.description: The relation name that makes this a subject set. Left out, the subject is an individual one.

Contract.RelationTuple.description: The relation fact `(resource_type:resource_id, relation, subject)`. The triple is unique within the tenant, so writing the same one again is idempotent. A subject carrying `subject_relation` denotes a subject set (`group:eng#member`). A `subject_id` of `*` is a wildcard, accepted only when a `direct` rule permits that `subject_type`.

Contract.RelationTupleDeleted.description: RelationTuples were deleted. A cascading per-object deletion is recorded through this event as well.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.RelationTupleInvalidError.description: A RelationTuple does not fit the registered authorization model: an unknown type or relation, a subject type that is not permitted, a wildcard that is not permitted, or the same tuple in both `writes` and `deletes`. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:relation_tuple_invalid`.

Contract.RelationTupleWriteRequest.description: The change WriteRelationTuples applies in one transaction. The same triple may not appear in both `writes` and `deletes`. An object listed in `delete_objects` has its RelationTuples removed on both the resource side and the subject side, so a deletion cascades.

Contract.RelationTupleWritten.description: RelationTuples were written. The individual tuples are not copied into the audit trail; only the count and the consistency token are kept.

source_id.description: The `User.id` or `Group.id` on the IdMagic side.

remote_id.description: The id of the downstream SCIM resource.

external_id.description: The `externalId` sent downstream; the IdMagic `source_id` by default.

last_synced_version.description: The `source_version` most recently applied. It is what resolves an out-of-order delivery.

Contract.RemoteResourceLink.description: The durable record correlating an IdMagic User or Group with a downstream resource. It is kept so that a 409 or a 404 can be resolved idempotently.

Contract.ReorderMyApplicationsRequest.description: A user saves their own manual portal order. `application_ids` may hold only apps assigned to them and visible.

Contract.RequestConsent.description: The event asking the resource owner for consent.

Contract.RequiredAction.description: The action forced on a user at their next sign-in. Published-language stub for IdManagement.RequiredAction, used only to name the action of a `set_required_action` or `clear_required_action`.

Contract.RequiredAuthnLevel.description: The authentication strength the sign-in policy demands. It maps the constrained choices, Password and Mfa, onto the internal acr and amr. When Mfa is not satisfied, the user is nudged to step up.

Contract.RequiredAuthnStrength.description: The authentication strength the sign-in policy demands. `Password` asks for nothing more (acr includes urn:idmagic:acr:pwd), and `Mfa` requires a second factor (acr equals urn:idmagic:acr:mfa, and amr holds one of otp, webauthn, hwk, or swk).

tenantId.description: The tenant the refusal happened in.

reason.description: Why it was refused, `invalid_target` for instance.

Contract.ResourceAudienceRejected.description: RFC 8707: the request was refused fail-closed because the resource indicator was unregistered, disabled, or given more than once. It covers the authorize, PAR, and token (authorization_code) paths. A refusal during a token exchange is expressed by `TokenExchangeRejected.reason`, and this event is not emitted for it.

Contract.ResourceIndicator.description: The `resource` parameter of RFC 8707: an absolute URI naming the requested audience, with no fragment. Only one is permitted per token, and naming several is refused with `invalid_target`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the token was issued in.

resource.description: The resource URI bound to the `aud` of the issued token.

Contract.ResourceScopedTokenIssued.description: RFC 8707: an access token was issued whose audience is strictly confined to a single McpResourceServer, following the resource indicator. It covers the authorize, PAR, and token (authorization_code) paths. Issuance confined by a resource through a token exchange is expressed by `TokenExchanged.audience`, and this event is not emitted for it.

name.description: The type name, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` and unique within the AuthorizationModel.

Contract.ResourceTypeDefinition.description: A resource type the authorization model defines. The `resource_type` and `subject_type` of a RelationTuple may only be type names declared here.

Contract.ResponseMode.description: How the authorization endpoint delivers the code to the redirect_uri. Wire values follow OAuth 2.0 Multiple Response Type Encoding Practices and OAuth 2.0 Form Post Response Mode.

Contract.ResponseType.description: Published-language stub for the authorization response type owned by the OAuth2 context. Wire value follows RFC 6749 section 3.1.1; only the authorization code flow is supported.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.RestoreGracePeriodExpiredError.description: RestoreAdminUser was called after the deletion grace period had elapsed. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:restore_grace_expired`.

Contract.RevocationEpochAdvanced.description: The revocation epoch of an Agent moved forward, settling a local revocation. The transmitter projector takes this event as its starting point and creates the CaepEvent and SecurityEventDelivery.

epoch.description: The epoch already advanced to. Absent for an Agent that has never been revoked.

Contract.RevocationReason.description: What moved the revocation epoch forward.

Contract.RevokeApplicationClientSecretRe.description: The list of non-sensitive metadata returned after one named credential has been revoked.

Contract.RevokeClientSecretResponse.description: The non-sensitive credential metadata after one credential has been revoked. Neither the secret nor a hash is included.

Contract.RevokeConsent.description: The lifecycle event withdrawing a consent logically.

Contract.RevokeRequest.description: The `/revoke` request (RFC 7009 section 2.1), which revokes the named token.

Contract.RevokeToken.description: The lifecycle event revoking a token.

Contract.Rotate.description: The event rotating a refresh token into a child token.

Contract.RotateApplicationClientSecretRe.description: The request to rotate the secret of an Application's OIDC protocol. `grace_days` is 7 when left out, and only 0 -- revoke at once -- or 1 to 30 days is accepted.
Returns the new secret once. It carries no hash, no existing secret, and no way to read the plaintext again.

Contract.RotateClientSecretRequest.description: The rotation request, naming how many days the existing secret overlaps. 0 revokes it at once, 1 to 30 gives it a grace, and leaving it out means 7 days.

Contract.RotateClientSecretResponse.description: The rotation response, returning the new secret once. There is no API to read it afterwards.

audience.description: The audience of the SP; the entity_id by default.

recipient.description: The Recipient of the bearer SubjectConfirmationData, that is, the ACS URL.

Contract.SamlAssertion.description: The `<saml:Assertion>` embedded in the SAMLResponse. It carries a Subject (the NameID and a bearer SubjectConfirmation), an AudienceRestriction, an AuthnStatement, and an AttributeStatement. The bearer SubjectConfirmationData carries Recipient (the ACS), NotOnOrAfter, and, for an SP-initiated flow, InResponseTo.

id.description: The request id. It round-trips as the InResponseTo of the SAMLResponse and in the SubjectConfirmationData of the assertion.

issuer.description: The entityID of the SP. It resolves to a registered SamlServiceProvider.

issue_instant.description: `AuthnRequest/@IssueInstant`. A request beyond the future skew or the maximum age is refused.

acs_url.description: The AssertionConsumerService URL the request names. Only an exact match against the permitted set is accepted.

acs_index.description: AssertionConsumerServiceIndex. Using it together with an ACS URL is refused, and so is naming it at all, because the initial implementation does not resolve an explicit index.

protocol_binding.description: `AuthnRequest/@ProtocolBinding`. Only absent or HTTP-POST is accepted.

destination.description: The IdP SSO endpoint URL the request was addressed to.

name_id_format.description: `NameIDPolicy/@Format`. Anything other than unspecified becomes the NameID format of the issued assertion.

force_authn.description: A demand to reauthenticate. When true, a caller who did not reauthenticate recently is sent back to sign in.

is_passive.description: A demand that there be no interaction. When true and the existing session cannot be used, a NoPassive response is returned rather than a move to the sign-in page.

Contract.SamlAuthnRequest.description: The intermediate form holding what has to be checked, extracted from a `<samlp:AuthnRequest>` received during SP-initiated SSO. HTTP-Redirect is deflate+base64 and HTTP-POST is base64; both are decoded before parsing. The decoded XML has a size ceiling, so a deflate bomb cannot get through. Version must be 2.0, and IssueInstant is required and has to sit inside both the permitted clock skew and the maximum age.

Contract.SamlBinding.description: The SAML 2.0 message bindings, used to receive an SP-initiated AuthnRequest and to return a SAMLResponse. HTTP-Redirect puts deflate+base64 in the query of a GET; HTTP-POST carries base64 in an auto-submitting form.

Contract.SamlIdentityProviderProfile.description: A SAML IdP trust boundary inside a tenant. The default profile uses the tenant-wide entityID and the existing SAML endpoints. An additional profile gets its own entityID, endpoints, and XmlFederationSigning key scope, each carrying the profile id.

Contract.SamlIdentityProviderProfileAdmi.description: How an IdP profile is represented for the administration console. Besides the persisted profile it returns the settings the server derived from the request tenant's canonical issuer, and how many SPs are currently assigned to it.

Contract.SamlIdentityProviderProfileMode.description: Whether an IdP profile may be shared by several SPs.

name.description: The display name of the profile.

mode.description: Whether the profile may be shared by several SPs.

Contract.SamlIdentityProviderProfileRequ.description: The JSON request creating or updating an additional SAML IdP profile. The default profile can be neither created nor changed this way.

tenantId.description: The tenant that logged out.

entityId.description: The entityID of the SP that asked for the logout, when it could be determined.

Contract.SamlLogout.description: A SAML Single Logout destroyed the local session. When there was a LogoutRequest, a LogoutResponse is returned to the registered SLO URL.

Contract.SamlNameIDFormat.description: The NameID format of an issued assertion. Both the SP metadata and the NameIDPolicy of an AuthnRequest may ask for one. When the AuthnRequest names anything other than unspecified it is honoured; when it names nothing, the format set in the SP's claim policy is used.

destination.description: The settled ACS URL, drawn from the permitted set.

in_response_to.description: The AuthnRequest id for an SP-initiated flow. Empty for an IdP-initiated one.

Contract.SamlResponse.description: The `<samlp:Response>` returned to the SP. It carries Status Success, an Issuer holding the IdP entityID, and a signed Assertion, and the whole Response is signed too when the SP is configured for it. Destination is the settled ACS URL, and InResponseTo is the AuthnRequest id for an SP-initiated flow. It is base64-encoded under the HTTP-POST binding and auto-posted to the ACS.

tenant_id.description: The tenant it belongs to. SP registrations and the SAML endpoints are separated per realm.

idp_profile_id.description: The SAML IdP profile assigned to this SP inside the tenant. An SSO or SLO request is accepted only when it matches the profile of the route.

entity_id.description: The identifier of the SP (its SAML entityID). It has to match the Issuer of the AuthnRequest exactly. The entityIDType of saml-schema-metadata-2.0.xsd fixes 1024 characters, but the ceiling here sits outside that so a non-conforming SP is not refused. A separate ceiling of 2048 bytes applies as the resource limit that keeps the value inside a btree index row.

application_id.description: The Application it corresponds to. Ordinary CRUD leaves it alone; only the bulk creation and deletion of an Application manage the relationship.

display_name.description: The display name in the administration UI.

acs_urls.description: The closed set of permitted AssertionConsumerService URLs. When an AuthnRequest names an ACS URL, only an exact match against this set is accepted, and only when both the ACS URL and the index are absent does the first entry become the default reply target. Resolving an index is not offered in the initial implementation.

slo_url.description: The SingleLogoutService URL of the SP, where a Single Logout reply is sent.

audience.description: The AudienceRestriction of an issued assertion. Empty means the entity_id is used.

claim_policy.description: The NameID and attribute (claim) issuance policy for this SP.

sign_assertion.description: Whether the issued Assertion carries an enveloped signature. It does by default.

sign_response.description: Whether the whole Response carries an enveloped signature. Turn it on for an SP that asks to "sign response".

want_authn_requests_signed.description: The per-SP policy for verifying signatures on an AuthnRequest or a LogoutRequest. When true, either the Redirect binding signature or the XML signature is verified against `authn_request_signing_certificate_pem`. It is not reflected in WantAuthnRequestsSigned in the IdP metadata.

authn_request_signing_certificate_pem.description: The X.509 certificate of the SP, as PEM, used to verify signatures on an AuthnRequest or a LogoutRequest. Required when `want_authn_requests_signed` is true.

Contract.SamlServiceProvider.description: The registration of a service provider (SP) for SAML 2.0 Web Browser SSO. It is identified by its entityID and bundles the closed set of permitted AssertionConsumerService URLs, the audience, the NameID format, the signature policy, and the claim issuance policy. An SP outside the catalogue, whose `application_id` is null, is allowed; when it is not null it names a `saml` Application of the same tenant, and at most one SP is bound to one Application.

entity_id.description: The identifier of the SP (its SAML entityID). It has to match the Issuer of the AuthnRequest exactly.

display_name.description: The display name in the administration UI.

idp_profile_id.description: The SAML IdP profile in the same tenant to assign to this SP.

acs_urls.description: The closed set of permitted AssertionConsumerService URLs.

slo_url.description: The SingleLogoutService URL of the SP.

audience.description: The AudienceRestriction of an issued assertion. Empty means the entity_id is used.

claim_policy.description: The NameID and attribute (claim) issuance policy for this SP.

sign_assertion.description: Whether the issued Assertion carries an enveloped signature. Left out, it does.

sign_response.description: Whether the whole Response carries an enveloped signature.

want_authn_requests_signed.description: Whether an AuthnRequest and a LogoutRequest have their signatures verified.

authn_request_signing_certificate_pem.description: The X.509 certificate of the SP, as PEM, used to verify those signatures. Required when `want_authn_requests_signed` is true.

Contract.SamlServiceProviderRequest.description: The JSON request registering or updating a SAML service provider (an upsert). It carries only what the caller may set; `application_id`, the tenant, and the timestamps stay with the server.

tenantId.description: The tenant that issued it.

entityId.description: The entityID of the SP it was issued to.

userId.description: The subject, the user the NameID resolved to.

Contract.SamlSignInIssued.description: A signed SAMLResponse was issued to an SP through SAML SSO.

tenantId.description: The tenant that refused it.

entityId.description: The SP entityID that was asked for, when it could be determined.

reason.description: A summary of why it was refused.

Contract.SamlSignInRejected.description: A SAML SSO request was refused: an unregistered entityID, an ACS URL outside the permitted set, an unassigned subject, a parse failure, and the like.

description.description: What the scheme is. Always English and never localized.

type.description: Scheme kind, such as `oauthbearertoken`.

Contract.ScimAuthenticationScheme.description: One authentication scheme the service provider accepts (RFC 7643 section 5).

Contract.ScimBulkConfig.description: Bulk operation support, as ServiceProviderConfig declares it (RFC 7643 section 5).

Contract.ScimFeatureSupport.description: Whether one optional SCIM feature is supported (RFC 7643 section 5).

maxResults.description: The largest page the server returns, whatever `count` the query asks for.

Contract.ScimFilterConfig.description: Filter support, as ServiceProviderConfig declares it (RFC 7643 section 5).

Contract.ScimGroupRef.description: Binds a SCIM 2.0 id to the internal Group it stands for (the group id).

totalResults.description: How many resources match the query in total, not how many this page carries.

startIndex.description: 1-based index of the first resource on this page.

itemsPerPage.description: How many resources this page carries.

Resources.description: The page of matching resources. Capitalized, as RFC 7644 section 3.4.2 spells it.

Contract.ScimListResponse.description: The SCIM query result envelope of RFC 7644 section 3.4.2.

status.description: The HTTP status code, as a decimal string.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized.

scimType.description: The SCIM detail error keyword of RFC 7644 section 3.12 table 9, such as `invalidFilter`, `invalidValue`, or `uniqueness`. Absent when no keyword applies.

Contract.ScimProtocolError.description: The SCIM protocol error response of RFC 7644 section 3.12. SCIM is a contact point whose shape the standard fixes, so it does not return Problem Details; the body is `application/json`.

Contract.ScimResource.description: A SCIM resource, sent to and returned by the /Users and /Groups endpoints (RFC 7643). The attributes present depend on which schemas the resource declares in `schemas`, so the contract records the resource as an open JSON object rather than fixing one attribute set; GetScimSchemas reports the attribute definitions the server honours. IdMagic supports the core User and Group schemas plus the enterprise User extension.

endpoint.description: Path the resource type is served under, relative to the SCIM base URL.

description.description: What the resource type is. Always English and never localized.

schema.description: URN of the core schema for this resource type.

Contract.ScimResourceType.description: One resource type the service provider exposes (RFC 7643 section 6).

id.description: URN of the schema this document defines.

description.description: What the schema is for. Always English and never localized.

Contract.ScimSchema.description: One schema the service provider honours (RFC 7643 section 7). IdMagic reports the core User schema, the enterprise User extension, and the core Group schema.

type.description: Attribute type, such as `string`, `boolean`, `reference`, or `complex`.

description.description: What the attribute holds. Always English and never localized.

referenceTypes.description: For `reference` attributes, which resource types the reference may point at.

subAttributes.description: For `complex` attributes, the definitions of the sub-attributes.

Contract.ScimSchemaAttribute.description: One attribute definition inside a SCIM schema (RFC 7643 section 7).

required.description: Whether a resource of this type must carry the extension.

Contract.ScimSchemaExtension.description: A schema a resource type extends beyond its core schema (RFC 7643 section 6), such as the enterprise User extension.

Contract.ScimServiceProviderConfig.description: The SCIM service provider configuration of RFC 7643 section 5, reporting which optional features this deployment supports.

Contract.ScimUserRef.description: Binds a SCIM 2.0 id to the internal User it stands for (the `sub`).

Contract.SecurityEventDelivery.description: The delivery state of an outbound SET. A projector creates it from RevocationEpochAdvanced, and delivery and retry are at-least-once.

Contract.SecurityEventDeliveryDeadLetter.description: A SecurityEventDelivery used up `max_delivery_attempts` and moved to dead_letter.

Contract.SecurityEventDeliveryFailed.description: A SecurityEventDelivery failed and a retry was scheduled.

Contract.SecurityEventDeliveryRetried.description: A failed SecurityEventDelivery was returned to pending for another attempt.

Contract.SecurityEventDeliveryStatus.description: The delivery state of an outbound SET.

Contract.SecurityEventReceived.description: An inbound SET was verified and applied as a local revocation.

streamId.description: When the rejection happened before the issuer was resolved, the stream may not be identifiable.

Contract.SecurityEventRejected.description: Verification of an inbound SET failed fail-closed and nothing was applied.

error.description: Always `security_event_rejected`.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the rejection. Always English and never localized.

Contract.SecurityEventRejectedError.description: Verification of a received SET failed fail-closed: an unregistered issuer, a bad signature, an expired token, an audience mismatch, a duplicate `jti`, or a subject that could not be resolved. The receive endpoint is a contact point whose shape RFC 8935 fixes, so it does not return Problem Details; the body is `application/json`. IdMagic currently emits `error` and `message` rather than the `err` and `description` of RFC 8935 section 2.3, and this model records what the server sends today.

error.description: Always `ssf_stream_not_found`.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Always English and never localized.

Contract.SecurityEventStreamNotFoundErro.description: The `stream_id` in the path does not name an SsfStream of this tenant. Returned by the receive endpoint, so the body is the `application/json` shape of that contact point, not Problem Details; the administration API reports the same condition as Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:ssf_stream_not_found`.

compact.description: The compact serialization of the signed JWT.

Contract.SecurityEventToken.description: A Security Event Token (RFC 8417): the signed compact JWT together with its decoded standard claims.

error.description: Always `security_event_token_too_large`.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Always English and never localized.

Contract.SecurityEventTokenTooLargeError.description: The Security Event Token in the request body is larger than the receive endpoint accepts. The receive endpoint is a contact point whose shape RFC 8935 fixes, so the body is `application/json` and carries `error` and `message` rather than Problem Details.

Contract.SecurityEventVerificationResult.description: The verification outcome of an inbound SET.

Contract.SecurityNotificationCategory.description:
The kinds of account security notification. Every message belongs to exactly one kind, and each kind
decides whether the user may stop receiving it. `new_device_sign_in` is a sign-in from a browser not seen before;
`credential_change` is a password change; `mfa_change` is an authentication factor, recovery code, or trusted device
being added or removed; `contact_change` is an email address change being requested and settled; `session_revoked` is
the user or an administrator explicitly revoking a session; and `impersonation` is an administrator beginning to act
as the user.

auth_methods.description: The authentication method accepted, `UsernameToken` for instance.

Contract.SecurityTokenEndpoint.description: An STS endpoint advertised in the WS-Trust and WS-Federation metadata, describing the authentication method and the binding it accepts.

Contract.SeedConflictError.description: A seed-managed target has manual drift and cannot be overwritten without an explicit reconcile. A seeding-tool domain condition, not an HTTP response body.

includes.description: A path relative to the root manifest directory. A cycle, a path outside the root, and a remote URL are all refused.

resources.description: The desired resources, keyed by kind, handed to the public command surface of the owning context. Any JSON value, because each kind carries the request shape of its own context and the set of kinds is open; an unknown kind and a duplicate logical key are both rejected. Seeding has no HTTP surface, so this shape is the manifest file rather than a request body.

generators.description: The bounded generators the profile and the explicit seed resolve to. Any JSON value, for the same reason as `resources`: each generator kind carries its own parameters. Generated performance users are login-disabled and hold no secret.

Contract.SeedManifest.description: A versioned manifest holding, per profile, the typed desired resources, the includes, and the deterministic generators. A secret appears only as a SeedSecretReference.

operations.description: A streamable rendering of the planned operations: logical key, operation kind, and a redacted summary. Any JSON value, because the summary shape follows the kind of each operation.

Contract.SeedPlan.description: The plan a seed run produced. It carries no secret and no full PII.

Contract.SeedRejectedError.description: The environment policy, the profile, a count ceiling, or an unknown key broke a safety rule. A seeding-tool domain condition, not an HTTP response body: seeding has no HTTP surface.

manifest_path.description: An explicit root manifest path. Left out, the repository default for the profile is used.

first_party_redirect_uris.description: The URIs to configure on the first-party client during a production bootstrap. In production a bootstrap run requires at least one, and a localhost URI is not accepted.

allow_large.description: Explicitly allows a count above the usual ceiling of the performance profile. A value above the absolute ceiling is still refused.

batch_size.description: How many records one batch applies while keeping the performance profile within bounded memory. Left out, a safe default is used; a value above the ceiling is refused.

Contract.SeedRequest.description: The input for planning or applying a profile. `profile` and `environment` are required, and raising a count has to be stated explicitly.

Contract.SeedSecretReference.description: An opaque reference used to materialize a secret. `version` identifies an intended rotation of the same secret.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.SelfDeleteForbiddenError.description: The operator tried to delete their own User. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:self_delete_forbidden`.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.SelfDisableForbiddenError.description: The operator tried to disable their own User. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:self_disable_forbidden`.

jkt.description: The SHA-256 thumbprint of the DPoP key (RFC 9449 section 6.1).

x5t_s256.description: The thumbprint of the mTLS client certificate (`x5t#S256`, RFC 8705).

Contract.SenderConstraintKind.description: How a token is bound to its holder (RFC 7800). `dpop` is the thumbprint of the DPoP public key, `mtls` the thumbprint of the mTLS client certificate.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.ServerError.description: An unexpected internal failure on the authorization server (RFC 6749 section 4.1.2.1, server_error).

Contract.SessionEndReason.description:
Why a LoginSession ended. `self_revoke` and `admin_revoke` are the user or an administrator revoking it
explicitly; `logout`, `idle`, and `absolute` are automatic; and `password_change` and `mfa_change` follow a credential
change.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

actorUserId.description: The `sub` of whoever performed the revocation; the user themselves for a self-revoke.

Contract.SessionEnded.description:
A LoginSession ended. When the user or an administrator revoked it explicitly, `actorUserId` is whoever acted
and `reason` is `self_revoke` or `admin_revoke`. The `sessionId` equals the OIDC `sid`, and the OAuth2 bounded context
uses it as the key to revoke the refresh token families whose `RefreshTokenRecord.sid` matches and to notify the
registered relying parties through front-channel and back-channel logout.
Access tokens themselves are not revoked immediately by this event; their short TTL takes care of them.

Contract.SessionImpersonationEnded.description: An impersonation session ended. It is not subject to shortened retention.

actorUserId.description: The `sub` of the administrator who impersonated.

Contract.SessionImpersonationStarted.description:
An administrator began a session acting as a user (impersonation). It is an audit event that presumes the user is
notified, and is not subject to shortened retention.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.SessionNotFoundError.description: The login session named by the request does not exist, or has already ended. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:session_not_found`.

Contract.SessionRecord.description:
The projection of one entry in the administrative session list. It holds no secret: only what is needed to
identify and audit a live session of the target user. Unlike the self-service AccountSession it has no
`current` marker, because the caller and the target user are different people.

Contract.SessionRecordListResponse.description: What ListSessions (administrative) returns: the live sessions of the target user, by start time, newest first.

Contract.SessionRefreshed.description: The validity of a LoginSession was extended, because it stayed active.

ip.description: The client IP at the start of the session. It is stored in plaintext for as long as the audit event is retained.

userAgent.description: The User-Agent at the start of the session. It is stored in plaintext for as long as the audit event is retained.

Contract.SessionStarted.description: A LoginSession began. It is the starting point of the session list and of an investigation.

allow_trusted_device.description:
When `required_authn` is `Mfa`, whether a remembered trusted device (amr holding `tdev`) may satisfy the MFA
requirement. False means MFA every time, admitting nothing but a genuine second factor.
It defaults to true, but as long as the tenant leaves `trusted_device_max_age_seconds` at zero, no trusted device is
ever issued or evaluated, so the effective default is not to remember anything.

Contract.SignInRule.description: One rule of a sign-in policy.

Contract.SignatureAlgorithm.description: The JWT signing algorithms. Confined to the strong asymmetric ones FAPI 2.0 permits; symmetric algorithms such as HS256 are excluded.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the key belongs to. It names an existing Tenant, and the kid of tenant B never appears in the JWKS of tenant A.

provider.description: Where the key material is kept and who performs the signature.

scope_id.description: An independent key lifecycle inside one tenant and use. Normally `default`; the profile id for an additional SAML IdP profile.

certificate_der.description: The DER of the self-signed X.509 certificate that goes with an XmlFederationSigning key. Empty for a Signing key, required for XML use. It is public information and holds no private key.

activated_at.description: When the key first became Active.

retired_at.description: When the key moved to Retired.

expires_at.description: When the grace during which a Verifying key stays published on the JWKS ends. From then on it leaves the JWKS and becomes eligible for archiving.

Contract.SigningKey.description:
An asymmetric key for signing tokens. Per tenant, use, and scope, one Active key and zero or more Verifying predecessors
are published (SigningKeyMinJwksOverlap). Listing, searching, rotating, and choosing a signing key all narrow by
`tenant_id`, `usage`, and `scope_id`. `tenant_id` names an existing Tenant. `scope_id` is `default` normally, and the
profile id for an additional SAML IdP profile, so that XML signing credentials stay separate.

Contract.SigningKeyArchived.description: A signing key moved from Retired to Archived after its grace ended; Archived is terminal and kept for audit.

Contract.SigningKeyRetired.description:
A signing key moved from Verifying to Retired and left the JWKS, either because SigningKeyMinJwksOverlap had passed or
because it was disabled as an emergency.

tenantId.description: The tenant the rotated signing key belongs to.

Contract.SigningKeyRotated.description: The signing key on the JWKS was rotated, every 90 days by default or as an emergency rotation.

Contract.SigningKeyState.description:
The internal states of SigningKeyLifecycle. Active is the current signing key, Verifying is a key that only verifies
already-issued tokens during the overlap after a rotation, Retired has left the JWKS, and Archived is kept for audit.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.SlowDownError.description: The client is polling the Device Authorization Grant too fast and must add five seconds to its interval (RFC 8628 section 3.5, slow_down).

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.SsfReceiverAcceptedAudiencesReq.description: `accepted_audiences` is empty. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:ssf_receiver_accepted_audiences_required`.

trusted_issuer.description: The issuer URL the `iss` claim of the external transmitter's SET must match.

Contract.SsfReceiverConfig.description: The trust settings for the external transmitter, accompanying an SsfStream with `direction=Receive`, one per stream. It reuses the same registered-issuer verification WorkloadTrustBundle uses. At least one of `jwks_uri` and inline `jwks` is required.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.SsfReceiverJwksRequiredError.description: Neither `jwks_uri` nor `jwks` was given. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:ssf_receiver_jwks_required`.

Contract.SsfReceiverStreamRegisterReques.description: The JSON request an administrator sends to register an SsfStream with `direction=Receive`.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

Contract.SsfReceiverTrustedIssuerInvalid.description: `trusted_issuer` is absent or is not an https URL. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:ssf_receiver_trusted_issuer_invalid`.

event_types.description: The subset of event types this stream sends or accepts.

Contract.SsfStream.description: The metadata every SSF stream a tenant registers shares. Depending on the direction, exactly one SsfTransmitterConfig or SsfReceiverConfig accompanies it.

Contract.SsfStreamDeleted.description: An administrator deleted an SsfStream. The TransmitterConfig or ReceiverConfig attached to it was deleted with it.

Contract.SsfStreamDirection.description: Which way the stream runs, seen from IdMagic. `Transmit` means IdMagic pushes CAEP events to an external receiver; `Receive` means IdMagic accepts events from an external transmitter.

Contract.SsfStreamDisabled.description: An administrator disabled an SsfStream. It neither delivers nor accepts anything afterwards.

Contract.SsfStreamEnabled.description: An administrator re-enabled a disabled SsfStream.

Contract.SsfStreamRegistered.description: An administrator registered a new SsfStream.

Contract.SsfStreamUpdateRequest.description: The JSON request an administrator sends to update the `event_types` of an SsfStream. A field left out keeps its current value.

Contract.SsfStreamUpdated.description: An administrator updated the metadata of an SsfStream.

Contract.SsfSubject.description: What a CAEP event is about. It maps one-to-one onto the subject representation of the access tokens IdMagic itself issues (tenant_id plus principal_id), so there is no separate subject mapping table of the kind WorkloadIdentity keeps.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

delivery_endpoint.description: The endpoint of the external receiver that accepts the push. It must be https.

audience.description: The `aud` claim of the SETs issued on this stream.

delivery_authorization.description: An optional bearer secret presented in the Authorization header when pushing to the receiver.

Contract.SsfTransmitterConfig.description: The delivery settings accompanying an SsfStream with `direction=Transmit`, one per stream.
