Contract.SsfTransmitterDeliveryEndpointI.description: `delivery_endpoint` is absent or is not an https URL. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:ssf_transmitter_delivery_endpoint_invalid`.

Contract.SsfTransmitterStreamRegisterReq.description: The JSON request an administrator sends to register an SsfStream with `direction=Transmit`.

Contract.StepUpCompleteRequest.description:
The input of CompleteStepUpAuthentication. Depending on `method` it uses the password or the code.
The material verified never reaches the audit trail or a log.

tenantId.description: The tenant the user belongs to.

Contract.StepUpCompleted.description:
A step-up reauthentication succeeded. `method` is the factor used, `password` or `totp`.
The material verified -- the password or the code -- is not in the payload.

Contract.StepUpMethod.description:
The factors usable for a step-up reauthentication. `password` always; `totp` and `webauthn` once enrolled;
`recovery_code` only while valid codes remain.

tenantId.description: The tenant the user belongs to.

Contract.StepUpRequested.description:
A user began a step-up reauthentication ahead of a high-sensitivity operation.
It is the request to be shown the available factors; the reauthentication has not succeeded yet.

Contract.StepUpStartResponse.description:
What StartStepUpAuthentication returns: the reauthentication methods available, which the UI offers as choices in
its reauthentication modal.

Contract.TOTPEnrollmentConfirmRequest.description:
The TOTP enrollment confirmation request (self-service). The secret is the one from the start,
and the code is the current one generated from it, as proof of possession.

Contract.TOTPEnrollmentStart.description:
What starting a TOTP enrollment returns (self-service). The client holds the secret until it confirms, and
`otpauth_uri` is offered for a QR code or manual entry. The secret is not persisted until it comes back with the
confirmation (ConfirmTotpEnrollment).

max_delegation_depth.description:
Tenant override for the maximum Token Exchange (RFC 8693) `act` chain depth. When omitted, the system default applies.
The override may only tighten the limit; PolicyOverrideWeakerError rejects values above the system default.
This asymmetric rule matches password_policy_override and prevents tenant settings from widening an authorization boundary.

trusted_device_max_age_seconds.description:
How many seconds a trusted device -- "remember this device" in the Authentication context -- stays valid.
Zero, or leaving it out, disables the feature for the whole tenant: no device is remembered and no second factor is skipped.
The system ceiling is 7,776,000 seconds (90 days), and a larger value is refused with PolicyOverrideWeakerError.

Contract.Tenant.description: The tenant (realm) aggregate. Clients, Users, Consents, policies, and branding all stay inside this authorization boundary.

product_name.description: The name shown on the sign-in screen and elsewhere. An empty string means unset, and the system default (IdMagic) is shown.

logo_object_key.description: The opaque key of the logo image object stored inside the tenant boundary. An administrator never enters it directly; it comes from UploadTenantBrandingAsset with `kind=Logo`.

logo_url.description: The internal serving URL the IdP builds from the stored logo.

favicon_object_key.description: The opaque key of the favicon image object stored inside the tenant boundary. It comes from UploadTenantBrandingAsset with `kind=Favicon`.

favicon_url.description: The internal serving URL the IdP builds from the stored favicon.

primary_color.description: The primary brand colour. It is injected only as the CSS custom property `--tenant-brand-primary`. Anything in `#rrggbb` form can be saved whatever its contrast ratio, and an empty string normalizes to unset and returns to the system default. Whether the palette is legible is the tenant's judgement.

accent_color.description: The accent brand colour. It is injected only as the CSS custom property `--tenant-brand-accent`. Anything in `#rrggbb` form can be saved whatever its contrast ratio, and an empty string normalizes to unset and returns to the system default. Whether the palette is legible is the tenant's judgement.

footer_link_1.description: The first footer link. The order is fixed as footer_link_1 then footer_link_2.

footer_link_2.description: The second footer link. The order is fixed as footer_link_1 then footer_link_2.

footer_text.description: The supplementary text shown in the footer, a copyright notice for instance. It is rendered as plain text, protected by nothing more than the renderer's default escaping.

updated_at.description: It advances on every update. It serves as the version and the ETag of the public response.

Contract.TenantBranding.description:
The per-tenant hosted UI branding settings. They are not embedded in the Tenant aggregate but held as a separate
entity, for the same reason as TenantUserAttributeSchema: sparse per-tenant configuration is kept apart from the Tenant
itself. Every field is optional, and a missing row, or a row with every field unset, means branding is unset and
GetTenantBranding falls back to the system default.
The colours, links, and text accept only a limited set of tokens; arbitrary CSS or HTML cannot be accepted structurally.

Contract.TenantBrandingAssetKind.description: The kinds of image asset a TenantBranding holds.

updated_at.description: Used as the version and the ETag once branding has been set at least once. Left out while it is unset.

Contract.TenantBrandingResponse.description:
The publicly safe projection GetTenantBranding, UpdateTenantBranding, and the asset upload and delete return.
An unset field stands for the system default, which the client resolves to `IdMagic` and the like.

Contract.TenantBrandingUpdateRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator updates the branding text, colours, and links. Image assets are handled separately, through UploadTenantBrandingAsset and DeleteTenantBrandingAsset. Only the fields given are changed, and passing null returns that field to unset. `primary_color` and `accent_color` return to unset on an empty string as well.

Contract.TenantBrandingUpdated.description: A tenant administrator updated the branding: its text, colours, links, or image assets.

Contract.TenantBrandingUploadResponse.description: How branding is represented after an image asset has been uploaded or deleted.

Contract.TenantCreateRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator registers a new tenant. `realm` is a URL-safe slug, and the server mints the UUID key (`id`).

Contract.TenantCreated.description: A system_admin created a new tenant.

id.description: Internal identifier, the value `EncryptedSecret.key_id` refers to.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the key belongs to. It names an existing Tenant.

version.description: A version number that rises monotonically within the tenant, by one on every rotation.

wrapped_dek.description: The DEK as the MasterKey provider wrapped it. The plaintext DEK never appears in storage, in a log, or in an event.

master_key_id.description: Identifies the MasterKey -- the provider's key and version -- that wrapped this DEK, so that rotation of the MasterKey itself can be traced.

Contract.TenantDataEncryptionKey.description: One version of a tenant's DEK. It holds only the key material the MasterKey provider wrapped (`wrapped_dek`); the plaintext DEK is never stored. A tenant has at most one Active version.

provider.description: The MasterKey provider name, such as `openbao` or `tink_cleartext`.

Contract.TenantDataKeyHealth.description: A key health snapshot for a system_admin. It carries no private key material.

Contract.TenantDefaultSignInPolicy.description: The tenant default sign-in policy. The ApplicationCatalog owns one per tenant, and it is the baseline applied when federation starts for every Application that has no policy of its own. Setting a policy on an application overrides the default for that application.

Contract.TenantDefaultSignInPolicyReques.description: The request in which an administrator replaces the tenant default sign-in policy.

unenrolled_user_count.description: How many active users of the tenant hold no TOTP or WebAuthn factor at all. It is used to gauge the impact before making MFA mandatory.

Contract.TenantDefaultSignInPolicyRespon.description: How the tenant default sign-in policy is represented.

Contract.TenantDefaultSignInPolicyUpdate.description: The tenant default sign-in policy was updated, clearing it included.

Contract.TenantDisabled.description: A system_admin disabled a tenant. Every protocol route of that tenant is refused with invalid_request.

Contract.TenantEnabled.description: A system_admin re-enabled a disabled tenant.

Contract.TenantEndpointStyle.description: The shape of a tenant's canonical location. A tenant has exactly one, and the issuer, the cookie scope, and the WebAuthn RP ID all follow from it. `path` is `{base}/realms/{realm}` on a shared host, and is the default because it needs neither wildcard DNS nor a certificate. `subdomain` is the tenant-specific host `{realm}.{tenant_base_domain}`, and it is what makes the features that need a tenant-specific origin work: `__Host-` cookies, a per-tenant WebAuthn RP ID, and a per-tenant branded origin. In a deployment where `tenant_base_domain` is unset, `subdomain` cannot be chosen.

label.description: The link text shown to the user. It is never interpreted as HTML or Markdown.

url.description: Where the link goes. Only the https scheme is on the allow list.

Contract.TenantFooterLink.description: A safe external link shown in the hosted UI footer, in a fixed order. The label is rendered as plain text and the URL may only be HTTPS. When one is present, both `label` and `url` have to be non-empty; giving only one of the two is refused.

attributes.description: The definitions, whose keys are unique.

Contract.TenantGroupAttributeSchema.description: The set of Group custom attribute definitions of one tenant. Group has nothing corresponding to the built-in catalogue of TenantUserAttributeSchema, so this set is the effective definition in full. It is a separate aggregate rather than something embedded in the tenant aggregate, and it cascades when the tenant is deleted.

attributes.description: The Group custom definitions the tenant may edit.

Contract.TenantGroupAttributeSchemaRespo.description: What `/api/admin/tenant/group_attribute_schema` returns. Group has no built-in catalogue, so unlike the User version it carries no `builtin` field.

attributes.description: The new list of custom definitions. An empty array deletes them all.

Contract.TenantGroupAttributeSchemaUpdat.description: The JSON request replacing the tenant's Group custom attribute definitions outright. A duplicate key is refused in the use case.
A tenant administrator updated the Group custom attribute definitions (TenantGroupAttributeSchema). No value is kept; only the list of custom attribute keys after the change is recorded.

Contract.TenantListResponse.description: The tenant list of the administration API.

ssf_streams.description: The ceiling on SsfStreams, transmit and receive counted together.

Contract.TenantQuota.description: The per-tenant resource ceilings, hard and soft. A system administrator may override them per tenant.

Contract.TenantQuotaUpdateRequest.description: The JSON request in which a system_admin overrides a tenant's Quota.

Contract.TenantQuotaUpdated.description: A system_admin overrode a tenant's resource quota.

tenant_id.description: The tenant this row is about.

usage.description: What the keys are for; today Signing.

active_kid.description: The kid of the currently active signing key. Absent for a tenant that has no key yet.

active_state.description: The state of the active key.

jwks_key_count.description: How many keys the JWKS carries (active plus verifying).

provider_healthy.description: Whether the KeyProvider is reachable. When false, new issuance stops fail-closed; the enforcement point is OAuth2.Token.

Contract.TenantSigningKey.description:
Signing key health for one tenant, returned so a system_admin can survey health across tenants:
provider, active kid, key count, and provider reachability.
No private key is included.

Contract.TenantStatus.description: The tenant state. `active` runs normally; `disabled` stops the tenant accepting any protocol traffic, so `/authorize`, `/token`, and the rest all give invalid_request.

id.description: The immutable UUID key of the tenant.

realm.description: The slug identifier that appears in the URL `/realms/{realm}/`.

trusted_device_max_age_seconds.description: How many seconds a trusted device stays valid. Zero, or leaving it out, disables the feature.

Contract.TenantSummaryResponse.description: How a tenant is represented. The list and the detail views of the administration UI return the same representation.

password_policy_override.description: Left out, the existing value is kept. Pass null explicitly to clear it.

max_delegation_depth.description: Maximum delegation depth. Omission preserves the current value, and zero restores the system default. Values above the system default are rejected.

trusted_device_max_age_seconds.description:
How many seconds a trusted device stays valid. Left out, the existing value is kept; 0 turns the feature off again.
A value above the system ceiling of 7,776,000 seconds (90 days) is refused.

default_locale.description: The tenant's default locale. Left out, the existing value is kept; an empty string returns it to the system default. An unsupported locale is refused.

Contract.TenantUpdateRequest.description: The JSON request in which an administrator updates a tenant's display name or password policy override. `id` and `status` are left alone; a status change goes through the dedicated disable and enable endpoints.

Contract.TenantUpdated.description: A system_admin updated a tenant's display name.

Contract.TenantUsage.description: How much of each resource a tenant currently uses.

attributes.description: The definitions, whose keys are unique and collide with no built-in attribute.

Contract.TenantUserAttributeSchema.description: The set of custom attribute definitions of one tenant. The built-in attributes live in code (BuiltinUserAttributeDefs), and this set holds only what the tenant added. It is a separate aggregate rather than something embedded in the tenant aggregate, and it cascades when the tenant is deleted.

attributes.description: The custom definitions the tenant may edit.

Contract.TenantUserAttributeSchemaRespon.description:
What `/api/admin/tenant/user_attribute_schema` returns. Besides the tenant's own custom attribute definitions
(`attributes`) it returns the built-in catalogue code holds (`builtin`) for reference, so the UI can list every attribute
while avoiding a key collision.

attributes.description: The new list of custom definitions. An empty array deletes them all.

Contract.TenantUserAttributeSchemaUpdate.description: The JSON request replacing the tenant's custom attribute definitions outright. A key that collides with a built-in attribute, and a duplicate key, are both refused in the use case.
A tenant administrator updated the custom attribute definitions (TenantUserAttributeSchema). No value is kept; only the list of custom attribute keys after the change is recorded.

Contract.TokenEndpointAuthMethod.description: Published-language stub for the token endpoint client authentication methods owned by the OAuth2 context. Wire values are the `token_endpoint_auth_method` values of OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 section 3 and RFC 8705 section 2.

tenantId.description: The tenant the token exchange was refused in.

actorUserId.description: The current actor, when it was known at the time of the refusal. Empty when it was not.

reason.description: Why it was refused, an OAuth error code for instance.

Contract.TokenExchangeRejected.description: RFC 8693: a token exchange request was refused fail-closed, for a policy violation or a failed check.

tenantId.description: The tenant the token exchange happened in.

actorUserId.description: The current actor of the issued token (`act.sub`).

subjectUserId.description: The subject of the issued token (`sub`). It keeps the `sub` of the `subject_token`.

audience.description: The `aud` of the issued token, taken from the `resource` parameter.

delegationDepth.description: How deeply the `act` claims of the issued token nest.

maxDelegationDepth.description:
Maximum delegation depth applied to this decision. The system default applies when the tenant has no override.
Recording the applied limit makes the decision reproducible from the audit event.

delegationMode.description: Delegation mode of the issued token, produced by the same derivation function used for introspection.

Contract.TokenExchanged.description: RFC 8693: a delegated token was issued through a token exchange. `delegationDepth` is how deeply the `act` claims of the issued token nest.

tenantId.description: The tenant the introspection happened in.

Contract.TokenIntrospected.description: `/introspect` was called and returned the token's state (RFC 7662). It is used to analyse how resource servers behave.

auth_req_id.description: The `auth_req_id` of the CIBA grant (`urn:openid:params:grant-type:ciba`). Until the approval is settled it returns `authorization_pending` or `slow_down`, and once settled it is exchanged for tokens exactly once.

subject_token.description: The `subject_token` of the RFC 8693 token-exchange grant. It is either a self-issued access token (`urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token`) or an external attestation JWT (`urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt`) issued by the issuer of a registered WorkloadTrustBundle.

subject_token_type.description: The URN naming the kind of `subject_token`. Left out, it is treated as a self-issued access token.

actor_token.description: The optional `actor_token` of the RFC 8693 token-exchange grant. It has to be a self-issued access token.

authorization_details.description: RFC 9396: the JSON string of structured details asking for a downscope during a token exchange. Optional.

resource.description: RFC 8707: the resource indicator for an authorization_code redemption, client_credentials, device_code, or token exchange. Naming the parameter more than once gives `invalid_target`. The refresh_token grant does not name it explicitly; the resource bound at the first issuance is carried automatically across rotations.

Contract.TokenRequest.description: The token endpoint request, sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

Contract.TokenResponse.description: The response body of a successful `/token` (RFC 6749 section 5.1). It returns the tokens issued and their kind.

tenantId.description: The tenant the revocation happened in.

Contract.TokenRevoked.description: A token was revoked, by `/revoke` or by an administrative operation (RFC 7009). It carries an audit and an immediacy requirement.

Contract.TokenType.description: Token kind carried by `token_type_hint` and by revocation audit events. Wire values follow RFC 7009 section 2.1.

id.description: The device identifier. It is the key for audit and for the user revoking it.

tenant_id.description: The tenant it belongs to. The cookie is realm-scoped, so it never resolves across tenants.

selector.description: The non-secret lookup key that forms the first half of the cookie, base64url-encoded. It is unique and used for nothing but locating one row.

verifier_hash.description: The SHA-256 of the second half of the cookie, the verifier, as hex. The plaintext is not stored, and it rotates on every use.

label.description:
A display label derived from the User-Agent, naming nothing beyond the browser and OS family, `Chrome / macOS` for instance.
Neither the raw User-Agent nor the IP is stored.

last_used_at.description: When it was last used to skip a second factor. The idle deadline is measured from here.

expires_at.description: `created_at` plus the tenant's `trusted_device_max_age_seconds`. The absolute deadline.

revoked_at.description: When it was revoked; null while it is not. Revocation is a tombstone and never deletes the row.

revoke_reason.description: The revocation reason, set together with `revoked_at`. Null while `revoked_at` is null.

Contract.TrustedDevice.description:
One trusted device, the "remember this device" credential. It is issued per user, and only when the user
explicitly consents right after a genuine second factor (TOTP or WebAuthn) has succeeded during sign-in. The browser
receives `selector.verifier` in a realm-scoped HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie, while the server stores nothing but the
selector and `verifier_hash` (SHA-256, as hex). The selector fetches one row and the verifier's hash is compared in
constant time, so neither the cookie plaintext nor a device fingerprint is ever stored.
The verifier rotates on every use, so a stolen old cookie is invalidated by the next legitimate one.
Validity is cut by both an absolute deadline (`expires_at`) and an idle one (`last_used_at` plus the idle window).

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

factor.description: The second factor that occasioned the remembering: `otp` or `webauthn`.

Contract.TrustedDeviceRegistered.description:
Right after a genuine second factor succeeded during sign-in, the user explicitly consented and the device was
remembered. Neither the cookie plaintext, nor the User-Agent, nor the IP is in the payload: only the device identifier
and the timestamps revocation decisions need.

Contract.TrustedDeviceRevokeReason.description:
Why a trusted device was revoked. `self_revoke` is the user revoking it explicitly; `password_change` and
`mfa_change` are bulk revocations following a credential change; `admin_revoke` is an administrator's authenticator
reset; `account_disabled` is the account being disabled; and `session_revoke` is the user or an administrator revoking
every session.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

Contract.TrustedDeviceRevoked.description:
A trusted device was revoked. Besides the user revoking it explicitly, it is emitted for the bulk revocations
that follow a credential change, an administrator's authenticator reset, an account being disabled, and every session
being revoked.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.UnauthorizedClientError.description: The client is not authorized to use this `grant_type` (RFC 6749 section 5.2, unauthorized_client).

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.UnknownCategoryError.description: A `category_id` assigned to an Application does not exist among the ApplicationCategory records of its tenant. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:unknown_category`.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.UnknownUserIdError.description: On the CIBA /bc-authorize endpoint, neither `login_hint` nor `id_token_hint` resolves to a User to ask for approval (OpenID Connect CIBA Core section 13, unknown_user_id). A user who is not active, and a user in another tenant, fold into the same error so the difference does not disclose whether the User exists.

error.description: The protocol error code. Identifies which condition occurred.

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the occurrence. Always English and never localized; the value is empty when the server has nothing safe to disclose, and the member is present either way.

Contract.UnsupportedGrantTypeError.description: The authorization server does not support this `grant_type` (RFC 6749 section 5.2, unsupported_grant_type).

disabled_categories.description: The kinds to stop receiving. Only optional kinds may be listed.

Contract.UpdateNotificationPreferencesRe.description:
The input of UpdateMyNotificationPreferences. It names the kinds to turn off rather than the ones to turn on,
so a kind added later is inherited as on by an existing setting. A request naming a mandatory kind is refused
with 400.

Contract.Use.description: The lifecycle event consuming a PAR `request_uri`, once.

Contract.User.description: The canonical user aggregate of the IdP. Protocol subjects are projected from this id, and profile extensions are kept in the sparse `attributes`.

key.description: The machine name of the attribute: snake_case starting with a letter, unique across the builtin catalogue and the tenant's custom attributes.

label.description: The label shown in the administration console and in self-service forms. Left out, the key itself is displayed.

type.description: The type of the attribute value. Validating a value against a definition whose type contradicts `multi_valued` fails.

multi_valued.description: Whether the attribute holds several values. It can be true only when `type` is `string_array`.

required.description: Whether a value is required when a User is created or updated.

editable_by_user.description: Whether the user may edit this attribute from their own self-service profile.

claim_name.description: The claim name to use when the attribute is issued as a claim. Left out, the key itself becomes the claim name.

oidc_scope.description: The OIDC scope that unlocks exposure as a claim. Left out, the `custom_attribute` scope is what unlocks it.

visibility.description: How far the attribute may be disclosed. There is no default: a definition without a value is refused, and so is a value outside the enum. Only `claim_exposed` may reach a claim.

pii.description: Whether the value holds personal information. Left out it is false, so an attribute that should be treated as PII has to say true explicitly.

Contract.UserAttributeDef.description: Published-language stub for the attribute definition the Tenancy context owns. Besides deciding attribute visibility during claim issuance, it appears verbatim in both the request and the response body of the tenant's user_attribute_schema.

tenantId.description: The tenant the authentication happened in. The audit view narrows by it.

sessionId.description: The id of the LoginSession the authentication started.

clientId.description: The OAuth client that started the authentication.

ip.description: The client IP. It is stored in plaintext for as long as the audit event is retained.

userAgent.description: The client User-Agent. It is stored in plaintext for as long as the audit event is retained.

countryCode.description: The country code from GeoIP; empty when GeoIP is not wired up.

deviceFingerprint.description: The device fingerprint. It is stored in plaintext for as long as the audit event is retained.

riskScore.description: The risk score. This work item only reserves the field; the value is null.

Contract.UserAuthenticated.description: A ResourceOwner authenticated successfully. `amr` lists the means actually used (OpenID Connect Core section 2).

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

Contract.UserCreated.description: An administrator created a user. Neither the initial password nor `password_hash` is in the audit event.

Contract.UserCsvTransferPolicy.description: The configurable safety policy User export and import share. It defaults to 100,000 data rows, 64 MiB per file, and 64 KiB per field. A successful User export always sits inside the same policy, so it can be previewed as it is. The ceilings do not express tenant capacity; they are an operational boundary on a single asynchronous artifact.

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

Contract.UserDeleted.description: A user was purged, either by an administrator or by the automatic purge once the grace period had elapsed. The PII has been anonymized and the related aggregates cascade-deleted. `reason` is a free-text note the administrator may leave, and is `auto_purge` for an automatic one.

Contract.UserDeprovisioned.description: A user deactivate or delete reached the downstream and the delivery settled as succeeded.

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

Contract.UserDisabled.description: An administrator disabled a user, refusing both new sign-ins and the use of existing sessions for them.

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

Contract.UserEnabled.description: An administrator re-enabled a disabled user.

group_roles.description: The union of the roles inherited from the groups they belong to.

Contract.UserGroupsResponse.description:
The groups a named User belongs to and the breakdown of their effective roles. The direct roles
(`user.roles`) and the roles inherited from groups are returned separately alongside their union, so the
administration UI can make effective roles easy to follow. `effective_roles` is `direct_roles` united with
`group_roles`; because it is derived across both User and Group, it is computed and exposed as a field of this
response rather than as a constraint on the User model.

status.description: Job status, from the Jobs context lifecycle.

result.description: Counts and digests the job produced. Absent until the job has run.

errors.description: One page of row errors, paginated by the standard cursor headers. Empty while the job is still running.

Contract.UserImportJob.description: The public view of a CSV user import job. A preview causes no side effects; an apply joins a succeeded preview of the same tenant on its `source_sha256`. Row errors name the column and a stable code, never the value, and neither passwords nor hashes are read or stored.

id.description: Job id, used to poll GetAdminUserImport and to start an apply from a preview.

status.description: Job status, from the Jobs context lifecycle.

Contract.UserImportJobRef.description: What the CSV user import endpoints return when a preview or an apply has been accepted. The job runs asynchronously; poll GetAdminUserImport with the `id` for progress and results.

Contract.UserImportMode.description: The stage of a CSV user import job. A preview is a read-only plan; an apply replans a succeeded preview payload against the current state and applies it.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the uploaded CSV. An apply must name a preview with the same digest.

preview_job_id.description: For an apply, the preview job it was started from.

accepted_rows.description: Compatibility field for older clients: created_rows + updated_rows + unchanged_rows. New clients use the per-operation counts.

error_artifact_ref.description: Reference to the stored error artifact, when the job produced one.

error_artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored error artifact.

error_total.description: How many row errors the job produced in total, not how many this page carries.

Contract.UserImportResult.description: Counts and digests a finished CSV user import job produced.

Contract.UserImportRowError.description: A safe validation or application error for one CSV row. It returns no value, only the column name and a stable code.

claims.description:
The additional claims formed by merging the scope-driven attribute claims (ClaimsForScopes) with the per-client
ClaimMapping claim policy. When a key collides with a standard claim, the standard claim wins.

Contract.UserInfoResponse.description: OpenID Connect Core section 5.3. It carries the mutable OIDC claims.

status_changed_at.description: When the current status was reached. The detailed transition history lives in the audit events.

Contract.UserLifecycle.description:
The operational lifecycle attributes of a User. `status` is the single source of truth and matches the
UserLifecycle state machine in the states section; the old `disabled_at` and `deleted_at` were folded into
`status` plus `status_changed_at`. A tombstone is `status == deleted`.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.UserNotFoundError.description: The User the request targets does not exist in this tenant. A User in another tenant is treated as nonexistent. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:user_not_found`.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

Contract.UserNotPendingDeletionError.description: The User that RestoreAdminUser targets is not in the `pending_deletion` state. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:not_pending_deletion`.

Contract.UserProvisioned.description: A user create or update reached the downstream and the delivery settled as succeeded.

Contract.UserProvisioningFailed.description: A user delivery used up `max_attempts` and settled as dead_letter. It is not emitted per attempt. A group delivery that dead-letters uses the same event.

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

actorUserId.description: Who cleared it. For an automatic clearing, the target themselves.

Contract.UserRequiredActionCleared.description: A forced action was cleared. Besides an administrator clearing it explicitly, it also fires when `update_password` is cleared automatically because the user changed their own password, and in that case the actor id is the target's own.

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

Contract.UserRequiredActionSet.description: An administrator gave a user an action to be forced at their next sign-in (a RequiredAction). `action` is an enum value and is safe to keep in the audit trail in plaintext.

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

Contract.UserRestored.description: An administrator restored a user in `pending_deletion`. The status returned to `active`, and they can sign in again with their PII and credentials intact.

amr.description: The technical values of RFC 8176 (RFC8176-AMR-VOCABULARY). The UI translates them into names meant for users: pwd is a password, otp an authenticator app, webauthn a passkey, rc a recovery code, and so on.

Contract.UserSignInActivity.description:
The projection of one entry in a user's own sign-in history. This slice derives from the existing audit
event store (UserAuthenticated), so the only attributes it holds are when it happened and by what means (amr).
Adding the IP, UA, sessionId, and clientId comes later, once the event itself has been extended.

Contract.UserSignInActivityResponse.description: What ListMySignInActivity and ListUserSignInActivity return: the most recent N entries, newest first.

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

Contract.UserSoftDeleted.description: An administrator soft-deleted a user. The status moved to `pending_deletion` and the PII, Consents, RefreshTokens, and Sessions were preserved. `reason` is a free-text note the administrator may leave.

Contract.UserStatus.description: The operational state of a User. Published-language stub for IdManagement.UserStatus, used only to evaluate the `from_status` and `to_status` of a trigger. IdManagement owns the single source of truth for the values.

tenantId.description: The tenant the operation acted in. It matches both the actor and the target.

Contract.UserUpdated.description: An administrator updated a user's profile or roles.

Contract.Validate.description: The lifecycle event validating an authorization request.

Contract.WebAuthnAssertionOptions.description:
What StartBrowserWebAuthn returns: the PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions to hand to
`navigator.credentials.get`, as JSON and unchanged. The challenge is bound to the pending login
session.

credential_id.description: The credential ID the authenticator returns, base64url-encoded. Unique within the RP.

public_key.description: The public key in COSE form, base64url-encoded.

sign_count.description: The signature counter of the most recent assertion. A counter that goes backwards is refused as a suspected clone (`sign_count_regression=reject`).

transports.description: The transport hints the authenticator declared: usb, nfc, ble, internal, or hybrid.

aaguid.description: The AAGUID of the authenticator, base64url-encoded. A hint about the model.

label.description: The display name the user gives it, `MacBook Touch ID` for instance.

backup_eligible.description: Whether the credential can be synchronized across devices (the WebAuthn BE flag).

backup_state.description: Whether the credential is currently backed up (the WebAuthn BS flag).

Contract.WebAuthnCredential.description:
One WebAuthn or passkey credential a user has enrolled. A user may hold several, so it is a
separate set from MfaFactor, uniquely identified by `credential_id`. `public_key` is the COSE public key and
`sign_count` the signature counter used to detect a clone. It is a possession factor bound to an origin and an RP, and
is used for phishing-resistant MFA and step-up. The ceremony resolves the RP ID and origin from the deployment
configuration and uses `user_verification=preferred`, `attestation=none` (enterprise attestation is not strictly
enforced), `resident_key=discouraged` (passwordless is out of scope), a 32-byte challenge, and a 120-second timeout
(WebAuthn Level 3 sections 5, 7, and 13).

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

Contract.WebAuthnCredentialRegistered.description:
A user enrolled a WebAuthn or passkey credential through self-service. Neither the public key nor
the `credential_id` reaches the audit trail -- only the kind does. The first one sets `User.mfa_enrolled` to true.

Contract.WebAuthnCredentialRemoveRequest.description: The input of RemoveWebAuthnCredential: it names the credential to remove by its `credential_id`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the target user belongs to.

Contract.WebAuthnCredentialRemoved.description:
A user removed a WebAuthn or passkey credential through self-service, having stepped up.
When no second factor is left, `User.mfa_enrolled` returns to false.

Contract.WebAuthnCredentialSummary.description:
The projection of one WebAuthn credential shown on the self-service security screen.
Neither the public key nor `sign_count` is returned: only what identification and display need.

Contract.WebAuthnRegistrationOptions.description:
What StartWebAuthnRegistration returns: the PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions to hand to
`navigator.credentials.create`, as JSON and unchanged. The challenge is short-lived and bound to the
server-side session.

attestation.description: The PublicKeyCredential holding an attestation response (WebAuthn Level 3).

Contract.WebAuthnRegistrationRequest.description:
The input of FinishWebAuthnRegistration: the attestation `navigator.credentials.create` returned,
sent back as JSON, optionally with a display label.

Contract.WebAuthnTransport.description: Hints about how a WebAuthn authenticator connects (WebAuthn Level 3 section 5.8.4, AuthenticatorTransport).

group_id.description: Required when `kind` is `add_group_member` or `remove_group_member`. Naming a dynamic group is a validation error at save time.

visibility.description: Optional when `kind` is `assign_application`; `visible` when left out. Published-language stub for a definition the Application context owns.

reason.description: An optional reason recorded when `kind` is `enable_user` or `disable_user`.

template_key.description: Required when `kind` is `send_email`. A label the workflow author gives the notification. The wording is resolved from LifecycleWorkflowNotification in the Tenancy notification template catalogue, and this value is passed into the body as a substitution variable. Assigning a different template per workflow is outside this context.

Contract.WorkflowActionDef.description:
One action definition a LifecycleWorkflowRevision fixes. Which fields it uses depends on the kind, and the existence of
what it refers to is checked both on create/update and on enable.

Contract.WorkflowActionKind.description: The kinds of WorkflowAction. Every one of them states a desired state, so each is idempotent and becomes a no_op when the state already holds.

field.description: A `TenantUserAttributeSchema.key`, or a built-in attribute key of User.

value.description: Any JSON value, because the type follows the AttributeType of `field`: a string, a number, a boolean, a date string, or an array of strings. The `in` operator takes an array of that type, and `exists` takes no value at all. One TypeSpec type cannot express that dependence, so the contract records the value as unconstrained and the server checks it against the tenant attribute schema.

Contract.WorkflowFilter.description:
One term of `WorkflowTrigger.filters`. Only a field that exists in the TenantUserAttributeSchema and whose type matches can be
stored; a free-text regex over PII and an unknown field are both refused at save time. Several filters are ANDed.

Contract.WorkflowFilterOperator.description: The comparison operators a WorkflowFilter may use. `eq` and `not_eq` are exact match and mismatch, `in` matches any member of a value set, and `exists` tests whether a value is present at all.

type.description: Problem type URI. IdMagic problem types are `urn:idmagic:error:<code>`, where `<code>` is the stable error code the server reports. The URI is not dereferenceable; clients switch on the URN suffix rather than fetching it.

title.description: Short human-readable summary derived from the error code: `invalid_role` becomes `Invalid role`. Stable for a given `type`.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body (RFC 9457 section 3.1).

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Always English and never localized; a UI that localizes maps the `type` URN suffix to its own message instead.

instance.description: Request correlation id, the same value the response carries in the `X-Request-ID` header. Absent when the request had no correlation id.

Contract.WorkflowRevisionConflictError.description: UpdateLifecycleWorkflow found that `expected_revision` does not match the current `LifecycleWorkflow.current_revision`, and rejected the lost update. The caller re-reads the latest revision and retries. RFC 9457 Problem Details with `type` = `urn:idmagic:error:workflow_revision_conflict`.

actions.description: The action list, expanded from the revision and fixed here. A later change to the definition does not change what this run means.

job_id.description: The `Jobs.JobRef.id` the dispatcher attaches after enqueueing. Unset until then.

Contract.WorkflowRun.description:
The unit of work produced by one firing of a WorkflowTrigger. The workflow_id, the revision, the trigger snapshot, the
target_user_id, and the expanded action list are all fixed at creation, so changing the definition afterwards does not
change what an existing run means. The dispatcher attaches `job_id` after enqueueing. Immediately before an action runs,
the target user and resource are re-checked inside the tenant, and runs against the same target_user_id are serialized in
`triggered_at` order.
`(tenant_id, workflow_id, revision, source_occurrence_id, target_user_id)` is the uniqueness constraint.

Contract.WorkflowRunListResponse.description: The run list response for a workflow.

Contract.WorkflowRunResponse.description:
The run detail response. It shows the trigger, the fixed revision, the target user, the Job attempts, and the outcome,
error code, and timestamps of each step. It carries no secret, email body, or attribute value.

Contract.WorkflowRunStatus.description: The states of WorkflowRunLifecycle. A no-op counts as a success.

source_occurrence_id.description: The id of the User mutation domain event that fired it. Redelivery of the same occurrence converges on the same run, so it is deduplicated.

changed_fields.description: When `kind` is `user_attributes_changed`, the names of the fields that actually changed. The values are not included.

Contract.WorkflowRunTriggerSnapshot.description:
The summary of a trigger firing, fixed when the WorkflowRun is created. The history keeps only the names of the changed
fields and whether each predicate held; the attribute values themselves are not kept, to protect PII.

error_code.description: A sanitized error code. It carries no attribute value and no email body.

Contract.WorkflowStep.description:
The execution record of one action inside a WorkflowRun. It holds the index in definition order and checkpoints the
outcome and a sanitized error code. It keeps no attribute value, email body, or secret.

Contract.WorkflowStepOutcome.description: The outcome of one WorkflowStep. `pending` is the initial value, before anything has been attempted.

Contract.WorkflowStepResponse.description: How a step is represented inside a run detail. It carries no secret, email body, or attribute value.

watched_attributes.description:
Required when `kind` is `user_attributes_changed`. It fires only when one of the listed fields actually changed; a field
merely present in the request with an unchanged value does not fire it.

from_status.description: Required when `kind` is `user_status_changed`: the `from` of a permitted UserLifecycle transition.

to_status.description: Required when `kind` is `user_status_changed`: the `to` of a permitted UserLifecycle transition.

Contract.WorkflowTriggerDef.description:
The trigger definition a LifecycleWorkflowRevision fixes. Depending on the kind it uses `watched_attributes`
or `from_status` and `to_status`. `filters` holds 0 to 20 terms, ANDed.

Contract.WorkflowTriggerKind.description: The kinds of condition a WorkflowTrigger fires on. The first version has only the three that start from a User mutation; date, cron, and wait steps are out of scope.

subject_token.description: The external attestation token as a raw string, a JWT-SVID for instance.

requested_audience.description: The `resource` parameter of the token exchange (RFC 8707). It is kept in the audit event.

Contract.WorkloadAttestation.description: The raw external attestation token and its verification context, handed over by the OAuth 2.0 token-exchange grant. The input of VerifyWorkloadAttestation.

reason.description: One of unregistered_issuer, trust_bundle_disabled, jwks_unavailable, invalid_signature, expired, audience_mismatch, ttl_exceeded, no_binding_match, ambiguous_match, agent_not_active, or agent_unbound.

trustBundleId.description: Set only when the issuer was registered.

Contract.WorkloadAttestationRejected.description: Verification of an external attestation token was refused fail-closed.

Contract.WorkloadAttestationRejectedErro.description: Verification of an external attestation token failed fail-closed: an unregistered issuer, a bad signature, an expired token, an audience mismatch, a TTL over the ceiling, a pattern mismatch, an ambiguous match, or a bound Agent that is not active. A domain condition; over HTTP it reaches the client as the token exchange InvalidGrantError.

client_id.description: The `client_id` of the AgentCredentialBinding the bound Agent holds. It becomes the `sub` of the issued token.

Contract.WorkloadIdentityGrant.description: The IdMagic principal an external attestation was projected onto once it passed verification. The OAuth 2.0 token-exchange use case treats it as the subject and resolves the bound OAuth2Client that `client_id` names through its own repository, to get the downscoping ceiling on scopes and grant types; WorkloadIdentity itself knows nothing about OAuth2Client.

Contract.WorkloadTokenExchanged.description: An external attestation passed verification and an IdMagic token was issued as the credential of the bound Agent.

tenant_id.description: The tenant it belongs to. Cross-tenant references are forbidden.

name.description: The administrative display name, unique within the tenant.

trust_domain.description: The SPIFFE trust domain, or a label the operator gives an issuer group.

issuer.description: The issuer URL the `iss` claim of the external attestation token must match. Unique within the tenant.

jwks_uri.description: Where the JWKS is fetched from. It must be https.

jwks.description: An inline JWKS, as an alternative to `jwks_uri`.

accepted_audiences.description: The accepted audiences; the `aud` claim of the external attestation token must match at least one of them.

max_subject_token_ttl_seconds.description: The ceiling on the external attestation token's own `exp - iat`. Exceeding it is refused fail-closed.

jwks_cached_at.description: When the JWKS was last fetched successfully. Used to judge how fresh the last-known-good cache is.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundle.description: A tenant-scoped trust setting for an external attestation issuer. `issuer` is unique within the tenant, and at least one of `jwks_uri` and inline `jwks` is required.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundleDeleted.description: An administrator deleted a WorkloadTrustBundle. The AgentWorkloadBindings under it were deleted with it.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundleDisabled.description: An administrator disabled a WorkloadTrustBundle. No binding under it can be used for an exchange afterwards.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundleListResponse.description: The WorkloadTrustBundle list of the administration API.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundleRefreshRespo.description: The response of RefreshWorkloadTrustBundleJWKS: whether the JWKS could actually be fetched. It is a test operation, so that a tenant finds a misconfiguration before it matters.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundleRegisterRequ.description: The JSON request an administrator sends to register a WorkloadTrustBundle.

has_inline_jwks.description: Whether an inline `jwks` is set. The `jwks` itself is not returned.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundleResponse.description: How a WorkloadTrustBundle is represented. The list and the detail endpoints of the administration API return the same representation. It carries no secret from `jwks`, only public key material.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundleUpdateReques.description: The JSON request an administrator sends to update the `name`, `jwks_uri`, `jwks`, `accepted_audiences`, or `max_subject_token_ttl_seconds` of a WorkloadTrustBundle. A field left out keeps its current value. `issuer` and `trust_domain` are immutable; changing them means registering again.

Contract.WorkloadTrustBundleUpdated.description: An administrator updated the metadata of a WorkloadTrustBundle.

wtrealm.description: The identifier of the RP: the WS-Fed wtrealm, which is also the SAML audience. WS-Federation says only that it is a URI, so the ceiling follows the URI class. A separate ceiling of 2048 bytes applies as the resource limit that keeps the value inside a btree index row.

application_id.description: The Application it corresponds to. Ordinary CRUD leaves it alone; only the bulk creation and deletion of an Application manage the relationship.

display_name.description: The display name in the administration UI.

reply_urls.description: The closed set of permitted `wreply` targets. Only an exact match against this set is accepted.

audience.description: The audience of an issued assertion. Empty means the wtrealm is used.

token_type.description: The SAML version of an issued assertion. Empty means SAML 1.1, the default Entra's WS-Fed expects.

claim_policy.description: The claim issuance policy for this RP.

entra_profile.description: The Microsoft Entra domain federation preset. It bundles the required claims and the sourceAnchor transform used when the federation is configured.

Contract.WsFedRelyingParty.description: The registration of a relying party (RP) for WS-Federation passive. It is identified by its wtrealm and bundles the closed set of permitted `wreply` targets, the audience, and the claim issuance policy. An RP outside the catalogue, whose `application_id` is null, is allowed; when it is not null it names a `wsfed` Application of the same tenant, and at most one RP is bound to one Application.

wtrealm.description: The identifier of the RP: the WS-Fed wtrealm, which is also the SAML audience.

display_name.description: The display name in the administration UI.

reply_urls.description: The closed set of permitted `wreply` targets. Only an exact match against this set is accepted.

audience.description: The audience of an issued assertion. Empty means the wtrealm is used.

claim_policy.description: The claim issuance policy for this RP.

Contract.WsFedRelyingPartyRequest.description: The JSON request registering or updating a WS-Federation relying party. It carries only what the caller may set; `application_id`, the tenant, and the timestamps stay with the server.

tenantId.description: The tenant that issued it.

wtrealm.description: The wtrealm of the RP it was issued to.

userId.description: The subject, the user the NameID resolved to.

Contract.WsFedSignInIssued.description: A signed assertion was issued to an RP through WS-Federation passive sign-in.

tenantId.description: The tenant that refused it.

wtrealm.description: The wtrealm that was asked for, when it could be determined.

reason.description: A summary of why it was refused.

Contract.WsFedSignInRejected.description: A WS-Federation passive sign-in was refused: an unregistered wtrealm, a `wreply` outside the permitted set, a failed check, and the like.

tenantId.description: The tenant that signed out.

wtrealm.description: The wtrealm of the RP that asked for the sign-out, when it could be determined.

Contract.WsFedSignOut.description: A WS-Federation sign-out destroyed the local session.

Contract.WsFedTokenType.description: The SAML version of the assertion WS-Federation issues, which also becomes the TokenType of the RSTR. SAML 1.1 (urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.0:assertion) is what Entra and AD FS default to for WS-Fed.

message_id.description: The WS-Addressing MessageID, used to prevent replay.

to.description: WS-Addressing `To`: the STS endpoint the request was addressed to.

username.description: The username of the WS-Security UsernameToken.

password.description: The password credential of the WS-Security UsernameToken.

applies_to.description: The RP, that is, the audience. It resolves to a registered WsFedRelyingParty.

token_type.description: The token type requested. Empty means the RP's default.

request_type.description: The WS-Trust RequestType. Only absent or Issue is accepted.

key_type.description: The WS-Trust KeyType. Only absent or Bearer is accepted.

Contract.WsTrustRequestSecurityToken.description: The intermediate form holding what has to be checked, extracted from the RST of the WS-Trust 1.3 Issue binding.

relates_to.description: The MessageID of the originating RST.

Contract.WsTrustResponse.description: The RSTR for a WS-Trust Issue. It carries the signed SAML assertion together with the lifetime and appliesTo.

tenantId.description: The tenant that issued it.

appliesTo.description: The RP, that is, the audience, it was issued to.

Contract.WsTrustTokenIssued.description: A signed assertion was issued through the WS-Trust active STS.

tenantId.description: The tenant that refused it.

appliesTo.description: The AppliesTo that was asked for, when it could be determined.

reason.description: A summary of why it was refused.

Contract.WsTrustTokenRejected.description: An Issue request to the WS-Trust active STS was refused.

force.description: Same meaning as `?purge=true`: skip the soft delete and anonymize immediately. Omitted means a soft delete.

observability.description: The observability backend the process started with.

authzen.description: The AuthZEN backend the process started with.
